We believe that the generative foam we describe, and in particular the boundaries between cells, could play an important role in determining where the errors of trained diffusion models redistribute the mass of the generated samples when the data are long-range correlated.

papers.title: Specification-Aware Predictive Uncertainty Decomposition
papers.abstract: Classical decompositions of predictive uncertainty, such as the information-theoretic one, are defined for a fixed representation $x$ of the input object. They do not consider that $x$ may be incomplete, nor do they measure how much the missing information can affect the prediction. In Large Language Models, users can clarify an underspecified input without any retraining. The clarified input can describe the user's unobserved intent $z^*$ more accurately and change the predictive uncertainty about the outcome. In this paper, we formalize this setting probabilistically and derive a three-term decomposition of prediction risk into specification, residual aleatoric, and epistemic uncertainties. We show that at the original information level, when only $x$ is available, the aleatoric uncertainty, represented by a Bayes risk, has two components. The first, which we call specification uncertainty, is the expected reduction in this Bayes risk from revealing the intent. The second is the residual aleatoric uncertainty, i.e., the Bayes risk that remains once the intent is known, averaged over its possible values $z$ given $x$. The distinction is important, as specification uncertainty informs the decision to request clarification before making a prediction. We build approximations of these components and connect them to existing uncertainty measures. Our experiments across different domains and modalities show distinct roles for the three components. Specification uncertainty is the most informative for detecting underspecified inputs, while residual aleatoric uncertainty is the most informative for detecting in-distribution prediction errors.

papers.title: Cyber-JEV: Matched Contrastive Fine-Tuning of Language Models for Fast Source-Code Vulnerability Triage
papers.abstract: Single-pass scoring models such as Jev give each code function a vulnerability probability, so that security teams can rank many functions for review without generating written explanations. Training an open-weight model for this task is limited by data. Benchmarks with both vulnerable and non-vulnerable labels keep few vulnerable functions once examples related to the test data are removed, while larger public vulnerability records mostly contain vulnerable functions only. Mixing the two lets the data source predict the label, and training on the labeled data alone leaves a model that often scores a fixed function above its vulnerable original. We present Cyber-JEV, a fine-tuning method that uses fix commits to turn these records into comparison groups. Each group holds a vulnerable function, its patched version and up to two unchanged functions from the same file, so the model sees the change that removed a recorded defect. One shared model learns two tasks: classifying functions from the labeled reference data, and ranking the vulnerable function above the other members of its group. At test time the input is one function and the output is a vulnerability score. On a test benchmark of 7,270 functions, an ensemble of five fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B models reaches an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.814, compared with 0.743 for Jev 1.13. With the 4,031 alerts of Jev as the review budget, it misses 16 of 322 vulnerable functions instead of 39. Compared with training on the reference data alone, it ranks the vulnerable version above the patched version 14.8 to 29.2 percentage points more often on three sets of real fixes. Such scores can order the changed functions of a pull request or a release for review under a fixed budget.

papers.title: Light nucleus and hypernucleus production at RHIC and LHC energies: a comparative study of phenomenological models
papers.abstract: This document summarizes the work of the EMMI Rapid Reaction Task Force on ``Understanding light (anti)nuclei production at RHIC and LHC'', which took place at GSI on 8--12 April 2024. The meeting brought together experimentalists and theorists to discuss the current understanding of light-nuclei and hypernuclei production in high-energy hadronic collisions, with particular emphasis on statistical hadronization, coalescence, kinetic, and transport approaches. The discussions addressed the experimental status and the ability of different theoretical descriptions to reproduce the available measurements, as well as the connections between nuclear production, femtoscopic correlations, source sizes, nuclear wave functions, and the formation dynamics of loosely bound states. This document reviews the main experimental and theoretical developments presented during the RRTF, summarizes the key questions that emerged from the discussions, and identifies observables and future measurements that may help discriminate among different production mechanisms.

papers.title: Labor Market Returns to Education and Intra-family Educational Inequality: Theory and Experimental Evidence
papers.abstract: How do labor market conditions shape educational inequality within- and between families? A growing body of evidence documents convex wage returns to education in labor markets across the world. We develop a theoretical model that demonstrates that earnings convexity can increase or decrease between-sibling differences in investments and outcomes depending on the parameter of parental inequality aversion. We recover the distribution of this structural parameter from a highly-incentivized lab-in-the-field experiment with 246 parents in San Luis Potosí, Mexico, in which token allocations determine children's access to an AI course. Parents make allocation decisions across six scenarios that vary convexity in the payoff function and endowment-investment substitutability. We identify three types of parents: Rawlsian parents display perfect inequality aversion (12.6%), interior parents that are moderately inequality tolerant (76.8%), and Utilitarian parents who maximize total payoffs (10.6%). While these three groups respond to earnings convexity in heterogeneous ways, on average, greater convexity increases the share allocated to the high-endowed child, thereby widening within-family inequality.

papers.title: Leverage Dynamics in Product-Market Networks
papers.abstract: We examine whether corporate leverage persistence reflects only firms' own adjustment frictions or also the past financing choices of economically connected firms. We combine annual firm fundamentals with time-varying text-based product-market networks and estimate a heterogeneous dynamic partial-adjustment model with interactive effects using defactored instrumental variables. The estimator accommodates time- varying network weights and spatial dependence in firm-specific coefficients. Network-weighted lagged leverage is positive and statistically significant, with a mean coefficient representing approximately 45% of the sum of the own and network lag coefficients for book leverage. Accounting for network dependence reduces the persistence attributed to firms' own financing histories and increases the implied own-firm speed of adjustment. Firm-specific estimates reveal significant product-market clustering in own-leverage persistence and in responses to several leverage determinants, showing that heterogeneity in financing behaviour is systematically related to product-market proximity. The evolution of product-market connections matters quantitatively for network dependence: holding the network fixed produces a substantially larger network coefficient and considerably larger indirect effects than using annual network weights. Network dependence is therefore an economically important component of leverage dynamics, while its measurement depends on both the specification of economic connections and heterogeneity in firm behaviour.

papers.title: Anion Engineering Enables Concurrent Optimization of Phonon and Carrier Transport in AMg$_2$X$_2$ Zintl Thermoelectrics
papers.abstract: The simultaneous suppression of lattice heat transport and enhancement of carrier transport is central to the development of high-performance thermoelectric materials. Here, we investigate the microscopic mechanisms governing phonon and carrier transport in CaAl$_2$Si$_2$-type AMg$_2$X$_2$ (A = Ca, Sr, Ba; X = P, As, Sb, Bi) Zintl compounds using first-principles calculations, machine-learning interatomic potentials, and Boltzmann transport theory. As X changes from P to Bi, the widening phonon band gap restricts three-phonon scattering channels and increases the relative importance of four-phonon processes. In CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ and BaMg$_2$Bi$_2$, four-phonon scattering dominates the relaxation of low-frequency heat-carrying modes at 900 K. The Bi-based series also exhibits an anomalous increase in lattice thermal conductivity from Ca to Ba despite the increasing cation mass. Mode-resolved analysis links the lower thermal conductivity of CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ to reduced low-frequency group velocities and stronger anharmonic scattering, with Ca-related mid-frequency vibrations providing additional four-phonon scattering channels. Including both particle-like and coherent contributions, its lattice thermal conductivity reaches 0.23 W$\cdot$m$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$ at 900 K. Meanwhile, the increasing covalent character of the vertical Mg-X bonds is accompanied by enhanced band-edge dispersion and reduced carrier effective masses. These electronic changes, together with conduction-band convergence, favor n-type transport and yield a predicted peak $ZT$ of 3.68 at 900 K in CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$. These results elucidate the interplay of phonon spectral structure and higher-order anharmonicity in thermal transport, alongside the distinct electronic response to anion substitution.

papers.title: Evidence of flare and coronal mass ejection-driven shock acceleration of relativistic protons on 21 November 2024
papers.abstract: On 21 November 2024 at 17:55 UTC, a solar flare erupted from far-side active region (AR) 13892, with enhanced hard X-ray flux measured by Solar Orbiter (SO). It was associated with a coronal mass ejection (CME) travelling at 1436 km/s along the limb. This event produced a strong and widespread solar energetic particle (SEP) event at Earth, STEREO-A and SO, with proton energies exceeding 100 MeV. We investigate the relativistic particle acceleration during this event, focusing on separating flare- and shock-related contributions and linking spectral evolution to the CME-driven shock properties. We combine multi-spacecraft energetic-particle observations with velocity dispersion analysis (VDA), three-dimensional CME-driven shock reconstruction, and magnetic connectivity modelling. Radio observations and SEP composition provided independent diagnostics of shock- and flare-associated particle acceleration, respectively. VDA yields solar release times (SRTs) consistent with an early flare-accelerated particle population at all three observers, despite their broad range of helio-longitudes. At STEREO-A, the early release is followed immediately by magnetic connection to an efficient CME-driven shock. A 3D reconstruction of the type II radio burst location confirms a connection between Earth and an efficient shock-acceleration region several minutes later. Within the adopted models, the SO release precedes magnetic connection to the reconstructed front, disfavouring acceleration at the connected shock as the source of the earliest particles. Despite this diversity, STEREO-A and SO show similar spectral evolution, while the near-Earth spectrum extends to relativistic energies and exhibits a high-energy rollover. SEP abundances also show signatures of flare-related acceleration at all three observers. The analysis suggests multiple acceleration processes acting non-uniformly across observers.

papers.title: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
papers.abstract: We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits. Adding a sparse factor to the gadget at the middle vertices of a single type then enforces full rank, with a controlled loss in expansion. To obtain the 2-group action, we observe that reducing the generators of the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2, instead of modulo an odd prime, gives Ramanujan Cayley graphs on finite 2-groups. This construction may be of independent interest. Plugging two such expanders into the balanced product of Lin and Hsieh gives the quantum codes, since full rank of the input graphs is inherited by the check matrices. Our construction supplies the code family sought by Hong, Guo, and Lucas. Applying their analysis, within their framework and under their dynamical assumptions, gives quantum memories whose free-energy density is analytic at every positive temperature and whose guaranteed lifetime is $exp(Ω(N))$ at sufficiently low fixed positive temperature, where N is the blocklength. This improves the previously guaranteed stretched-exponential timescale.

papers.title: One Image Is Enough: Self-Generated Supervision for Personalizing Human Video Diffusion at Test Time
papers.abstract: Pose-driven human video diffusion animates a person from a single reference image and a target pose sequence, yet it struggles to preserve identity, rendering the face and garments unfaithfully as the pose departs from it. Personalization is the standard remedy, but its supervision is missing: one image fixes identity at a single pose, while a multi-pose subject video cannot be assumed in practice. Instead, we synthesize the missing supervision. A domain-tuned, pose-conditioned generator produces pseudo-ground-truth frames at selected key poses. An inference-time reference-only sampler steers these candidates toward the subject and keeps the most identity-consistent. A per-subject low-rank adapter then trains on static clips of them, configured from the reference alone, with no subject video, ground truth, or labels. Although lower in fidelity, these synthetic frames supervise more effectively than real ones. Real frames as captured carry motion that erodes the temporal prior, while a static clip conveys appearance alone. On TikTok and UBC Fashion, the adapted model improves the base on every metric, inverts the identity-versus-motion trade-off, and matches or surpasses adaptation on five real frames despite using none. Code and weights are available at https://github.com/SadmanPinon/one-image-is-enough.

papers.title: J-PAS: Exploring the connection between local environment and the triggering of bursty star formation in Extreme Emission Line Galaxies
papers.abstract: [Abridged]Extreme Emission Line Galaxies (EELGs) are compact, low-mass systems undergoing intense bursts of star formation, whose physical conditions resemble those of galaxies in the early Universe. We characterise the local environment of EELGs identified in the J-PAS survey to determine whether their extreme properties are associated with the presence of nearby companions, as expected if galaxy-galaxy interactions were the main trigger of the burst. We analyse 917 EELGs from the J-PAS internal data release at $0.03 \lesssim z \lesssim 0.9$ over $\sim$30 deg$^2$. We use the Pair Probability Function formalism, based on the full photometric redshift probability distributions, to identify companions within projected separations up to 200 kpc and velocity differences up to 500 km s$^{-1}$. Stellar masses, star formation rates, dust attenuation, and metallicity estimates were derived for the EELGs and their companions through SED fitting with CIGALE, and Monte Carlo simulations were used to correct for projection and completeness effects. The average pair fraction of the EELGs is $f_\mathrm{pair} = 0.162^{+0.048}_{-0.033}$, indicating that only $\sim$16% of the sample has detectable companions, a value lower than the observed average for other star-forming galaxies within the adopted limits. When detected within the sensitivity and stellar-mass completeness limits of J-PAS, companions tend to be more massive and to show higher SED-based metallicity estimates than the EELGs, suggesting that the latter are typically the low-mass components of asymmetric pairs. However, lower-mass companions below these limits may remain undetected. No statistically significant correlation is found between the equivalent widths of the [OIII]$λ$5007, H$β$, and H$α$ emission lines and the projected separation to the detected companions within the J-PAS limits.

papers.title: SHq: Learnable Grids for LLM Weight Quantization
papers.abstract: Block-scaled lookup-table (LUT) formats, which represent weights as indices into a small value set (the grid), have become standard for low-bit LLM quantization, ranging from NF4 and BOF4 to the 3-bit LUT instruction in NVIDIA Rubin. While these formats leave the grid definition flexible, existing implementations rely on fixed grids derived either from numerical data types (INT, FP) or assumed weight distributions (NF, BOF). We demonstrate that no single fixed grid is universally optimal; the best fixed grid varies with bit-width: BOFS at 2 bits, NF at 4 and 5 bits, and INT at 6 bits. We introduce SHq, a closed-form family of grids parameterized by two critical degrees of freedom: a companding strength α that interpolates level spacing from uniform to floating-point-like, and an offset c that introduces asymmetry. This offset allows the sign bit of the FP8 block scale, otherwise unused, to select between the grid and its mirror image, up to doubling the number of distinct values available per block. SHq modifies only the lookup table contents and serves as a drop-in replacement for the grid in any such format. Across five models ranging from 3B to 35B parameters, including a mixture-of-experts architecture, evaluated at 2-6 bits using RTN and GPTQ, SHq achieves the lowest KL divergence in every setting at 3 and 4 bits and in most settings at 2, 5 and 6 bits. It outperforms the best fixed grid by up to 34% and remains superior under mixed-precision configurations. At 4.5 bits per weight, the SHq format reduces the KL divergence of NVFP4 by 41-67% while improving downstream accuracy. Grid families incorporating both spacing and offset parameters perform comparably, whereas those lacking an offset exhibit clearly higher error, confirming that these two degrees of freedom drive the observed gains. We therefore propose SHq as the standard grid for block-scaled lookup-table formats.

papers.title: Operator Fejér--Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial with bounded-operator coefficients that is positive semidefinite on $K$ belongs to the operator quadratic module generated by $S$. We also show that if such a polynomial has degree at most $\tt{d}$, then it admits a certificate of weighted degree at most $\tt{d}+c_S$, where $c_S$ depends only on $S$, not on the polynomial or the coefficient Hilbert space. In contrast to the scalar case, where natural preorderings admit the degree bound $\tt{d}$ independently of $K$, we show that no uniform additive constant exists for natural matrix preorderings. We construct quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials positive semidefinite on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees in the corresponding natural preorderings diverge as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap length remains bounded below. Conversely, we establish uniform bounds of the form $\tt{d}+C$ for families of interval unions contained in a fixed compact interval when interval lengths and gap lengths have uniform positive lower bounds. Our proofs develop two techniques that may be of independent interest. First, a quadratic reduction principle represents arbitrary-degree operator polynomials as compressions of quadratic ones on enlarged Hilbert spaces. A perturbation argument and the closedness of truncated operator quadratic modules then extend uniform degree bounds from the quadratic case to arbitrary degrees with linear degree bounds of slope $1$. Second, a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil transfers positivity on interval unions to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fejér--Riesz theorem yields certificates.

papers.title: ReContact: Reconstruct and Retarget Human Contacts from Video for Contact-Rich Humanoid Manipulation
papers.abstract: Contact transitions allow humanoid robots to redistribute object support across the whole body, enabling manipulation beyond hand-only grasps. Human videos provide a scalable source of such transitions for robots to learn from. However, body occlusion disrupts object pose tracking and corrupts retargeted motion. Moreover, accurately reproducing the object trajectory does not ensure that the robot applies stabilizing forces at the intended contacts, risking slips or drops in later phases. To address these challenges, we propose ReContact, which reconstructs and retargets human-object interactions through an object-centric contact plan. The plan specifies contact phases, contact pairs, anchors, pressing directions, and sticking or sliding modes. Contact priors stabilize object pose reconstruction through occlusion. A residual policy over a frozen whole-body tracker is rewarded for making contact at planned anchors with forces aligned to the specified directions. In simulation, on a thigh-supported regrasp task, ReContact achieves the planned two-palm bottom hold in 83.5 of episodes over three training seeds, versus 0.16% for the best adapted baseline. One policy trained on 247 references re-solved for new placements raises in-workspace tube-transfer success from 20.4% (source reference only) to 97.8%. On a real Unitree G1, policies execute seven contact-rich manipulation and two loco-manipulation tasks.

papers.title: Revisiting (Bijective) Burrows-Wheeler Transform Space-Time Trade-Off Constructions
papers.abstract: The bijective Burrows-Wheeler transform (BBWT) replaces the delimiter of the ordinary BWT by a Lyndon factorization and sorts factor conjugates in $ω$-order. It admits quadratic-time constant-workspace algorithms and linear-time linear-space algorithms. We extend the small-space BWT trade-off of Crochemore et al. [JDA,'15] to the BBWT and accelerate both constructions. For $τ\in [3..n]$, let $σ_τ\le\min(σ,τ+1)$ be the maximum construction-batch alphabet size. We construct either transform in $ O\!\left( \frac{n^2}τ \frac{\logτ}{\log\logτ} \right) $ time and $O(τσ_τ)$ additional space, assuming $τσ_τ=O(n)$. This improves the transferred $O((n^2/τ)\logτ)$ bound by a $\log\logτ$ factor. If $σ_τ\in w^{O(1)}$, where $w\inΩ(\log n)$ is the word size, the time improves to $ O\!\left( \frac{n^2}τ + \frac{n\logτ}{\log\logτ} \right). $ For inversion, the same bounds hold with the global alphabet size $σ$ in place of $σ_τ$.

papers.title: On blow-up for the cut-off Boltzmann equation with very hard potentials
papers.abstract: We construct smooth, strictly positive solutions of the three-dimensional cut-off Boltzmann equation with very hard potentials whose densities become unbounded in finite time. A main ingredient is a new velocity weight that is Gaussian on a ball and has a polynomial tail of fixed order. We establish coercive estimates for the linearized collision operator and bilinear estimates for the collision term, with constants independent of the radius of the Gaussian region. Combining these weighted estimates with an imploding solution of the compressible Euler equations, we develop an energy framework that controls the Boltzmann solution up to the blow-up time. The initial data agree with a constant Maxwellian outside a bounded spatial region and have finite relative entropy.

papers.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic with Program Costs
papers.abstract: We introduce $\mathbb{N}\mathtt{PDL}$, a resource-aware variant of Propositional Dynamic Logic ($\mathtt{PDL}$) capable of accounting for program costs measured by natural numbers (such as time or space in the sense of computability theory). In this framework, programs correspond to transition systems weighted by extended natural numbers, and the syntax of our logic includes formulas expressing which properties are reachable by program executions within specific cost constraints. First, we explain how the standard program constructs of non-deterministic choice, sequential composition, iteration, and tests are interpreted in this weighted setting and establish the validity of their corresponding reduction axioms. Using an appropriate adaptation of the (Fischer-Ladner) filtration technique, we proceed to prove decidability and completeness for $\mathbb{N}\mathtt{PDL}$ as our main results. We furthermore provide upper and lower complexity bounds for this logic using translations between standard $\mathtt{PDL}$ and $\mathbb{N}\mathtt{PDL}$.

papers.title: Towards Optimal Routing Strategies for qLDPC codes on Silicon Spin Qubits
papers.abstract: One of the major challenges of implementing high-rate quantum error correction codes, like qLDPC codes, is realizing the required long-range interactions. Spin qubit platforms can provide this connectivity by shuttling qubits next to each other whenever they need to interact. When doing this, the performance of the code depends on the shuttling strategy. We study memory experiments of the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle (Gross) code on two shuttling grids for future spin qubit devices: a square grid and a square grid with diagonals. We compare three shuttling strategies, structured and random initial layouts, and a range of shuttling noise models spanning best- and worst-case scenarios. The best strategy minimizes the longest distance travelled rather than the total distance. The initial layout has only a weak effect, whereas adding diagonals to the grid reduces the logical error rate by up to two orders of magnitude which may have implications for future hardware design.

papers.title: Inducing cooperative dynamics in an inhomogeneous many-emitter ensemble with a pulse sequence
papers.abstract: Driving a many-particle quantum system with an appropriately tuned external field can give rise to features in its nonequilibrium dynamics that are absent in the equilibrium counterpart. Cooperative dynamics in a dense ensemble of quantum emitters manifested through superradiance, a burst in the emission intensity as a function of time, is typically suppressed by spectral disparities among emitters in the ensemble. We demonstrate the enhancement of cooperative dynamics in a spectrally inhomogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters when it is driven by a periodic pulse sequence. Using both a semi-analytical mean-field solution and a digital quantum simulation, we examine the coherence of the pulse-driven ensemble and the intensity of the emitted radiation as a function of the spectral disparity in the ensemble, as a function of time, the number of atoms in the system, and as a function of the inter-pulse delay. We identify clear signatures of the enhanced cooperative dynamics for the pulse-driven inhomogeneous ensemble when dephasing in the dynamics of the ensemble is suppressed by a sufficient number of pulses during the individual emitter lifetime. These results demonstrate a post-fabrication tuning knob based on externally applied control fields for the dynamics of the many-emitter ensemble.

papers.title: Memory Admission and Result-Retention Sizing in an RV32IMC FPGA Soft Processor
papers.abstract: In FPGA soft processors with shared backing block RAM, memory admission can stall a multiplication after its product has been prepared. We study how admission timing changes result retention in PaceRV, our board-tested five-stage RV32IMC core, using fixed binaries and matched dynamic instructions. Offering data requests one edge earlier reduces geometric-mean Embench cycles by 18.2% and retention opportunities from 375,063 to 4,373. Admission and retention cycle gains are conditional and non-additive. Under slower reads, a 99% capture target selects an 18-edge validity window with registered requests and 28 edges with early requests, although no multiplication matched within both measurement intervals waits longer. A predeclared sizing rule predicts opportunity recovery exactly in all finite tests, including kernels excluded from model development. Independent timing analysis closely estimates execution-cycle savings. The results support choosing admission first, then deciding whether to extend validity and sizing it against an explicit capture or missed-opportunity objective.

papers.title: Introducing Cluster Efficiency to LLM Serving: Pooling Economical Accelerators over Fast Interconnects
papers.abstract: Long-context large language model (LLM) serving places substantial demands on compute, memory capacity, and memory bandwidth. Economical accelerators can offer these resources at lower cost, but their limited per-device capacity requires pooling across devices, making communication overhead critical. We study cluster efficiency, measured in tokens per dollar and per joule, and show how low-latency, high-bandwidth interconnects enable economical accelerators to retain their cost advantage. Guided by a characterization of coding-agent workloads and accelerator scaling, we realize this design on the Tenstorrent Galaxy, a cluster of Blackhole chips. The serving stack combines integrated communication engines, pipelined ring transfers, communication-computation overlap, and device-side decode replay to reduce collective overhead. Across three dense models in BF16 and 8-bit configurations with 8K-256K-token contexts, the Galaxy achieves 1.07-2.24$\times$ the tokens per dollar of an eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell server under a three-year acquisition-and-electricity cost model. Emulating TCP-class communication on the same chips reduces throughput by 23.5-67.4% and eliminates the cost advantage in every evaluated configuration. These results demonstrate how fast interconnects translate the per-dollar resource advantages of economical accelerators into cost-efficient long-context LLM serving.

papers.title: Enhancing Grid Stability with Synchronverter-Based Control for Grid-Side Converters in Wind Power Systems
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new synchronverter control strategy for wind turbine grid-side converters, aimed at bolstering grid resilience by providing essential inertial frequency support without the need for additional energy storage components. The strategy harnesses the inherent energy storage capability of the DC-link capacitor to emulate the dynamic behavior of a synchronous generator, effectively contributing to grid inertia. A dual-controller architecture is implemented, consisting of a slow PI controller to maintain DC voltage stability and a fast protection mechanism to prevent overvoltage and undervoltage excursions. Critically, the control scheme facilitates controlled reductions of up to 10% in the DC-link voltage, generating a power reserve that can be strategically deployed for inertia emulation while preserving safe operating limits. The efficacy of the proposed method is validated through simulations of a representative three-turbine wind power plant, incorporating coordinated operation via virtual friction for inter-machine damping and local-global control strategies. Results showcase the superior performance of the proposed strategy compared to conventional grid-following control, emphasizing its potential to significantly improve grid stability and address the increasing challenges posed by high renewable energy penetration.

papers.title: Information Limits for Stable Reduction of Coupled Diffusion Systems
papers.abstract: Eliminating an unresolved diffusion field from a coupled parabolic system produces an operator-valued memory term and a contribution from the hidden initial state. We study whether a reduced prediction of the retained field meets a prescribed tolerance. For known hidden initial data, the discarded response, damped by diffusion and transmitted through the coupling, gives an upper error bound; an auxiliary diffusion problem supplies a lower bound. Rigorous discretisation bounds then yield tests that accept, reject or remain undecided. If the discarded initial state is known only through a norm bound, the minimum worst-case error equals that bound multiplied by the time-uniform gain from the missing state to the retained trajectory. Our main result encloses this infinite-dimensional gain using a finite spectral Galerkin evolution, its residual in the full equations and an explicit diffusion tail. The enclosure converges without compactness or smallness of the coupling. Strict comparisons of the optimal radius with a tolerance have finite certificates if all endpoint quantities admit arbitrarily accurate rigorous enclosures. Multiplication-coupling examples with infinitely many dynamically coupled modes illustrate both settings, including explicit finite-element error budgets.

papers.title: CAREFUL-Bench: Effect-Aware, Judge-Free Evaluation of Multi-Turn LLM Function Calling
papers.abstract: The multi-turn checker of the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) checks only the final state of a simulated service, never the calls that produced it. Extra calls cost nothing, no function doc says what a function does, and the scripted user never answers a proposal, so a model that asks before deleting or paying fails the turn; 322 of the 734 reference turns in the base category act destructively without confirmation. We add effect information to BFCL without replacing it. Effect declarations for all 128 functions are inferred by executing each function in BFCL's own simulators and diffing the state; the remaining judgment, which writes are destructive, is made by four annotators, two humans and two language models (Fleiss' kappa = 0.75), and adjudicated. A judge-free replay scorer re-scores any logged BFCL run, reproduces BFCL's results on all 800 reference trajectories, and reports, alongside the official score, unrequested destructive calls, duplicate writes, redundant reads, surplus steps and their token cost. A confirmation-aware protocol adds a deterministic user that answers proposals. On 11 open models the effect-aware score preserves the official ranking (rho = 0.99) but changes the gaps: the leader loses 14.0 points to unrequested destructive calls, and surplus steps account for 2-28% of all input tokens. Effect hints in the function docs produce no measurable change for any of eight models, consistent with their advisory status in the Model Context Protocol. A user that answers recovers up to four points for the models that ask and none for the rest, with every comparison paired on the same conversations. The gains come from clarifying questions rather than requests for permission: of the 712 conversations that require a destructive call, no model completes more than 6 with every such call confirmed, a difference the official score does not record.

papers.title: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library
papers.abstract: Quantum software ecosystems provide increasingly capable tools for simulation and hardware execution, but differences in programming models, supported features, and backend capabilities can make it difficult to move and systematically compare the same quantum algorithm across execution environments. We introduce eigenkit, a provider-neutral quantum computing library that separates algorithm definition from backend execution through a common circuit representation and provider interface. The library currently supports 12 execution providers spanning simulators and quantum hardware, provides backend-independent gradient computation, and integrates with standard scientific-computing and machine-learning workflows through NumPy, PyTorch, and scikit-learn interfaces. We evaluate the practical relevance of this abstraction across both simulation and quantum hardware. Simulator performance varies substantially with circuit size, structure, batching, and application workload, showing that no single backend is consistently preferable. On quantum hardware, experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald show that which processor is better suited to a given algorithm depends not only on hardware constraints, but also on how well the topology of the quantum algorithm matches the physical connectivity of the processor. These results demonstrate that backend portability is not only a software-design convenience, but can be important for both computational efficiency and quantum execution quality.

papers.title: Symmetry, uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive solutions of the Choquard equation
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions \(Q\in H^1(\mathbb R^N)\) of \[-ΔQ+Q=(I_α*Q^p)Q^{p-1},\] where \(I_α\) is the Riesz potential of order \(α\), \(N\ge1\), \(0<α<N\), \(p>1+α/N\), and \((N-2)p<N+α\). We prove that every such solution is radially symmetric and strictly decreasing about some point. For \(p\ge2\), we establish uniqueness up to translations and show that the real linearized operator has Morse index one and kernel spanned by \(\partial_1Q,\ldots,\partial_NQ\). The symmetry proof uses the method of moving planes. Uniqueness follows from nondegeneracy and compactness through a continuation argument.

papers.title: Utility-Aware Generative Recommendation: Utility-Enriched Semantic Codes and Utility-Guided Decoding
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation has been widely adopted in large-scale industrial recommendation systems, where multimodal item embeddings are quantized into offline semantic identifiers (SIDs) and items are retrieved by autoregressively generating their SIDs. However, conventional SID construction often underrepresents item utility reflected in post-exposure behaviors such as shares, long views, and video completion, making semantically similar items with different utility insufficiently distinguishable while struggling to accommodate rapidly changing utility signals. Moreover, generation likelihood may be misaligned with downstream utility, causing high-utility candidates to be prematurely pruned during beam search before post-generation reranking or training-time reward alignment can effectively compensate. To address these limitations, we propose UAGR, which aligns both SID construction and decoding with downstream multi-objective utility. Our Utility-Enriched Semantic Codes preserve the original semantic information while incorporating item-level utility without increasing SID length or vocabulary size, supporting incremental utility updates with no additional tokenization or sequence-decoding cost. Meanwhile, our Utility-Guided Decoding estimates candidate utility by combining predictions of multiple post-exposure outcomes and incorporates these estimates into beam scoring, reducing the risk of prematurely pruning high-utility paths while enabling flexible utility control without interfering with generative backbone training. Extensive offline experiments and online A/B tests under real-world traffic demonstrate the effectiveness and deployability of UAGR, which has been fully deployed on Kuaishou and increases video watch time by 0.206\% online.

papers.title: Maximum entropy reconstruction of discrete-time Markov chains under partial information
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the reconstruction of discrete-time Markov chains from incomplete information using the maximum entropy rate principle. Three settings are considered: prescribed graph topology alone, topology with a fully specified stationary distribution, and topology with partially specified stationary probabilities. We investigate the relationship between entropy-maximizing transition mechanisms and Luce's choice axiom, establishing conditions under which optimal transition matrices admit a Luce-score representation. When the stationary distribution is fully prescribed, we develop a constructive feasibility test and a system-theoretic iterative algorithm based on a Lyapunov-like function. Unlike conventional matrix-scaling approaches, the proposed algorithm operates directly on Luce scores. We illustrate the results for selected graph topologies, including complete graphs without self-loops and odd cycles. We also provide a counterexample to a previously stated uniqueness claim, showing that distinct, nonproportional Luce-score vectors can generate the same entropy-maximizing transition matrix. For partially prescribed stationary distributions, we extend the score-based approach to jointly reconstruct the unknown stationary probabilities and transition mechanism through an iterative procedure involving a parameterized Lyapunov-like function. Overall, the proposed framework integrates graph compatibility, entropy-rate maximization, and probabilistic choice representations, offering constructive tools for reconstructing Markov chains under different levels of stationary information and structural constraints.

papers.title: Supporting Habit Formation in Pre-Meal Photo Capture: A Longitudinal Study of Behavior Change Techniques
papers.abstract: Pre-meal photo capture is lightweight only with a smartphone, yet habit formation requires repeatedly initiating and completing the action within the narrow window before the first bite. We examine how supports based on behavior change techniques can shape capture adherence, perceived habit, and support needs over time. Using a participant-informed selection process, we implemented three smartphone supports targeting Prompts/cues, Focus on past success, and Social support. We evaluated them in a five-week field study with 54 participants, spanning support, withdrawal, and reinstatement, followed by interviews and a three-week follow-up. Across 4,945 main meals, 63.9\% were confirmed pre-meal captures, and adherence was broadly maintained across phases. Perceived automaticity and spontaneous remembering improved mainly during initial support. As capture became more familiar, participants combined spontaneous remembering with deliberate strategies, reduced active feature use while continuing to value support availability, and carried the practice forward through accumulated records, familiar tools, and chosen relationships. These findings frame BCT support for pre-meal photo capture as a configurable arrangement. Systems should preserve a predictable capture pathway while adapting when, how, and through whom support remains available.

papers.title: Classification Aggregation with Multiple Memberships
papers.abstract: People face the problem of classifying objects into categories while aggregating their opinions. We axiomatically study such a classification aggregation problem with multiple memberships, meaning that each individual assigns one category to every object, whereas the resulting classification may assign more than one category. Under the natural settings and axioms (i.e., Independence and Supportiveness), each of our new axioms -- Responsibility, Split Stability and Rejection Stability -- characterises what we call the junta rules. The rules assign a category to an object exactly when some member of a fixed coalition does so. The coalitions that can secure an assignment form a grill, a topological structure implied by an ultrafilter. Hence, the study parallels the literature on Arrow's theorem characterised by the decisive coalition structures. An infinite population setting is also investigated to clarify the differences among the axioms.

papers.title: Distilling Literary Sentiment from LLM Annotations into an Ordinal BERT Model
papers.abstract: The scarcity of human-annotated literary corpora limits the development of domain-specific sentiment analysis models. This study investigates whether LLM-generated annotations can supervise smaller models for literary sentiment analysis. We fine-tune five BERT models using ordinal regression on 10,889 literary sentences annotated by Gemma 4 31B on a ten-point sentiment scale. The models are evaluated against 1,923 human-annotated sentences from Hemingway's "The Old Man and the Sea", alongside the teacher model and conventional baselines. BERT-large achieves a Kendall's $τ$ of 0.589, approaching the teacher's 0.604. Although a constant-neutral predictor achieves the lowest overall mean absolute error (MAE), BERT-base outperforms the teacher on non-neutral sentences, achieving an MAE of 0.726 versus 1.116. These findings demonstrate the potential of LLM-generated supervision for developing smaller literary sentiment models, while highlighting the limitations of aggregate error metrics on predominantly neutral datasets.

papers.title: On local spectra of classical distance-regular graphs with $b = 2$
papers.abstract: Using a combination of spectral techniques and combinatorial counts, we prove a number of non-existence results for putative distance-regular graphs with classical parameters, focusing on the case $b=2$. Among those, the case $(d,b,α,β)=(d,2,1,2^d-2)$ passed all known feasibility conditions and required a deeper combinatorial analysis, from which nonexistence has been derived whenever $d \ge 9$. In doing so, we constructed a new family of regular graphs with four distinct eigenvalues which would have been local graphs in such a distance-regular graph.

papers.title: Language Models Can Benefit from Domain-Specific Inductive Biases
papers.abstract: Language models are typically trained with a single choice of architecture on diverse domains and data sources. Modern transformers have been extensively refined for such general-purpose learning, but are they equally effective across different subsets of the pretraining data? We investigate this question by training small language models from scratch on representative subsets of pretraining data such as web text, code, and mathematics. We introduce variants of transformers in which standard activation functions are replaced with learned splines tuned on specific datasets, providing a simple way to modify their inductive biases. Using a mix-and-match of architectures and datasets, we evaluate cross-domain transfer, i.e. how well does an architecture tuned for one domain perform on data from another? We find that the tuned transformer variants improve training efficiency or generalization on all seven of our tested datasets, but the gains are often domain-specific. For example, architectures tuned on a natural language dataset such as FineWeb perform well on TinyStories, whereas those tuned on mathematics perform poorly on natural language. We identify several mechanisms underlying these improvements, including wider loss basins and more abundant "lottery tickets". Our results show that different subsets of pretraining data can benefit from different learning mechanisms, highlighting a limitation of the prevailing trend towards a small set of general-purpose architectures and optimizers. This points to an opportunity to improve data efficiency by developing domain-specific learning strategies that retain the ability to train general-purpose models.

papers.title: Machine-learning discovery potential for a heavy Higgs boson in $e^+e^-\to ZH$ at a future lepton collider
papers.abstract: We study the discovery potential for a CP-even heavy neutral Higgs boson $H$ in the Type-I two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) at a future $e^+e^-$ collider with $\sqrt{s}=500~\mathrm{GeV}$, focusing on the process $e^+e^-\to ZH$ with $H\to WW$, and with $Z\to\ell\ell$ or $Z\toνν$. The final states are four jets plus two leptons ($4j2\ell$) and four jets plus missing transverse momentum ($4j2ν$). We compare a cut-based analysis with two multivariate strategies: a one-dimensional Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) trained per mass point, and a two-dimensional (BDT $\times$ $m_H$) template analysed with a profile likelihood. The 2D template improves the expected discovery significance by a factor of $2.5$--$3.6$ in the $4j2\ell$ channel and by a factor of $5$--$18$ in the $4j2ν$ channel relative to the cut-based analysis, with the largest gains at high $m_H$ where the cut-based mass window loses efficiency. We translate the expected exclusions into $95\%$ CL upper limits on $σ\times$ BR and discuss the implications for the Type-I 2HDM parameter space.

papers.title: Can You Predict the Next Mind? Toward Multi-Turn Multi-Party Mental World Modeling
papers.abstract: While multimodal foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in physical world modeling, generation, and embodied reasoning, their capacity for dynamic mental world modeling remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks predominantly focus on static mental state perception or short-horizon decision-making, overlooking the dynamic mental trajectories inherent in multi-party, multi-turn interactions. To bridge this gap, we introduce M$^3$WME-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate mental world modeling conditioned on the evolving actions of interactants. Specifically, models are tasked with forecasting a target subject's future mental states and behaviors over extended social interactions. In addition to the benchmark suite, we construct M$^3$WME-23K, a dedicated training dataset, and establish a competitive baseline named MindNext-7B. Extensive evaluations across four representative paradigms (general MLLMs, emotion-specialized MLLMs, agentic frameworks, and World Foundation Models) reveal that current systems consistently struggle to anticipate forward-looking mental states. Mechanistic analyses further reveal that existing architectures fundamentally lack forward mental state transition dynamics. Our findings highlight a pivotal challenge in advancing agents from physical to mental world modeling, charting new directions for socially adaptive AI.

papers.title: Finding Errors Is Not Enough: Selective Model Escalation for Entity-Targeted Sentiment Analysis
papers.abstract: Improving a sentiment classifier with limited resources involves more than simply deciding how much data to collect or which model to train. A labelled collection may lack examples of an important class. Once trained, a classifier may benefit from another model even when that model is weaker on its own. We study these decisions in document-level Entity-Level Sentiment Analysis (ELSA), primarily using South Slavic news. We first compare acquisition orders as collections grow. We then use uncertainty to choose which predictions to revisit, how many to process, and whether an alternative encoder or local LLM can correct them. Finally, we select complete routing policies on development data for held-out evaluation. Minority-prioritised acquisition helps at some very small training sizes, but not consistently thereafter. On SentiCoref, an oracle correcting all errors in the least-confident 10% without harming correct predictions would add 9.14 Macro-F1 points; however the best evaluated action gains only 0.90. Encoder averaging helps on AspectBench and NewsMTSC but harms SentiCoref, where selective LLM assistance is more promising. Both development-selected policies route 30% of records to the encoder-assisted LLM, yielding observed gains of 1.02 points on SentiCoref (interval includes zero) and 1.71 on NewsMTSC, at substantially different inference costs.

papers.title: Same Function, Different CPU: Quantifying Hardware Heterogeneity in Commercial FaaS Platforms
papers.abstract: Serverless computing, particularly Function-as-a-Service (FaaS), abstracts operational concerns such as scaling, scheduling, and resource management from users. This abstraction, however, conceals a heterogeneous hardware fleet on which function execution environments are scheduled behind a unified function interface. Consequently, otherwise identical invocations may run on different CPU types that differ in performance, a hardware lottery that users can neither see nor control. Since the resulting variability is entangled with other sources, such as noisy neighbors or diurnal effects, its contribution to overall performance variability and how this contribution differs across providers remain unclear. In this paper, we systematically study hardware heterogeneity and its impact on function performance across four widely used commercial FaaS platforms, covering regional, configurational, and temporal differences. Using variance decomposition, we find that CPU heterogeneity alone explains 4 % to 97 % of the performance variance on AWS Lambda and Google Cloud Run Functions. On Azure Functions, in contrast, we identify a platform-level mechanism that produces bimodal execution durations and overshadows CPU effects. We observe that the CPU composition on AWS Lambda shifts within a single week. Additionally, we reveal that on Google Cloud Run Functions and Alibaba Function Compute, the availability of instruction set extensions such as SHA-NI differs between CPU types, widening the performance gap further. Since all platforms bill by duration, performance gaps between CPU types translate directly into cost, with invocations on the slowest CPU type costing up to three times as much as those on the fastest.

papers.title: Fischer-Burmeister-based Multiplier Dynamics in Inequality-Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: We study proportional-integral multiplier feedback for inequality-constrained optimization using the Fischer-Burmeister complementarity residual. We construct explicit dynamics and characterize gain-dependent stability and convergence rates. For a single active constraint, we derive exact local stability and decay-rate conditions, including a tradeoff between continuous-time convergence and discretization costs. For strongly convex objectives with affine constraints, we establish global convergence and characterize geometric conditions for uniform exponential stability. Numerical experiments compare feedback structures and computational costs.

papers.title: MS-DOTT: A Multi-Modal Dataset for Off-Road Traversability Estimation
papers.abstract: Autonomous robots are gaining traction in off-road environments, driven by their rising demand in agriculture, defense, and search-and-rescue operations. However, these environments are inherently unpredictable and navigation remains a formidable challenge given the complex environmental conditions including challenging terrain and varying illumination. Off-road autonomy requires robust perception across multiple spatial scales and imaging modalities, yet most sensing setups struggle to capture both far-field environmental context and near-field terrain detail simultaneously across various illumination conditions. To facilitate development of robust off-road perception and traversability estimation systems, we propose MS-DOTT (Multi-Sensor Dataset for Off-road Terrain Traversability) a comprehensive multi-modal off-road dataset with long-range 3D sensing and short-range, fine-grained perception to facilitate high-fidelity terrain understanding by combining proprioceptive signals for tracking vehicle dynamics with exteroceptive imaging and pointcloud data. The dataset includes trajectories recorded across nominal lighting, low-light, and no-light conditions with diverse 2D and 3D sensing for both long-range large-scale and short-range high-resolution sensing, as well as 4D RADAR measurements that provide velocity estimates for detected pointclouds. We demonstrate the utility of the dataset by adapting a SOTA multi-sensor fusion method for the purpose of traversability estimation. This dataset will aid the robotics community in advancing research and development of methods for traversability estimation, off-road perception and multi-sensor fusion in unstructured environments.

papers.title: Needle-beam generation from SPDC photons using inverse-designed flat optics
papers.abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the generation of needle-like beams from spontaneous parametric downconversion (SPDC) light using a compact inverse-designed multilevel diffractive lens (MDL). The nonclassical nature of the SPDC source is independently verified through a three-detector heralded Hanbury Brown-Twiss measurement performed before the MDL, yielding a zero-delay second-order correlation value of approximately 0.14. Spatial measurements using an intensified charge-coupled device reveal that the MDL maintains a tightly confined focal distribution over an axial distance of approximately 11 mm under collinear SPDC illumination, substantially reducing diffraction-induced broadening compared with a conventional plano-convex lens of the same nominal focal length. Under non-collinear SPDC illumination, two distinct regions of extended axial confinement are observed, demonstrating the dependence of the engineered focal distribution on the incident spatial field. These results establish a compact flat-optical approach for engineering extended-focus SPDC photon fields, with potential applications in structured quantum photonics.

papers.title: Computational performance versus numerical accuracy in the acoustic terms of weakly-compressible SPH
papers.abstract: Accurate computation of the acoustic terms in weakly-compressible SPH, including the equation of state, its inverse, and the evaluation of the local speed of sound, is essential to ensure energy conservation, robust solid boundary conditions, and correct open boundary behavior. In the classic Cole's equation of state, using values of the polytropic constant $γ\ne 1$ can lead to significant precision loss, particularly when computations are performed in single precision, as is common in GPU implementations. We extend here our previous results on the optimal choice of state variable by introducing a new higher-precision form for all three acoustic terms, denoted \texttt{explog}, and assess its numerical accuracy and computational performance across a variety of devices and test cases. We find that the new form evaluates the acoustic terms with a maximum ULP of~2 for arguments less than $0.125$, and has higher errors in less than 1\% of the arguments larger than the threshold. Combined with a rewritten expression of the pressure at solid boundary particles in the ``dummy'' model, it provides consistently more accurate results, maintaining deviations from the reference pressure profile to below 2\%, even in presence of a rough bottom terrain. Computationally, the new formulation is also faster than the naive one on GPU, and only marginally slower on CPU.

papers.title: ILLRAW: Illumination-Aware RAW Object Detection
papers.abstract: Existing RAW-based detectors typically introduce learnable ISP modules to convert RAW inputs into sRGB-like formats to fit off-the-shelf detectors. However, this RAW-to-sRGB paradigm decouples representation learning from the downstream detection task. Crucially, it forces the network to inherit human-centric visual priors while discarding intrinsic RAW advantages, such as linear sensor responses and high-bit-depth, minimally processed scene cues. In this paper, we propose \textbf{ILLRAW}, an \textbf{ILL}umination-aware end-to-end \textbf{RAW} object detection framework. Instead of reconstructing visually plausible sRGB images, ILLRAW directly learns detection-oriented RAW features through a lightweight feature adapter inserted at the input stage of existing detectors. ILLRAW estimates an illumination mask and introduces channel-sensitive embeddings to model Bayer-channel responses. These features are fused by an illumination attention fusion module. Experiments show clear improvements on the diverse AODRaw benchmark and competitive performance on LOD and PascalRAW, with particularly strong results under dark exposure.

papers.title: LLMs and the Organization of Scientific Work
papers.abstract: The advent of large language models (LLMs) represents a technological revolution for science. Their diffusion may reshape not only how scientists conduct research, but also how they organize their work within teams. Here, we develop a conceptual framework in which LLMs expand individual capabilities across a range of research activities, reducing reliance on complementary human inputs within tasks and facilitating a more specialized division of labor among team members. We further propose that teams' history of collaboration may constrain their ability to reorganize in response to the new technological capabilities. Using CRediT contribution statements from approximately 120,000 PLOS ONE articles published between 2018 and 2025, we investigate changes in the division of labor within scientific teams following the release of ChatGPT in late 2022. We document three main findings. First, participation in scientific tasks falls below its previous trajectory, particularly in conceptualization, execution, and writing. Second, researchers become more specialized, exhibiting narrower task portfolios and less overlap in their contributions with co-authors. Third, these changes are concentrated among newly formed teams, whose members have no prior collaboration ties, whereas established teams, whose members have all collaborated previously, exhibit considerably greater organizational inertia. Our findings suggest that, in the wake of LLM diffusion, scientific work is being reorganized around greater individual autonomy and an increasingly specialized division of labor within teams.

papers.title: Emergent stigmergy and pheromone-guided decisions in a foraging collective
papers.abstract: Ants in a colony forage and recruit other nest-mates for cooperative transport of food through stigmergy. Traditional approach to capture the foraging dynamics relies on fine-tuning phenomenological rules for pheromone deposition, chemotaxis, evaporation, and behavioral switching after reaching the food source. Here, we show that stigmergy emerges from an infinite-horizon stochastic optimal control problem involving outbound foragers traveling from the nest to the food source and returning agents traveling from the food source to the nest. Pheromone dynamics along a trail emerge from the forward propagating Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, with the Bellman discount rate setting the rate of pheromone evaporation. Using this mapping, we identify the conditions under which trail feedback suppresses exploration or leads to the exploitation of established trails. For ants exploring multiple trails, we also find flux-potential relations, analogous to Ohm's law, with ant flux and inverse of squared value field playing the roles of current and resistance on the network. Our model captures collective behavior observed in the classic double-bridge experiments: trail selection on identical routes through a symmetry-breaking instability, selection of the shorter bridge, and bistability in the trail-length ratio that can leave ants transiently committed to the longer route. Our formulation places collective foraging in the broader framework of stochastic optimal control, while simultaneously providing an unifying picture on their emergent behavior consistent with experimental observations.

papers.title: Local limit Theorem for Directed polymers in a random environment in the full weak disorder regime
papers.abstract: For directed polymers in random environment, we provide a short and mostly self-contained proof of the local limit theorem in the full weak disorder phase, including the critical inverse temperature $β_c$. That is, the point-to-point partition function is well approximated by the product of two independent point-to-line partition functions (one starting from each endpoint of the system) multiplied by the simple random walk transition kernel. The approximation is valid in the $L^p$ sense for an optimal range of $p$. The result is new at $β=β_c$ and for $p>2$, and in all cases the proof is significantly simpler, technically and conceptually, than what can be found in the literature. As a consequence of the result we establish an invariance principle for the polymer measure with fixed end-point, valid for all $β\in [0,β_c]$.

papers.title: SyncHeC: Markerless Spatio-Temporal Hand-Eye Calibration via Differentiable Rendering and Continuous-Time Joint Optimization
papers.abstract: Markerless hand-eye calibration under continuous motion requires jointly resolving camera geometry and the time offset between images and joint states. We present SyncHeC (Synchronized Hand-Eye Calibration), a dense differentiable-rendering framework that estimates both from a single robot trajectory. Continuous-time forward kinematics makes latency differentiable, metric depth complements mask contours, and an offline planner combines spatial sensitivity with temporal excitation. Alternating updates support Eye-to-Hand, Eye-in-Hand, and multi-camera calibration. On a 7-DoF arm, one $6.5$\,s motion yields $0.21$\,cm translation error against a marker-board reference, $0.34$\,cm touch-test error, and $2.7$\,ms latency error relative to an $87$\,ms reference with $95\%$ uncertainty of $\pm1.5$\,ms. Against CM-Calib on matched recordings, translation and nominal latency errors improve by $3.7\times$ and $2.3\times$. Experiments span seven arms and four depth sensors. Compensating the recovered offset during policy training and deployment increases success by $8.1$ percentage points across six families and six tasks ($1{,}800$ matched pairs; paired $95\%$ confidence interval $[6.3,9.9]$ points).

papers.title: Fluid Antenna Array-Enabled Near-Field ISAC: Joint Port Position Optimization and Transmit Beamforming Design
papers.abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) have shown that activating a single port from a densely packed antenna array can yield spatial diversity comparable to that of tens of independent antennas, a property that has substantially improved communication reliability and efficiency. The fluid antenna array (FAA) extends this concept to multi-port configurations while avoiding complex multi-dimensional spatial correlation, and offers significant geometrical flexibility under a finite aperture and a limited port budget. These attributes motivate environment-adaptive array geometry for sensing in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Although this flexibility enables adaptive array geometries that exploit near-field distance-angle information, improving multi-parameter target estimation under communication and deployment constraints remains challenging. In this paper, we propose a planar FAA-assisted near-field ISAC framework for multiuser communication and target sensing. Specifically, we derive the Fisher information matrix (FIM) and the corresponding Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for the joint estimation of target range, zenith angle, azimuth angle, and radial velocity. Based on the derived CRB, we jointly optimize the FAA port positions and transmit beamforming to improve sensing accuracy while satisfying communication signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), transmit power, and physical deployment constraints. To solve the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a two-stage alternating optimization algorithm, in which transmit beamforming is optimized through semidefinite relaxation (SDR), while FAA port positions are successively optimized through discrete search and continuous refinement. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm achieves favorable sensing performance while maintaining a reasonable computational cost.

papers.title: Features Extraction Across Multi-Source Heterogeneous Data
papers.abstract: High-dimensional data from multiple sources often combine shared structure with source-specific variation. We study heterogeneous principal component analysis, which seeks to recover common and private principal subspaces when their dimensions are unknown. {We propose \emph{Feature Extraction (FE)}, a novel data-driven framework with two steps. First, the Eigenvector-based Spike-Count (ESC) estimator determines the number of principal components (PC) in each source using only sample eigenvector information, rather than eigenvalue-based criteria. Second, FE identifies the locations of common features by comparing bias-corrected inner products between sample eigenvectors across sources. These matches yield estimates of the common and source-specific subspaces without iterative optimization. We establish the consistency of our estimators under a spiked covariance model in a high-dimensional regime where the dimension and sample size grow proportionally. Simulations and applications to federated image data and U.S. housing prices demonstrate the performance of FE in rank recovery, subspace estimation, and data reconstruction.} Code is available at https://github.com/liwenbo-research/HeterogeneousPCA

papers.title: Quantifying Bicycle Setup Differences on the Road: Field Estimates of CdA, Crr and Power Demand
papers.abstract: Individual bicycle configurations can be assessed in situ using power and speed measurements without a velodrome or wind tunnel. We apply an integrated energy-balance workflow to five configurations tested by one rider on a road section. Five nominal power levels, each ridden in both directions, yield 25 paired observations. Kinetic-energy changes are corrected explicitly; gravitational work cancels between spatially matched outward and return sections. A shared effective rolling-resistance coefficient Crr and a separate aerodynamic drag area CdA for each setup are estimated jointly. The fitted drag areas range from 0.2288 to 0.3601m^2, with a common Crr=0.00551 +/- 0.00047. At 40km/h, the estimated differences are 17.4 +/- 5.5W favouring the EZ-covered over the uncovered 80mm rear-wheel configuration and 64.3 +/- 4.0W favouring the aerobar position over the drops on the tested road bike. The helmet swap yields a difference of 3.5 +/- 2.8W. Reported uncertainties combine statistical variability and assumed input uncertainties and represent one standard deviation. The study demonstrates a practical workflow for quantifying individual setup differences and connecting resistance estimates to power-speed predictions under specified reference conditions.

papers.title: Noise-resilient collective order through temporal memory in self-propelled particles
papers.abstract: Temporal memory can stabilise collective motion by filtering noisy local observations, but persistent information can also impede adaptation when the collective state changes. We investigate this competition in Vicsek-type systems using two distinct alignment rules: a finite buffer of past observations and a recursive update of an internal directional state. In both models, increasing effective memory shifts the loss of polar order to stronger noise and can restore ordered motion under conditions for which the corresponding memoryless Vicsek model is disordered. The stationary responses of the two models show an approximate correspondence when parameterised by a kernel-based effective memory, consistent with temporal averaging playing a common role in their ordering behaviour rather than from the details of the memory implementation. Their transient dynamics, however, are not determined by effective memory alone. Following a collective perturbation, recovery is fastest at an intermediate memory depth and becomes slower when outdated observations are retained too strongly. Temporal integration therefore produces a trade-off: deeper memory improves noise resilience, whereas excessive persistence reduces responsiveness. These results identify memory depth as a control parameter that separates the optimisation of stationary order from that of dynamical recovery in noisy active systems.

papers.title: Shot-to-shot statistical fluctuations during beam self-cleaning in multimode fibers
papers.abstract: Beam self-cleaning in multimode optical fibers has recently been interpreted within a thermodynamic framework, in which nonlinear propagation drives the optical field towards a statistical equilibrium state. While this interpretation has been supported by measurements of modal populations and entropy, the role of shot-to-shot spatial fluctuations of the output beam has so far remained unexplored. Here, we experimentally show that the transverse output beam profile becomes progressively more reproducible from shot to shot as beam self-cleaning develops. This behavior is consistent with the thermodynamic expectation that relative fluctuations become increasingly small as the system approaches equilibrium.

papers.title: BLPO: Beyond-Local Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon tasks require large language model (LLM) agents to coordinate interdependent actions, a capability central to automating complex workflows. Stepwise group-based reinforcement learning provides finer credit than trajectory-level supervision, but reliable comparisons must account for differences in interaction history. Enforcing this consistency within the limited rollouts of each task can leave insufficient support for estimating action preferences. We propose Beyond-Local Policy Optimization (BLPO), which estimates task-progress advantages from experience shared across tasks and training updates. We summarize trajectory prefixes into task-progress states and abstract actions by their function, allowing corresponding decisions from different tasks to contribute to shared estimates. To control bias and noise from heterogeneous tasks, we accumulate context-relative returns in a global memory with balanced aggregation and reliability weighting. These global advantages complement local comparisons over normalized actions and trajectory-level credit without a learned critic or additional rollouts. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop with 1.5B and 7B policies show improved task success over the evaluated baselines under matched training budgets. Further analyses show faster learning and shorter trajectories with little computational overhead.

papers.title: Decomposition of disk and jet optical emission: Case of PKS~1510-089 and PKS~0736+017
papers.abstract: Measuring BLR size and black hole mass of jetted quasars with strong radio emission is challenging due to the contribution from non-thermal synchrotron radiation from the jet in the optical continuum. Here, we investigate the optical continuum emission in two flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs), PKS~0736+017 and PKS~1510-089, by separating the thermal emission from the accretion disk and the non-thermal synchrotron emission from the jet using their distinct polarization signatures. Our analysis combines multi-epoch optical spectro-photometric and polarimetric observations from the archival optical continuum, H$β$ emission line light curves from earlier reverberation mapping campaigns, and 37 GHz radio data. For PKS~0736+017, we find that the disk contributes approximately 70 % ($f_d = 0.70^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$) of the total optical emission. After removing the jet component, we obtain a revised H$β$ lag of $84.8^{+23.2}_{-18.4}$ days. In contrast, the disk contribution in PKS~1510-089 is lower with 37.5 % ($f_d = 0.37^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$), with a corresponding H$β$ lag of $54.4^{+4.4}_{-5.4}$ days. Our findings highlight the need for careful decomposition of optical light curves in jet-dominated AGN.

papers.title: Q-CamTuning: A Multimodal Large Language Model for Fine-Grained Quality Reasoning in Livestreaming Camera Tuning
papers.abstract: With the popularization of livestreaming applications, automatic camera tuning has become indispensable for ordinary users to enjoy high Quality of Experience (QoE). However, the existing Image Quality Assessment (IQA) methods face two challenges in camera tuning. First, they struggle to identify subtle quality difference between images, which is common in camera tuning. Second, the ability to explain fine-grained differences and to provide suggestions for camera tuning are even more lacking. To address these challenges, we first construct FGLive-Comments, an instruction tuning dataset with rich annotations of both preferences for fine-grained image pairs and quality reasoning from global and local visual evidence, which supports selective adjustment recommendations of camera parameters. Based on FGLive-Comments, we develop Q-CamTuning, a multimodal large language model for livestreaming camera tuning. Its progressive perception-evidence-guidance framework learns quality-aware visual representations, enhances fine-grained reasoning with global-local evidence, and maps quality issues to camera-parameter adjustment directions. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that Q-CamTuning outperforms existing IQA models in both quality scoring and fine-grained image pair ranking. User study also validates its ability to recommend camera tuning suggestions.

papers.title: E-GenRM: Generative Reward Modeling for Open-Ended E-Commerce Shopping Agents
papers.abstract: We present E-GenRM (E-commerce Generative Reward Model), a generative reward model tailored to e-commerce shopping agents. User expectations are shifting from simple product queries to open-ended shopping tasks. However, existing trajectories and reward designs remain largely bounded by current agent usage patterns and known failures, providing limited guidance for further capability improvement. These limitations call for an integrated reward modeling framework for open-ended shopping agent tasks. On the data side, E-GenRM leverages naturally occurring user behavior across the shopping app to construct diverse, long-horizon conversational trajectories beyond established usage patterns. On the modeling side, E-GenRM first learns from behavior-grounded evaluation chains through supervised fine-tuning. It is then optimized through criterion-guided reinforcement learning, which rewards correct preference judgments and evidence-supported factual claims under each criterion. Personalized hard-negative training further improves its sensitivity to user preferences reflected in shopping behavior, beyond explicit requirements. We additionally develop an active evidence retrieval extension that acquires missing e-commerce information for evaluation. On E-GenRM-Bench, E-GenRM-27B achieves 87.40\% preference accuracy, outperforming the strongest baseline by 6.97 percentage points. In a 14-day online A/B test on Taobao, a shopping agent post-trained with E-GenRM improves the effective shopping-assistance rate by 1.39 percentage points and user satisfaction by 2.33 percentage points.

papers.title: Systematic Derivation of Leakage in Massey Secret Sharing Schemes
papers.abstract: Leakage attacks on secret sharing schemes can be based on the exploitation of partial information about individual shares to recover the underlying secret. In coding theory, linear exact repair schemes (LERSs) allow the recovery of a codeword symbol from limited information obtained from the remaining symbols.
