We compute the residual entropies of both models with transfer matrices on cylinders of up to twelve vertices in circumference, extrapolated with the finite-size correction predicted by conformal invariance, which we adapt to the triangular geometry and verify at two exactly solved points. The number of upward arrows crossing the cylinder is conserved, and the cost of changing it shows that both models are critical, with the long-distance behaviour of a free massless field. Chiral ice is the extreme point of a region of the phase diagram in which ordering had been suggested; along two paths through that region we find the same critical behaviour at every point, with no feature at the proposed boundary of the region. Along Baxter's exactly solved curve we obtain the corresponding exponents in closed form.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
papers.abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We prove strict strong positivity for good prefixes with at most three repeated blocks after the first factor. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguyên's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact Kähler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential positivity and on solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.

papers.title: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.

papers.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements
papers.abstract: Despite recent advances in CUAs, their development remains constrained by the limited diversity, controllability, and reliability of interaction data. Moreover, conventional optimization pipelines lack iterative feedback, while existing recursive improvement approaches often rely on self-generated experiences, limiting ability expansion and yielding diminishing returns. To address these challenges, we introduce CUA-Master, a nested double-loop recursive improvement framework. At the system level, an outer world-data-model flywheel continuously incorporates open-world corpus and leverages evolving model weaknesses to guide subsequent data construction and optimization iterations. At the data level, an inner flywheel couples open-world seeding and autocatalytic propagation. The former mines authentic workflows as seed tasks from instructional videos, and employs visual-semantic dual-path trajectory reconstruction; The latter transforms these seeds into reusable primitives for controllable synthesis of diverse, complex, and verifiable tasks. To enable efficient and reliable trajectory collection, we further introduce a feedback-guided snapshot-rollback retry mechanism in various real environments. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CUA-Master-27B achieves competitive performance across GUI-only and GUI-CLI hybrid benchmarks, scoring 80.2 on OSWorld Verified, 36.9 on OSWorld 2.0, 43.9 on WeaveBench, and 25.0 on Agents' Last Exam. Our framework also substantially improves the quality and efficiency of data synthesis, and exhibits continuous gains across recursive iterations.

papers.title: Failure of bounded $\bar\partial$-solvability on pseudoconvex domains of finite type
papers.abstract: We show that for every integer $n\ge3$ there is a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with smooth real-analytic boundary whose maximum boundary D'Angelo $1$-type is $16$, carrying a $\bar\partial$-closed form continuous on the closure and smooth in the domain with no bounded distributional solution. On each fixed domain, we also construct a uniformly bounded sequence of smooth $\bar\partial$-closed data for which every bounded solution has norm at least $ck^{1/320}$ for all sufficiently large $k$. Each datum in this sequence and a corresponding solution extend smoothly to a neighborhood of the closure. The obstruction comes from a singular curve in two weak complex tangential directions, whose normalization admits holomorphic functions that do not extend to a neighborhood of the curve.

papers.title: Belief Propagation-Informed Tesseract Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: In quantum error correction, the decoder must estimate the errors from the measurement data accurately and fast enough to avoid a backlog. Search-based decoders such as Tesseract achieve high accuracy by finding a minimum-weight set of error events with an A* search, but their search effort grows rapidly with the physical error rate and the code size. To reduce this search effort while maintaining a logical error rate close to that of Tesseract, we propose a belief propagation (BP)-guided modification of the Tesseract decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Damped sum-product BP is applied to the triggered detectors before the Tesseract search. If the detectors triggered by the BP hard decision match the triggered detectors, this hard decision is accepted directly, and the Tesseract search is skipped. Otherwise, the BP marginal probability estimates, weighted by a trust coefficient, modify the search priority, while the path cost keeps the channel-prior weights so that the decoding objective is unchanged. The framework also supports BP-based initialization, in which selected BP decisions form the starting point of a residual search whose signed-cost objective allows incorrect initial decisions to be removed. A node-exploration limit bounds this residual search; if the limit is reached, the decoder falls back to the BP-guided search on the original triggered detector set. The method is evaluated on the [[72,12,6]], [[90,8,10]], and [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle codes under circuit-level noise. With BP-based initialization and a global trust coefficient, the number of Tesseract search nodes expanded is reduced by up to more than two orders of magnitude at low physical error rates, while the logical error rate remains close to that of Tesseract.

papers.title: Global attractor for weakly damped nonlinear parametric Klein-Gordon Schr{ö}dinger system
papers.abstract: We consider a damped forced nonlinear Klein-Gordon Schr\''{o}dinger (KGS) system known as the parametric KGS system with Yukawa coupling. We prove the regularity of the global attractor for this infinite-dimensional dynamical system, i.e. that the global attractor is included into a smaller Sobolev space than the energy space. We prove that this global attractor has finite fractal dimension, without any assumption on the decay of the forcing terms.

papers.title: An Information Hierarchy of Privacy Filters and Odometers
papers.abstract: In sequential data analysis, privacy loss accumulates over time, and privacy filters and odometers are used to control and track this cumulative cost. We study how the information used by differential privacy filters and odometers fundamentally limits what they can achieve. We formalise three levels of information: spec-level information, fixed prior to the interaction; mechanism-level information, which includes the mechanisms instantiated during the interaction; and realisation-level information, which further includes the realised interaction. We classify privacy filters and odometers by the least informative level sufficient to determine their behaviour. Our main results establish strict and arbitrarily large separations in achievable performance across this information hierarchy. For privacy filters, moving up the hierarchy can yield an unbounded utility advantage, quantified by a clipped measure of the number of allowed releases. For privacy odometers, it can yield an arbitrarily large improvement in precision, quantified by the expected peak excess of the reported bound over the realised privacy loss. Further, although the information classes are distinct, we show that moving to a richer class need incur essentially no loss in performance. Finally, we show that randomisation provides a resource orthogonal to information: at every information level, it can yield an arbitrarily large utility improvement over deterministic filters. Thus, information access and randomisation can be viewed as fundamental resources governing privacy procedures in adaptive interactions.

papers.title: Molecular gas in the disks and tails of ram pressure stripped Coma galaxies
papers.abstract: We present new IRAM 30 m observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) emission in five Coma cluster galaxies undergoing ram pressure stripping. Molecular gas is detected in four galaxies, and CO emission is clearly detected in the stripped tails of three, extending up to $\sim50$ kpc from the stellar disks. The molecular gas masses in the tails range from a few $\times10^8\,M_\odot$ and account for up to 10-20% of the molecular gas remaining in the parent disks. Compared with field scaling relations, several galaxies exhibit elevated molecular-to-stellar gas ratios despite being H I deficient. This enhancement persists toward the lower-mass end of our sample, even in the massive Coma cluster environment, consistent with ram-pressure-induced compression of atomic gas and enhanced H I-to-H$_2$ conversion in the disks. At the same time, the total gas fractions of most galaxies remain close to those of field galaxies with similar stellar masses when the molecular gas in the tails is included, indicating that gas removal and phase transformation act simultaneously. We further investigate the relation between molecular and ionized gas by comparing CO and H$α$ emission in the stripped regions. Although CO is preferentially detected in H$α$-bright regions, the increased scatter compared with previous studies suggests the presence of both star-forming and diffuse CO components in the tails. Our results highlight the dual role of ram pressure stripping in dense environments: it efficiently removes gas from galaxies while also promoting molecular gas formation in both the disks and stripped material, thereby shaping short-term star formation in cluster galaxies.

papers.title: Behavioral Affinity Transduction for Zero-Shot Vision-Language Classification
papers.abstract: An image that is hard to classify on its own may have a helpful neighbor in the same unlabeled batch. Zero-shot vision-language models (VLMs) score images independently and leave this evidence unused. We study small unlabeled query batches with no labeled examples. Visual similarity can reflect pose or background, so it may connect images from different classes. Each image's scores over the class vocabulary offer another way to choose neighbors. We introduce Behavioral Affinity Transduction (BAT), which builds a sparse graph from these class-response profiles. The graph supplies neighbor evidence during prediction. For EM-Dirichlet, it also screens candidate classes and initializes assignments. BAT plugs into direct and iterative readouts of a frozen VLM. Across diverse datasets, BAT improves the mean accuracy of every tested readout. In the main RN50 comparison, soft and hard EM-Dirichlet gain $4.22$ and $2.72$ percentage points.

papers.title: Meet Students Where They Are: Student-Prefix Teacher Adaptation for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) mitigates the student's exposure bias by optimizing on student-generated trajectories. However, student-generated prefixes may contain reasoning errors or follow patterns unfamiliar to the teacher, undermining the reliability of its token-level supervision. This degradation becomes more pronounced as prefixes grow longer. To address this teacher-side distribution mismatch, we propose Student-Prefix Teacher Adaptation (SPTA), which adapts the teacher to the states on which it is queried during distillation. Specifically, before OPD starts, we collect student rollout prefixes with random lengths and continually train the teacher to continue from the prefixes using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). By treating each prefix as context and rewarding correct final answers, the teacher learns to recover from student-induced states rather than imitate the student's reasoning. Then, the adapted teacher is used for standard OPD, with no changes to the distillation objective. Experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks show that our SPTA improves average student performance over standard OPD and OPD with task-level RLVR-adapted teachers. These results highlight the importance of adapting teachers not only to solve problems independently, but also to provide reliable guidance on the states their students actually visit.

papers.title: Global attractor for two-dimensional weakly damped nonlinear parametric Klein-Gordon Schrodinger system
papers.abstract: We consider a damped forced nonlinear Klein-Gordon Schr {ö}dinger (KGS) system known as the parametric KGS system with Yukawa coupling where the space variable belongs to R 2 . We prove the existence of a global attractor in dimension 2. Moreover we prove that this global attractor is regular and has finite fractal dimension.

papers.title: From Simulation to Sustainable Urban Mobility: A Purpose-Driven Framework for Advanced EV Charging Technology Transfer
papers.abstract: The integration of electric vehicles (EVs) into urban mobility systems offers both opportunities and challenges for cities pursuing sustainability and energy efficiency. While simulation-based approaches have demonstrated the technical feasibility of advanced charging strategies, such as smart charging, bidirectional charging, and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G), their real-world impact is often constrained by policy, business models, and stakeholder engagement. This paper introduces a purpose-driven technology transfer (PDTT) framework that systematically connects simulation insights with the needs of urban stakeholders. Leveraging a modular simulation architecture based on Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO), we evaluate the operational and sustainability impacts of advanced EV charging in complex urban scenarios, assessing indicators such as energy efficiency and CO2 emissions. The PDTT framework guides the translation of simulation results into actionable pathways for deployment, policy design, and market innovation, supporting co-creation with city planners, utilities, and communities. Our findings highlight the value of simulation as a diagnostic and engagement tool, and demonstrate how a multidimensional, stakeholder-centered approach can accelerate the sustainable adoption of advanced EV charging technologies in smart city contexts.

papers.title: Znaki: A Russian Fingerspelling Recognition Dataset
papers.abstract: Fingerspelling - the sequential signing of letters that compose proper names, technical terms, and out-of-vocabulary words - is an integral component of any sign language. Despite Russian Sign Language (RSL) being used by more than 150,000 native signers, no public fingerspelling dataset for RSL exists, in contrast to American, British, German, and several other sign languages. We introduce Znaki the first open RSL fingerspelling dataset: 37,252 video recordings (35.4 hours) of 1,593 unique sequences - proper names sampled from 16 domain categories - recorded by 68 native RSL signers (37 Deaf, 29 hard-of-hearing, and 2 certified interpreters) through a crowdsourcing pipeline with a two-stage signer qualification procedure and expert validation. The dataset covers all 33 Cyrillic handshapes, and its letter-frequency distribution matches the Russian National Corpus. As reference points for future research, we establish two baselines adapted from American Sign Language fingerspelling recognition: a Squeezeformer-based encoder-decoder, reaching a character-level accuracy ($1-\mathrm{CER}$) of 0.932 and a sequence accuracy of 0.596, and Fingerspelling-PoseNet, reaching 0.886 and 0.545, respectively.

papers.title: De-lensing cosmic birefringence with joint reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstruction of anisotropic cosmic birefringence from the CMB is limited by lensing $B$-mode sample variance and partially degenerate with the lensing curl. We study the joint reconstruction of lensing (gradient and curl) and birefringence at the maximum-a-posteriori point, whose spectra are near-optimal statistics. We predict the joint response and noise analytically, validate them on simulations, and show unbiased inference of its amplitude. Errors will shrink $5$-fold relative to quadratic estimators at SPT-3G+ depths, promising much tighter constraints on parity-violating new physics, owing to the removal of the lensing $B$-polarization sample variance.

papers.title: Dynamic Coalition Formation Under Capacity Constraints: A Regime-Switching Value-Investing Game
papers.abstract: Edge computing service deployment requires the Network Operator (NO) and Service Providers (SPs) to coordinate investment and resource allocation under uncertain demand. This paper develops an audit-based service management framework for daily coalition formation with fixed capacity and service-level agreement (SLA) reservations. A two-stage coalitional game separates infrastructure investment from operational participation. Demand follows a Geometric Random Walk (GRW), and SPs apply an ordered admission and suspension rule using reported marginal contributions. With the NO held fixed, the operational coalition value is submodular; mandatory reservations can produce negative Shapley payoffs. We derive a separable benchmark, compute operational Shapley allocations, and give a sufficient condition for convergence to an individual equilibrium. A probabilistic audit mechanism provides a conditional daily truthfulness guarantee under verified settlement and enforceable penalties. For five service classes over three years, the reference run gains 12.4% over static grand-coalition membership and recovers 94.6% of the full-information optimum. Across 30 runs, the median gain is 13.3%. Sensitivity tests examine policy parameters, capacity and alternative demand models. The gain depends on capacity and update order; abundant capacity can make the admission rule underperform static membership.

papers.title: KlaskTron: An Open-Source Platform for Physical Adversarial Multi-Agent RL
papers.abstract: Progress in robot learning, particularly physical multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), is currently challenged by a limited availability of accessible, standardized benchmarks. While simulation-based MARL has produced remarkable emergent behaviors, from coordinated team play to complex tool use, translating these advances to physical systems remains difficult. A key barrier is infrastructural: physical platforms are often prohibitively expensive, require specialized facilities, or lack open mechanisms and designs for reproducibility. We introduce KlaskTron, an open-source, low-cost (<\$2500 USD), desktop-scale robotic testbed for adversarial MARL based on the dynamic tabletop game KLASK. The platform features dual CoreXY gantries with high-torque brushless motors, enabling the high-speed, precise manipulation required for competitive play. Crucially, we provide a complete ecosystem: hardware designs (CAD, BOM), a GPU-native digital twin in NVIDIA Isaac Lab for high-fidelity modeling and simulation, and a validated sim-to-real baseline using a learned neural actuator model. We demonstrate that this baseline enables zero-shot policy transfer, with trained agents exhibiting emergent adversarial behaviors. To ensure full reproducibility of our results, all project assets are released publicly: hardware CAD/BOM and assembly documentation at [https://idscethzurich.github.io/klask_hardware], inference software stack at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_software] and the simulation and MARL setup at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_rl].

papers.title: Regularity of core coupled high-spin structure in neutron-rich $^{196-202}$Au isotopes approaching N $=126$
papers.abstract: Excited states built upon long-lived high-spin isomers in hard-to-reach neutron-rich Au ($Z=79$) isotopes were populated using multi-nucleon transfer reactions between $^{136}$Xe and $^{198}$Pt at 7 MeV/u. These states in $^{196,\,198-202}$Au were identified for the first time using the powerful combination of the VAMOS++ spectrometer, the CATLIFE detection system, and the AGATA $γ$-ray tracking array. Their measured energies exhibit remarkable regularity as a function of neutron number and are seen to be inherited from the energies of yrast-band members in the corresponding Hg ($Z=80$) isotope. Large-scale shell-model calculations reproduce the observed regularity and show that these states arise from the unique-parity orbitals $\pi0h_{11/2}$ and $\nu0i_{13/2}$ coupled to the Hg core. This regularity is due to the dominant proton configurations of the Hg and Au isotopes, where the level energies are almost independent of different neutron-orbital occupancies. The calculated Au wave functions show significant higher-spin components of the corresponding Hg core, unlike what is expected in the conventional interpretation in terms of the weak-coupling/decoupling limits of the particle-core coupling model.

papers.title: When Optimization Meets Human Intent: Human-Centered Diffusion Model Optimization
papers.abstract: Diffusion models are evolving from general tools into personalized systems that adapt to user needs through fine-tuning and guidance. However, diffusion optimization mainly targets measurable objectives such as aesthetics, rarely examining whether they align with human intent. Human needs are multidimensional, contextual, and dynamic, whereas existing methods approximate them with fixed metrics. Because these metrics capture human needs only partially and may amplify deviations from true intent during optimization, higher scores need not yield results better matching human expectations. To understand how human needs enter and influence optimization, we systematically analyze how human intent is expressed, translated into optimizable objectives, applied to model behavior or generation, and evaluated through outputs. We further discuss trade-offs affecting human-intent alignment in personalized image generation and gaps between automated metrics and real user judgments. This human-centered synthesis reorganizes diffusion optimization and provides a systematic reference for personalized generation systems designed for human preferences.

papers.title: Exact fermionic matrix elements from the Bethe-ansatz solution of the Richardson-Gaudin model
papers.abstract: We introduce an effective Hamiltonian description of mesoscopic superconducting systems based on the Bethe-ansatz solution of the Richardson--Gaudin model. Our central result is a compact determinant formula for the matrix elements of fermionic creation and annihilation operators, expressed entirely in terms of eigenvalue-based variables. This formula allows single-electron tunneling terms to be represented directly in the eigenbasis of the Richardson--Gaudin model, extending the eigenvalue-based framework beyond overlaps and previously known form factors. As a benchmark, we apply the method to a superconducting Anderson impurity model comprising a quantum dot coupled to an ultrasmall superconducting grain. The resulting low-energy description, formulated naturally in the canonical ensemble, captures even-odd effects, subgap excitations, and quantum-dot physics. The same framework gives access to observables not previously computed for such grain-dot systems in the canonical ensemble, such as the fixed-particle-number optical conductivity and flux-tunable spectra.

papers.title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Scaling depth is a key route to stronger large language models, but Pre-LN architectures often suffer from depth-wise information dilution, limiting the effective use of deep layers. While cross-layer connectivity has proven effective at mitigating this problem, existing designs usually introduce additional computation or memory access. We revisit cross-layer KV sharing as an efficient form of such connectivity. Beyond cache compression, each KV reuse edge creates a direct gradient path from deep layers to source KV projections, turning KV sharing into an implicit structural regularizer for KV representation geometry. We provide a systematic analysis of this mechanism, showing that proper sharing topologies sharpen key retrieval directions while enriching the value content subspace, whereas existing adjacent or global-anchor designs do not fully exploit this effect. Motivated by this, we propose DepthGraft, a hierarchical KV-sharing architecture that reconstructs deep-layer KV from stride-aligned shallow-middle source pairs. DepthGraft distributes non-local gradient flow across source layers, while preserving prefill early completion and reducing KV cache by roughly one third. Experiments on dense and MoE models from 0.5B to 16B parameters show consistent downstream improvements under both GQA and MLA. Notably, on the 16B MoE model, DepthGraft achieves a 7.0% absolute improvement on MMLU-Pro, along with gains of 6.6% on CMMLU and 6.4% on C3. These results validate the potential of DepthGraft as a scalable design for large-scale pretraining. The project page is available at https://github.com/jianke0604/DepthGraft.

papers.title: Visual-to-Executable Procedural Reconstruction of Buildings
papers.abstract: Procedural modeling offers compact, editable, and reusable representations for architectural content, but building such models still depends heavily on manually authored grammars. We study image-based procedural building reconstruction from in-the-wild images, with the goal of recovering an executable procedural description that can be instantiated as an editable 3D building asset. Because a single image provides only partial and view-dependent evidence, we focus on recovering the dominant visible facade(s) and attach the recovered facade program to a simple mass model for building-level instantiation. Our method decomposes this task into two structured prediction stages. First, a Global Structure Layout Tree recovers facade-scale split-and-repeat organization through a fine-tuned layout model with render-guided visual-symbolic reflection. Second, a Component Parameterization schema maps representative facade tiles to structured procedural attributes for local architectural component synthesis. These two representations are then deterministically compiled into executable Computer Generated Architecture (CGA) programs, avoiding the brittleness of direct low-level program generation. Experiments show that the proposed framework handles both regular facades and challenging in-the-wild images, while maintaining high structural consistency, procedural executability, and fine-grained architectural detail. The recovered programs further enable controllable and reusable 3D building asset generation.

papers.title: Writing with Near-Field: towards Atomic Resolution in Material Processing
papers.abstract: Direct laser writing with ultra-short pulses is the most flexible route to two- and three-dimensional (2D/3D) material modification, yet its resolution is judged against the optical diffraction limit. This review argues the opposite: the finest, most reproducible modifications come not from shortening the wavelength but from localising the absorber. Through the threshold effect and a transient epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) state - the dielectric-to-metal (Die-Met) state of the excited solid - the deposited energy is confined to a dipole-like nano-seed whose near-field intensity falls as r^-6 (ideal point dipole). The localisation is thus set by the seed size, not the focal wavelength, and the final feature is shaped by the material response: post-pulse heat flow, cavitation and quenching. We show that polarisation controls the anisotropy of deposition: the quasi-static near-field and interface boundary conditions select the writing direction and the modification orientation, down to a single defect. We survey energy-deposition mechanisms from 100 nm to the single-nanometer scale and link them to working engineering: stitch-free large-area patterning and record aspect-ratio (10^3-10^4) dicing and wafering of transparent crystals. Finally, we conjecture guided volumetric deposition, in which laser-inscribed lossy nano-seeds act as antennas that let cavity microwaves anneal the modified nano-volumes from within, as a 2.45 GHz oven heats food through water-dipole absorption. Throughout, atomic resolution is used in a quantum-confined sense and denotes a direction of travel: 10-20 nm features are demonstrated, while deterministic single-defect and single-bond modification remain goals. The thesis is that ultrafast direct write beats diffraction-limited intuition because the material itself forms a transient nanoscale absorber whose near-field and boundary conditions govern energy deposition.

papers.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree at least $750$ satisfies $χ(G)\le\max\{ω(G),Δ(G)-1\}$. The proof starts with a random partial colouring and completes it on large cliques using a list-colouring condition that remains valid as the rest of the graph is coloured. Disjoint stars provide the required colours. We estimate the number of stars that can be chosen after the clique colours have been exposed, while keeping their endpoint set fixed. A common exponential-moment argument reduces intervals of packing sizes to endpoint comparisons. More detailed neighbourhood estimates handle the remaining vertices. The final probability inequalities are verified by directed rational and interval arithmetic.

papers.title: Reed-Muller Codes are Optimal Binary Linear 3-Query LCCs
papers.abstract: We prove that any linear $3$-query locally correctable code $C \colon \mathbb{F}_2^k \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with constant correction radius must have length $n \geq 2^{Ω(\sqrt{k})}$. This improves on the prior best lower bound of $2^{Ω(\sqrt{k/\log k})}$, due to [AG24], and shows that the folklore construction of linear $3$-LCCs from Reed-Muller codes, which achieve length $n = 2^{O(\sqrt{k})}$, is optimal up to constant factors in the exponent. Our proof builds on the approach of [KM24a], further refined in [Yan24,KM24b], that uses "chain derived equations" in combination with Kikuchi graphs. The crux of our argument is to show that a certain edge-coloured Kikuchi graph has a unique colour cycle: a cycle in which some colour is used exactly once. We do this by controlling the distribution of colours at each vertex in the graph using a random walk mixing argument and a novel hypergraph decomposition based on edge expansion of the hypergraph's "flattening" into a graph.

papers.title: Controlling Sharpening in LLM Post-Training
papers.abstract: LLM post-training via reinforcement learning has shown consistent improvements in accuracy at the cost of reducing behavioral coverage - a phenomenon known as sharpening that can stall progress on difficult tasks. Repeated sampling objectives such as $\mathrm{pass@k}$ and $\mathrm{max@k}$ are known to mitigate sharpening, but the mechanism behind it remains poorly understood. Moreover, existing approaches for $\mathrm{@k}$ optimization use dedicated algorithms, and no general framework exists for adapting established policy optimization methods from $\mathrm{@}1$ to $\mathrm{@k}$. We derive the optimal policies for KL-regularized $\mathrm{pass@k}$ and $\mathrm{max@k}$ objectives in closed form. Our explicit solutions reveal that $\mathrm{@k}$ optimization naturally redistributes learning pressure based on prompt difficulty, directing it toward harder problems. Crucially, we show that standard $\mathrm{@}1$ objectives achieve these exact same optimal policies through prompt-adaptive regularization or reward transformation. Ultimately, this yields an optimizer-independent explanation for why $\mathrm{@k}$ objectives reduce sharpening on easy tasks while prioritizing success on harder ones. Building on these insights, we introduce $\mathrm{@k}$ Adaptive Pressure for Policy Optimization (KAPPO). Following a one-time reference calibration, KAPPO seamlessly adapts existing $\mathrm{@}1$ methods to $\mathrm{@k}$ via prompt-adaptive regularization or reward transformation, without otherwise altering their training procedures. Experiments with several RL methods on mathematical reasoning and code generation demonstrate that KAPPO provides direct control over sharpening. Crucially, we demonstrate that $\mathrm{@k}$ pressure can be fully realized with single completion training, matching the performance of multi-completion $\mathrm{@k}$ optimizers at a fraction of the cost.

papers.title: A combined segmented anode gas ionization chamber and time-of-flight detector for heavy ion elastic recoil detection analysis
papers.abstract: A dedicated detector system for heavy ion elastic recoil detection analysis at the Tandem Laboratory of Uppsala University is presented. Benefits of combining a time-of-flight measurement with a segmented anode gas ionization chamber are demonstrated. The capability of ion species identification is improved with the present system, compared to that obtained when using a single solid state silicon detector for the full ion energy signal. The system enables separation of light elements, up to Neon, based on atomic number while signals from heavy elements such as molybdenum and tungsten are separated based on mass, to a sample depth on the order of one micrometer. The performance of the system is discussed and a selection of material analysis applications is given. Plasma-facing materials from fusion experiments, in particular metal mirrors, are used as a main example for the discussion. Marker experiments using nitrogen-15 or oxygen-18 are specific cases for which the described improved species separation and sensitivity are required. Resilience to radiation damage and significantly improved energy resolution for heavy elements at low energies are additional benefits of the gas ionization chamber over a solid state detector based system.

papers.title: Correlated Catalysis Removes the Strong Converse for Entanglement Distillation
papers.abstract: Entanglement distillation converts noisy shared quantum states into maximally entangled pairs using local operations and classical communication. The distillable entanglement $E_D$ determines the maximum asymptotic rate at which this process can be performed reliably. For several classes of quantum states, distillation above this rate obeys a strong converse: the fidelity with the target state vanishes asymptotically. Here we show that correlated catalysis removes the strong converse for every distillable bipartite state. Specifically, at any target rate $R>E_D$, the optimal asymptotic fidelity is given by $E_D/R$. Thus, although catalysis does not increase the maximum reliable distillation rate, it allows nonvanishing fidelity at every finite rate. Remarkably, this advantage persists even when the catalyst is returned exactly at every finite blocklength and the correlations between the output and catalyst vanish asymptotically. We further characterize the catalyst size required to sustain nonvanishing fidelity above the reliable distillation rate.

papers.title: Electromagnetic Structure of $Ω_{ccc}^{++}$ and $Ω_{bbb}^{-}$ baryons from a covariant three-body Faddeev equation
papers.abstract: We investigate the electromagnetic structure of the ground-state $Ω_{ccc}^{++}$ and $Ω_{bbb}^{-}$ baryons using a Poincaré-covariant three-body Faddeev equation within the rainbow--ladder truncation. We calculate the complete set of elastic spin-$3/2$ multipole form factors, $G_{E0}$, $G_{M1}$, $G_{E2}$, and $G_{M3}$. The leading electric and magnetic form factors become markedly harder from the charm to the bottom sector, revealing the substantially more compact electromagnetic structure of the $Ω_{bbb}^{-}$. For $Ω_{ccc}^{++}$, the electric form factor and charge radius at low momentum transfer agree well with the available lQCD results. From the magnetic-dipole form factor at zero momentum transfer, $G_{M1}(0)$, we obtain the magnetic moments $μ_{Ω_{ccc}^{++}}=1.26\,μ_N$ and $μ_{Ω_{bbb}^{-}}=-0.207\,μ_N$. For $G_{E2}$ and $G_{M3}$, the electric-quadrupole structure exhibits a stronger charm-to-bottom evolution than the charge-normalized magnetic-octupole structure. Finally, comparison of the charm and bottom systems shows that both $G_{M1}(0)$ and the relation between the electric and magnetic radii move closer to their leading nonrelativistic heavy-quark expectations as the quark mass increases.

papers.title: FlowBatt: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Battery Degradation Prediction
papers.abstract: Battery degradation remains a central challenge in the development and broad application of sustainable energy technologies. Accurate degradation prediction is challenging, as battery aging emerges from complex and heterogeneous interactions among cycling behavior, operating conditions, and cell chemistry. Existing machine-learning approaches typically focus on deterministic end-of-life predictions or modeling degradation curves within fixed chemistry settings, leaving probabilistic state of health (SOH) trajectory modeling across heterogeneous chemistries underexplored. We introduce FlowBatt, a use-inspired conditional generative framework that adapts flow matching with a diffusion transformer (DiT) backbone to battery degradation trajectory modeling. FlowBatt models full SOH trajectories as probabilistic degradation processes conditioned on early-cycle capacity data. To strengthen this conditioning pathway, we use explainable AI analysis to diagnose and improve the encoder that maps early-cycle capacity matrices into conditioning vectors. We evaluate FlowBatt on five public benchmark settings spanning diverse chemistries and aging conditions, comparing it with supervised and diffusion-based trajectory models as well as established baselines for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction under shared data splits. FlowBatt achieves the best trajectory-wise SOH prediction performance on all five datasets, with errors below 2.5%, and delivers competitive RUL prediction performance. By generating multiple plausible trajectories, FlowBatt provides empirical prediction intervals for battery degradation modeling. These results indicate that flow-matching-based trajectory modeling is a promising framework for probabilistic battery health prediction.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Relaxed Multiplication in List Coloring
papers.abstract: Jiang and Zhu [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 137 (2019) 112--117] asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(km+1:m)$-choosable for every positive integer $m$. We answer this question negatively by constructing a graph with chromatic number and choice number $k$ that is not $(km+1:m)$-choosable for every $k\ge3$ and $m\ge10$. More generally, for integers $k\ge3$, $m\ge2$, and $t\ge0$, satisfying $m>8t+ε$, where $ε\in\{0,1\}$ is the parity of $m$, we construct such a graph that is not $(km+t:m)$-choosable. This also answers negatively the equivalent question of Xu and Zhu [SIAM J. Discrete Math., 36 (2022) 2585--2601] asking whether the strong fractional choice number of every graph is at most its choice number. This also indicates that, for each $k\ge3$, the supremum of the strong fractional choice numbers of graphs with choice number $k$ is at least $k+1/8$. When $t=0$, our construction yields counterexamples to multiplication for every $k\ge3$ and $m\ge2$. In particular, it yields a $3$-choosable graph on $91$ vertices that is not $(6:2)$-choosable, answering a question of Dvořák, Hu and Sereni [ Adv. Comb. (2019), Paper No. 5].

papers.title: From PID to Reinforcement Learning in Building HVAC Control: A Control-Architecture Review of Tuning Strategies, Formulations, and Deployment Trade-offs
papers.abstract: This paper reviews control architectures for building heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems, addressing the tension among energy demand, occupant comfort and equipment operability, and situating proportional-integral-derivative (PID) regulation within a layered control stack that also includes rule-based and model-based supervisory control and data-driven reinforcement learning (RL). It examines the thermostat-PID layer from two-position and scheduled setpoint control through proportional, PI and PID regulation and their tuning, then formulates RL for building control as a Markov decision process. Its central contribution is a taxonomy of where RL meets PID: RL as a gain tuner for an existing loop, as a direct replacement for the regulatory controller, as a hybrid with model predictive control, and as supervisory setpoint and schedule generation. Across these classes, the review establishes that the physical loop remains invariant while the intervention point changes, and that the classes differ in their requirements for actuation authority, state information, modelling, commissioning and constraint handling. It further establishes that PID is inexpensive and well codified but limited by nonlinearity, time variation, discrete mode switching, loop interaction and slow plant dynamics, while RL's admissible position must be argued rather than assumed. The paper concludes that these architectures are not competing philosophies of control but nested points of attachment on one HVAC plant, with hybrid implementations possible, and that deployment trade-offs must be assessed according to the specific control interface and scaffolding required.

papers.title: Any uniformly rectifiable set is contained in a set with Poincaré inequality
papers.abstract: We show that any uniformly $d$-rectifiable subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is contained in an Ahlfors $d$-regular set in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ which supports a $(1,1)$-Poincaré inequality. This provides a natural converse to a recent result of Azzam.

papers.title: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
papers.abstract: Machine learning supports materials design, atomistic simulation and experimental characterization, yet models and workflows remain fragmented. We present PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework integrating heterogeneous materials-learning tasks while preserving task-specific representations and scientific semantics. It unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management and workflows across six task classes: property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation and microscopy image processing. Task interfaces record physical quantities, units, aggregation conventions and references, making cross-task composition verifiable. A shared compiler backend enables switching from dynamic-graph to compiled execution through one setting, using graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-targeted code generation without changing model definitions. Across 65 model instances in 11 groups, compiled execution accelerated every instance in eight groups, with group median speedups of 11%-224% and group maximum speedups of 11%-336%. Case studies on LiMnO2 and toluene link structure generation or spectrum elucidation, interatomic-potential relaxation, property prediction and electron-density prediction, using same-geometry density functional theory (DFT) calculations as references. For LiMnO2, predicted formation energies for generated and relaxed structures differed from same-geometry PBE+U references by at most 7 meV per atom, while the computational cost of model steps was less than one-twentieth of a DFT single-point calculation. PaddleMaterials extends unified materials workflows beyond conventional property, potential and structure-generation tasks while supporting verifiable cross-task operations and compiled execution.

papers.title: Minimax regret and monotone optimality in multiple testing
papers.abstract: Confirmatory trials may seek efficacy claims in a prespecified subgroup and the full popu- lation, although benefit outside the subgroup is uncertain. We measure power loss relative to the marginal level-α test available if the population to protect were known, using the same experiment. In a bivariate Gaussian model with known covariance, we minimise the largest power loss, or regret, over prespecified ranges of target and non-target effects, subject to strong familywise error control and coordinatewise monotonicity. We optimise over monotone closed- testing procedures with fixed marginal tests, allowing randomisation in the shared intersection test. Monotonicity places the worst non-target mean at its lower planning bound for each target effect. On the resulting reduced planning set, every least-favourable distribution is supported on exactly two efficacy scenarios, one for each target population. Under a condition on the effect ranges and covariance, the minimax procedure is nonrandomised and unique up to null sets. An integral criterion characterises exactly when a calibrated step-up procedure attains the minimax value within this class. Bounds for the continuous problem quantify possible improve- ments over simple procedures. An asthma planning example illustrates power allocation and the compatibility of target assignments with treatment benefits and burdens.

papers.title: Dissecting Geometric Constraints in Grokking: Interaction-Dependent Acceleration in Modular Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Spherical transformer configurations can accelerate grokking through simultaneous modifications of several model properties. The present study investigated the contributions of these modifications in the published Sphere+Fourier configuration using 960 controlled modular-arithmetic runs. A complete factorial analysis varied residual projection, readout weight normalization, logit scale, and weight decay. Across four matched settings with weight decay, the successful-run mean crossing times without projection were 8-37 times those observed with projection. However, residual projection was insufficient to induce grokking without additional interventions. Various other unprojected configurations also generalized. Since projection altered the magnitude entering the readout, these comparisons could not separate geometry from output scale. A separate 100-run fixed-horizon study demonstrated faster first crossing for the complete configuration across five train/test partitions. Faster crossing did not necessarily correspond to greater persistence over extended training. Control experiments demonstrated rapid grokking without Fourier initialization. Task and depth sweeps also identified conditions in which the configuration failed to reach the criterion by 50K epochs. Accordingly, the observed acceleration depended on interactions among the components and did not extend uniformly across the tested tasks or depths.

papers.title: Toward Knowledge-Centric AI: Discovering, Internalizing, and Using Explicit Knowledge Across Agents and Generations
papers.abstract: Knowledge is how understanding accumulates across people and generations: durable records that outlive their producers and that others can check, combine, teach, and correct. AI agents are now built and run by many independent users and organizations, and each agent is upgraded, replaced, or retired within months. Yet what an agent learns stays trapped in model parameters, a transient context window, or a system-specific memory store that is appended to and retrieved from rather than processed. We argue that the next generation of AI should be knowledge-centric, built around an explicit, continuously evolving knowledge layer independent of any single agent. In this loop, agents discover knowledge from their environments and trajectories; the layer internalizes it by turning fragmented, heterogeneous records and experience into composable, revisable understanding; and agents across systems and generations use the result and return new outcomes for revision. While discovery and use have advanced rapidly with large language model agents, internalization remains the bottleneck. We argue that internalization should become a persistent object of training and maintenance-centered on condition-preserving conceptualization of events and deductive, inductive, and abductive reasoning across noisy, heterogeneous representations (text, tables, graphs, rules, and programs). To power this layer, we call for knowledge foundation models that provide shared neural capacity for knowledge computation, and outline a research agenda showing how an explicit knowledge layer delivers reuse, cost efficiency, auditability, and continuity across agent generations.

papers.title: Adaptive accuracy-driven splitting in Ozaki matrix multiplication and application to block LU factorization
papers.abstract: The Ozaki scheme for matrix multiplication computes an accurate matrix product by splitting the input matrices and evaluating a sequence of low-precision matrix products. Its accuracy and computational cost depend strongly on the number of splits. We develop accuracy-driven criteria for selecting this number in both Ozaki matrix multiplication and in block LU factorization using Ozaki trailing updates. For matrix multiplication, we derive normwise and componentwise criteria that determine how many split products are required to achieve a given accuracy requirement. For block LU, we present a fixed normwise strategy with essentially no selection cost, an LU-aware adaptive normwise strategy that can reduce the number of splits in subsequent trailing updates, and a componentwise strategy that uses information accumulated from preceding updates to guide the later selections. In the componentwise strategy, when the required number of splits exceeds a prescribed maximum, the corresponding update is instead carried out using ordinary matrix multiplication. We also provide rigorous backward error bounds for these approaches. Numerical experiments show that the adaptive normwise strategy can reduce the number of splits while preserving normwise accuracy, whereas the componentwise strategy can provide smaller componentwise backward errors when stronger local accuracy is needed.

papers.title: Taming a macroscopic free mass through continuous quantum measurement
papers.abstract: The free particle is the most elementary dynamical system in quantum mechanics. Despite remarkable progress in quantum control of increasingly massive solid-state mechanical oscillators, the analogous control of the free-particle counterpart has remained elusive. Dissipation and environmental noise have prevented such control in the inherently low-frequency domain of free-particle dynamics---a regime of growing importance for quantum sensing and tests of fundamental physics. Here we realize a suspended 1-milligram rotor operating in the free-particle regime with exceptional environmental isolation. Combining this isolation with a low-noise measurement architecture, we directly resolve thermal fluctuations in the motion associated with a damping rate of only 7~nHz. Through continuous quantum measurement of the rotor, we localize its otherwise unconfined motion, obtaining conditional states with entropic temperatures as low as 140~nK as a quantitative measure of control in the free-particle regime. This is two orders of magnitude below temperatures previously achieved in tabletop optomechanical experiments. We demonstrate immediate utilities of the new operating regime, setting new constraints on modifications of quantum mechanics and benchmarking inferred entanglement-to-decoherence rate ratios nearly two orders of magnitude beyond the state of the art for tests of gravity at the quantum-classical interface.

papers.title: Characterisation of surface layers formed on plasma-facing components in controlled fusion devices: Role of heavy ion elastic recoil detection
papers.abstract: Wall components retrieved from the TEXTOR tokamak after tracer experiments with nitrogen-15 and molybdenum hexafluoride (MoF6) injection were studied to determine deposition patterns and, by this, to conclude on material migration. Toroidal limiter tiles made of carbon fibre composites and fine grain graphite were examined using time-of-flight heavy ion elastic recoil detection analysis. Molybdenum deposition patterns indicated migration based on erosion and prompt re-deposition. Nitrogen-15 was trapped together with the deposited molybdenum. Some information on the depth distribution of species in the top 400 nm layer of the limiters was obtained; however surface roughness of the samples strongly limited resolution. In the case of molybdenum, the largest concentration was found in the 100 nm outermost layer, whereas fluorine and nitrogen-15 displayed more irregular profiles. Other species, besides deuterium fuel and carbon-12, were also identified: boron-10 and boron-11 originating from boronisations, carbon-13 from earlier tracer experiments, nitrogen-14 from plasma edge cooling and metals eroded from the Inconel wall.

papers.title: Searching the Plane in the Segment Visibility Model
papers.abstract: We study deterministic search by $n \geq 2$ unit-speed robots starting at the origin of the Euclidean plane. We introduce the concept of \emph{segment visibility} whereby a stationary target $x$ at distance $d=\|x\|>0$ is discovered at the first instant $t$ when $x$ belongs to the segment joining a pair of robots at time $t$. Discovery time is compared with the omniscient optimum $d$. We distinguish two knowledge models according to whether the robots know $d$ in advance. For $n=2$ robots, in the \emph{known-$d$} model, we give a symmetric four-phase algorithm and prove that its competitive ratio is optimal: $1+\sqrt3+π/6$; the matching lower bound follows from the known-distance two-robot shoreline-search theorem through an explicit reduction to segment detection. For $n=2$ robots, in the \emph{unknown-$d$} model, a three-circle construction and a quantitative initial-path estimate yield the stronger lower bound $\sqrt3+π/6+\sqrt{17}/4 \approx3.286425990$, giving an explicit positive cost for not knowing the radius; we also analyze a feasible antipodal-diameter logarithmic-spiral algorithm with optimized ratio $8.928516954\ldots$, thus proving that the competitive ratio when $d$ is unknown is at least $ \sqrt3+π/6+\sqrt{17}/4 $ and at most $8.928516954\ldots.$ For $n \geq 3$ robots, the competitive ratio of finding the target is exactly $\sec (π/n)$ regardless of whether or not $d$ is known to the robots.

papers.title: Beyond Surface Metrics: Multi-Condition Requirements in Enterprise Maintenance and AI Coding Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Repository-level AI coding benchmarks measure task success but do not directly capture the conditions required for software maintenance completion. We study multi-condition fulfillment, where a maintenance task must satisfy multiple operational conditions, sometimes with directional dependencies. Using a fixed 18-criterion taxonomy, we analyze 2,925 Apache Fineract issues and 944 tasks from SWE-bench Pro, SWE-PolyBench Java, and SWE-EVO. We examine condition breadth, corpus-level co-occurrence, and source-grounded directional requirement relationships. Among 1,177 benchmark task pairs matched on issue classification, modified-file count, and code churn, the mean fulfillment-set Jaccard distance is 0.8138, and 57.4% have disjoint condition sets. Condition count alone does not explain this contrast: SWE-bench Pro averages 2.47 conditions per task, versus 1.78 for Fineract. Temporal (B4) and numerical (B2) conditions have a phi coefficient of +0.430 in Fineract versus -0.013 in the pooled benchmark corpus. Among temporally tagged tasks, numerical conditions are also specified in 48.85% (254/520) of Fineract cases versus 5.81% (5/86) of benchmark cases. We document 16 directional relationships in Fineract requirements involving time, calculation, and state preservation, and inspect four benchmark cases to illustrate how relevant conditions appear in evaluation assertions. These examples do not quantify benchmark-wide oracle omissions. The results show that similar surface task profiles can mask substantially different fulfillment-condition sets. We recommend reporting condition breadth, co-occurrence, and directional relationships separately. The corpus comparisons are descriptive and may reflect domain differences; they do not establish causality or production failure rates.

papers.title: FineCraft: Enhancing VLA Models for Fine-Grained Manipulation
papers.abstract: Fine-grained manipulation couples instruction grounding, local visual precision, and sustained execution. We present FineCraft, a framework that adapts pretrained models for fine-grained manipulation in the MetaFine Challenge. A task-routed mixture of policies selects independently adapted DINOv2-DiT or pretrained $π_{0.5}$ policies through a common observation-action interface. Local visual features help identify the instructed object parts, demonstrations and expert continuations teach the required actions, and new observations guide replanning during execution. FineCraft ranks fourth with an overall score of $0.878$, exceeding the published reference on all five tasks. Official results and local diagnostics characterize performance across visual perturbations, instruction changes, and multi-stage manipulation. Code is available at https://github.com/eqcy/FineCraft

papers.title: Enforced Gaplessness by Combining Non-Anomalous Symmetries
papers.abstract: Symmetry-enforced gaplessness is a phenomenon in which a quantum system is forced to be gapless due to its global symmetry. Previous works have mainly focused on anomalous symmetries. Another approach, using symmetry spans, which specify two embeddings of a common symmetry into two larger symmetries, was proposed by the authors. In this work, we show that a symmetry span can enforce gaplessness even when both larger symmetries are invertible and non-anomalous: each alone admits a trivially gapped phase, but because the embeddings differ by a twist associated with a symmetry-protected topological phase, the symmetry they generate admits no gapped phase with finitely many ground states. We present such a span of a finite group and $\mathrm{U}(1)^2$ in 1+1 dimensions, with continuum realizations and a lattice Hamiltonian, with a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space and finitely many parameters, that is gapless in any region of its parameter space. We also discuss a 2+1-dimensional example and spans of only finite symmetries.

papers.title: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
papers.abstract: LaBraM, an early EEG foundation model, demonstrated that large-scale EEG pretraining can yield strong representations for diverse downstream tasks. Building on this foundation, we expand pretraining data and model capacity while retaining its core encoder and objective. We train ten encoders with 5.8 million to 1.97 billion parameters on three EEG collections spanning 25,067 to 79,910 hours, adapting signal preparation and training to heterogeneous recordings. Across 23 tasks, Atom-L* reaches 59.05% mean balanced accuracy at its best evaluated full fine-tuning (Full-FT) checkpoint, 3.61 percentage points above the strongest baseline EEG foundation model. Quark-G leads linear probing (LP) at 54.33%, a 1.24-point margin. Both also lead average task rank. At the last evaluated checkpoints, larger encoders improve Full-FT more consistently than LP, and stronger LP does not guarantee stronger Full-FT. Preserving patch structure improves LP over average pooling. Data-fraction experiments suggest capacity-dependent saturation, while checkpoint trajectories show that downstream performance can decline as pretraining loss falls. Joint classification with a shared Qwen3 readout reaches 50.50% with Molecule-H and Qwen3-8B; increasing language-model size provides no consistent gain. These results demonstrate the value of scaling LaBraM and the importance of matching pretraining scale to downstream adaptation.

papers.title: Causal discovery needs explicit epistemic standards
papers.abstract: There are many causal discovery algorithms, but few guiding principles for choosing between them. Methods are usually compared through three lenses: identifiability, consistency, and benchmarks. Each introduces assumptions about the data-generating process that are often untestable. We argue that there are no shared standards for comparing, prioritizing, or even discussing those assumptions. We support this claim by showing that (i) identifiability assumptions are often preferred by convention rather than by principle, (ii) uniform consistency requires further untestable assumptions, while the weaker pointwise consistency has arguably narrowed algorithm design, and (iii) benchmarks are not neutral tests but carry an epistemic role of their own: they quietly fix which regimes matter, which guarantees come into play, and what counts as success. In doing so, they shape what algorithm comparisons are taken to show and thus perform some of the same epistemic work as theory, but less transparently. In this position paper we argue for a more transparent, integrated practice: Make the epistemic standards for discussing identifiability and consistency assumptions explicit, especially their failure modes and scope conditions; design benchmarks to operationalize those standards, by stress-testing and ablating both. Then, theoretical and empirical results jointly clarify when, why, and how algorithms may work rather than accumulate as disconnected advances.

papers.title: Causal Mediation Analysis with High-Dimensional Surrogates: Identification, Estimation and Inference under Latent Factor Models
papers.abstract: Causal mediation analysis is an important tool for understanding how a treatment affects an outcome through intermediate variables referred to as mediators. However, in many applications, these mediators and pre-treatment covariates are not directly observed and are instead measured through noisy, high-dimensional surrogates. Mediation analysis when such latent variables are observed only through these surrogates remains less explored. In this paper, we propose Factor-Adjusted Regression for Mediation Analysis (FARMA), a factor-based framework for estimating direct and indirect effects when either one or both of the mediators and relevant pre-treatment covariates are latent. FARMA uses the surrogate measurements to recover information about the underlying latent variables. Under a latent factor structure, we show that the direct and indirect effects are approximately identified, with an approximation error that vanishes as the surrogate dimensions grow. We further show that our estimator is $\sqrt{n}$-consistent and asymptotically normal. We combine the theory with extensive simulation studies and apply it to data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) study, where we investigate whether the effect of depressive symptoms on cognitive impairment is mediated through the latent process underlying high-dimensional DNA methylation measurements.

papers.title: Rollout then Recycle: 3,718 Labelled Real-Robot Episodes from Benchmarking 7 Policies on 12 Tasks
papers.abstract: We release all 3,718 episodes from the ArmnetBench v0.1 evaluation (arXiv:2607.24481), which contains 600 teleoperated demonstrations and 3,118 rollouts of seven imitation-learning and vision-language-action policies on 12 tabletop tasks, recorded on low-cost SO-101 arms; 73% of the rollouts are failures. Every policy for a task was trained or fine-tuned on the same 50 demonstrations and rolled out on the same cell, so the corpus contains many policies' failures on shared tasks. An operator labelled every rollout successful, suboptimal or failure. Each episode has three camera views, joint states and actions and is available on the Hugging Face Hub in LeRobot v3.0 and a reward-model format. This note documents how the episodes were collected and the limitations that could affect their use.

papers.title: An Erdős-Pach-Pollack-Tuza theorem for oriented diameter
papers.abstract: The oriented diameter of a bridgeless graph is the minimum diameter of its strong orientations. Erdős, Pach, Pollack and Tuza proved that every connected graph of order $n$ and minimum degree $δ\ge 2$ has diameter at most $3n/(δ+1)-1$, which is sharp up to an additive constant. Cochran and Wang conjectured that the oriented diameter obeys the same bound up to an absolute additive constant. We prove this conjecture: every bridgeless graph of order $n$ and minimum degree $δ$ has a strong orientation of diameter at most $3n/(δ+1)+10^{17}$. Thus the bound of Erdős, Pach, Pollack and Tuza for the diameter carries over to the oriented diameter, with only the additive constant changed; in particular, the coefficient $3$ is best possible.

papers.title: Relativistic Kohn--Sham Theory of Paramagnetic Magnetic-Resonance Properties
papers.abstract: A general density functional theory based relativistic theory for paramagnetic NMR (pNMR) shifts, EPR g-tensors and hyperfine coupling tensors as well as magnetizabilities is derived. The formulation uses spin--orbit exact two-component (X2C) theory, gauge-including atomic orbitals, and generalized complex Kohn--Sham response equations with all ingredients being implemented analytically with the help of Goldstone modes and an orientation-constrained shielding. Additionally, we describe a two-component augmented Roothaan--Hall (ARH) solver for robust and stable convergence, which ensures that both a stationary point and a minimum are found. This is crucial for the convergence of the response equations for properties of paramagnetic systems. The extension of common population analyses for the two-component theory to aid in the interpretation of the spectra is further described. Using these new techniques, we are able to analyze the success and failure of density functional theory for relativistic open-shell systems including actinide complexes.

papers.title: ViAdminShift: A Vietnamese Benchmark for Event-Level Knowledge Updates Built from the 2025 Administrative Reform
papers.abstract: On July 1, 2025, Vietnam reduced its 63 provinces to 34, abolished its 696 districts, and replaced its 10,035 commune-level units (wards) with 3,321. ViAdminShift, a Vietnamese language resource about this event, consists of 7,995 benchmark items, 2,281 retrieval passages from pre- and post-reform Wikipedia revisions and dated templates, and old-to-new tables that a released script rebuilds from the official conversion table (not redistributed). Changed items store the pre-reform answer (except 121 address items), a $2\times2$ design uses untouched units as controls, and 400 addresses appear without diacritics. The tables agree with an independent lineage on 10,564 of 10,565 official pairs, disagreements were settled against the resolutions, and the probing-track scorer agrees with both authors' blind labels (Cohen's $κ=0.91$ and $0.89$). Data, outputs, code, and a datasheet are released. In the probing track, at least 20 of 67 models know the reform. Fourteen of them give the new province alone for at most 11% of plain questions about old addresses (old province only: 14-100%); a bare date recovers up to 100%. Post hoc (80 province-free addresses, single runs), with reasoning off, today's date in the system prompt leaves 68-100% old-province-only answers for 10 of 12 models; with reasoning, an "as of" prefix in the question leaves none for seven of eight. On the 1,262-item benchmark subset, with same-source old and new passages, small models unaware of the reform give 14-30% outdated answers and the five benchmark-track knowers (also differing in size or provider) 0-5%.

papers.title: Statistical Modeling of Foreground Galactic Cirrus for Diffuse Halo Light Measurement
papers.abstract: Galactic cirrus, the diffuse Milky Way starlight scattered by interstellar dust, has become a major source of systematic uncertainty in measurements of extragalactic diffuse emission at ultra-low surface brightness levels. Proper modeling and correction of this foreground is crucial to unlock the full potential of next-generation deep imaging surveys for studies of faint diffuse emission such as galactic stellar halos, ultra-diffuse galaxies, and intracluster light (ICL). We develop a statistical approach to reconstruct the 2D distribution of the Galactic cirrus while preserving the underlying diffuse extragalactic emission from stellar halos. We combine the broad dust morphology traced by far-infrared emission with multiscale structural information extracted from the optical images. The method synthesizes plausible cirrus structures through iteratively refining the foreground, the smooth diffuse light model, and the residual sky. The performance is assessed through injection--recovery experiments using Euclid VIS observations of the Abell 2390 cluster, which show substantial improvements in recovered stellar halo photometry, although residual biases depend on the local foreground structure and sky estimation. We apply the method to the central Abell 2390 field to correct for a prominent cirrus complex near its brightest cluster galaxy (BCG), revealing a smoother BCG+ICL distribution with a steeper outer light profile and reduced contamination in the integrated light. Our results demonstrate the potential of statistical modeling of Galactic cirrus to improve diffuse light photometry in deep wide-field imaging surveys.

papers.title: PagedMoE: Cross-Precision Expert Caching for Token-Level Dynamic Precision in SSD-Resident MoE Inference
papers.abstract: Large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are promising for local inference because sparse routing allows the routed-expert pool to reside on SSD while DRAM caches recently used experts. However, under practical DRAM cache capacities, substantial SSD I/O remains on the critical path despite I/O-computation overlap. Token-level dynamic expert precision offers a natural way to reduce this data demand by allocating bits according to expert importance and quantization sensitivity. Nevertheless, treating each bit-width of the same expert as an independent object prevents cross-precision cache reuse, causing overlapping data to be fetched repeatedly. The key insight is that precision should instead denote the refinement depth of one shared expert state. Based on this insight, we present PagedMoE, which stores each expert once using a prefix-compatible tree codebook and bitplane layout. Lower-precision representations are valid prefixes of higher-precision ones, allowing cached data to be reused or extended by fetching only missing bitplanes. PagedMoE selects the required prefix length before I/O using current routing weights and offline expert-specific error profiles, and directly executes cached 1-8-bit prefixes without materializing full-precision experts. At an average routed-expert precision of 2.5 bits, PagedMoE achieves quality close to GPTQ-INT4 on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B and to MXFP4 on most evaluated GLM5.2 tasks. With a 24 GiB expert cache, it reaches 8.89 tokens/s on Qwen3.5, 1.33x the throughput of the same dynamic requests using independent precision objects and 1.56x that of uniform 4-bit execution.

papers.title: Final coalgebras over R-modules
papers.abstract: Final coalgebras and the coinduction principle for coalgebras over $R$-modules, where $R$ is a commutative ring, are essential in determining the denotational behaviour of various types of linear weighted automata. The goal of this paper is to provide lower and upper bounds on the ordinals that are needed to construct final coalgebras over $R$-modules as the limit of a transfinite sequence of functor iterations. We give an example of a binary intersection preserving finitary functor on the category of abelian groups, which is the category of modules over integers, that fails to converge in $ω\cdot 2$ steps, thus settling an open problem of Adámek, Milius, and Moss. Then we relate this to the failure of the Artinian property of the integers and show that all finitary functors on $R$-modules for a Noetherian ring $R$ with Krull dimension $n$, which preserve countable directed intersections and a generalised notion of monomorphism, converge in $ω\cdot (n + 2)$ steps. We also establish how the connection between Aczel-Mendler bisimulation and behavioural equivalence is mediated by the functor $\operatorname{Ext}^1$. These results show that homological algebra tools can play an important role in coalgebra.

papers.title: Constructing free subgroups of matrix groups
papers.abstract: The Tits alternative asserts that a finitely generated linear group is either solvable-by-finite or contains a non-abelian free subgroup. Given a non-solvable-by-finite subgroup G of GL(d, F), where F is the field of complex numbers or a non-archimedean local field, we present methods to construct explicitly a non-abelian 2-generator free subgroup of G in specific cases. Our implementations in the computeralgebra system Oscar are publicly available.

papers.title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
papers.abstract: Determining the representative volume element is essential for establishing statistically meaningful microstructure-property relationships. Conventional approaches rely on the convergence of selected geometric descriptors, which may yield different estimates of the representative volume. Here, we propose a topology-based framework for assessing the representative scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed using plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (121.8 um x 83.97 um x 45.99 um). Persistent homology was used to characterize the pore network, and normalized persistence images of subvolumes were compared with those of the largest available reference volume using the L1 distance. This provides a continuous measure of topological similarity across observation scales, rather than defining representativeness through a single convergence threshold. The topological distance decreases with increasing volume and is described by empirical exponential models over the investigated range (R2 in [0.972, 0.983]). Comparison with porosity and specific surface area highlights differences in the scale-dependent behavior of geometric and topological descriptors. The framework was also tested on three independent synthetic realizations, demonstrating its potential for quantitative assessment of topological similarity in porous microstructures.

papers.title: Functional Logic Programming: Improving Logic Programs with Ease
papers.abstract: Logic programming is based on defining relations. Functions are often considered as syntactic sugar which can be transformed into predicates so that their logic is not used for computational purposes. In this paper, we show that the use of functions improves the operational behavior of logic programs without loosing the flexibility of logic programming. For this purpose, we present a systematic transformation from predicates and goals into functions and nested expressions, respectively. By evaluating functions in a demand-driven manner and taking potential failures into account, it is ensured that the execution of the transformed programs will never require more steps than the original programs but can decrease the number of steps---in the best case reducing infinite search spaces to finite ones. Thus, functional logic programming provides an adequate basis to improve the operational behavior of logic programs without changing their semantics. This also shows that, from an operational point of view, functional logic programming has clear advantages compared to relation-based logic programming.

papers.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in cowork agents are shifting human-AI collaboration toward real-world automation, delivering software, designs, and other artifacts. However, such productivity work demands both high-quality delivery on complex productivity tasks and continued monitoring and decision-making over long horizons, a combination that remains an open challenge. We introduce CoworkOS, a general-purpose harness for long-horizon work that separates task strategy from execution management: the model decides actions, delegation, and acceptance, while the runtime maintains state and feedback. Its three-layer architecture enables direct execution or delegation to Subagents, synchronously or asynchronously, under stable responsibilities.
