These results motivate a simple post-model layer: subtract a penalty for loading on the recent common return mode before forming the portfolio. In a frozen panel of ten liquid cross-asset ETFs, 760 completed weeks from January 2012 through July 2026, and exact self-financing costs of 10 basis points per dollar traded, this layer changes maximum drawdown from 23.6% to 14.1%, volatility from 12.6% to 10.7%, and excess-return Sharpe from 0.664 to 0.667. A volatility-matched momentum diagnostic still draws down 19.9%. Paired stationary-bootstrap uncertainty is wide: the 95% interval for drawdown improvement is $[-3.3,18.4]$ percentage points and includes zero. The result establishes a reproducible risk-control association and specifies the holdings-and-flow validation needed to attribute the common direction to AI crowding. AI-use disclosure. Generative AI tools, including OpenAI Codex, assisted manuscript preparation. For this preprint version, Codex assisted with LaTeX editing, author and venue metadata, compilation, and layout checks.

papers.title: Online Class Posteriors for Interpretable and Controllable Discrete Diffusion
papers.abstract: Discrete diffusion models remain far less understood than their continuous counterparts, despite recent breakthroughs across modalities, most notably in text. Leveraging tools from continuous diffusion, we formulate a theoretical framework to track the class-conditional posterior in an online manner by combining conditional and unconditional model predictions. In masked language modeling, this posterior offers highly interpretable dynamics: tokens aligned with a class boost the posterior, while contradictory ones suppress it. We also show that the posterior can be used for logical guidance operations (AND, OR, NOT) in discrete diffusion. These operations enable precise control over generation, such as avoiding specific classes. In addition, we discuss a mismatch in the formulation of classifier-free guidance between discrete and continuous settings: discrete models mix the data distributions, while continuous models mix the marginals. We validate our methods and discuss their potential applications on synthetic data, with all quantities analytically tractable, as well as on MNIST, text, and antibody sequences.

papers.title: Bg-Mix: On Using Image Backgrounds for Data Augmentation in Electron Microscopy Images
papers.abstract: Electron microscopy (EM) serves as a cornerstone in virology enabling the visualization of viral particles and is widely used in research, diagnostics and morphological characterization of pathogens. Computer-assisted image analysis can help facilitate and speed up this labor-intensive method, however, typical EM virus datasets are small and sparsely labeled, resulting in a lack of readily available deep learning models due to training limitations. To overcome data shortages and leverage content-rich, diverse sample backgrounds, we employed background-based data augmentation. To this end, we propose Bg-Mix, a form of data augmentation method, which decomposes training images into foreground objects and backgrounds and subsequently rearranges both into novel augmented images. This not only enhances the performance of object detection models but also increases the diversity of the training data. Using Bg-Mix provides an increase between +0.8 and +3.3 box mean average precision (mAP) points over the baseline when tested across two datasets using two architectures, thereby demonstrating its effectiveness.

papers.title: Radial Symmetry and Nondegeneracy for Singular Liouville Systems with Small Singular Exponents
papers.abstract: We extend the classification (Lin and Zhang, Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Anal. Non Linéaire \textbf{27}, 2010) to finite-mass singular Liouville systems with sufficiently small positive singular exponents. For symmetric, entrywise nonnegative, irreducible and invertible coupling matrices, every solution whose mass vector lies near a fixed compact subset of the regular mass surface is radial about the singular point and is uniquely determined by its component masses up to dilation. We also establish nondegeneracy modulo dilation. To overcome the failure of the moving-plane argument for positive exponents, we use compactness and a local reduction based on integral identities. The results also hold for nonzero nonnegative exponent vectors and for small mixed-sign vectors satisfying an explicit integral inequality.

papers.title: Expander Routing under Adversarial Deletions via Temporal Aggregation
papers.abstract: In expander routing, we seek to establish paths in the expander graph between given source-target pairs while minimizing both dilation (maximum path length) and congestion (maximum edge load). We study this problem in a decremental dynamic setting where the underlying graph remains an expander despite ongoing edge deletions, and source-target pairs can be added or removed. Our goal is to maintain paths under these updates while keeping dilation and congestion low and performing low computation per update. We present a randomized algorithm that maintains paths with polylogarithmic dilation and congestion against an adaptive adversary, while incurring only polylogarithmic amortized computation per update, all with high probability. Our approach leverages a recent technique called Temporal Aggregation to maintain a collection of low-congestion, low-dilation random walks resilient to adaptive adversaries.

papers.title: Lattice Green's functions for Poisson problems with two unbounded and one periodic direction
papers.abstract: Fourier-based Poisson solvers treat periodic directions spectrally and unbounded ones by the Hockney--Eastwood convolution with a free-space kernel. With two unbounded and one periodic direction, the setting of vortex tubes, wakes and jets, the kernel used so far by these solvers combines the two-dimensional kernel on the zero periodic mode with the symbol of the operator sampled on the doubled grid on every other mode. We show that the second ingredient is not exact: the error is the field of the periodic images of the source and independent of the mesh size. While the period $L_z$ is not much longer than the unbounded extent $L_x$, it is of order $\exp(-2πd/L_z)$, with $d$ the distance to the nearest image; beyond, it grows like $(L_z/L_x)^2$. The error is thus small on cubic domains, but larger than the solution itself on elongated ones. We remove the approximation by extending the integral representation of the exact second-order kernel of Hou and Colonius: the screened kernel of each mode is evaluated in closed form along one unbounded direction and by Gauss--Legendre quadrature along the other, for the high-order dimension-split and Mehrstellen stencils, at a one-off cost of about one solve. The kernels, implemented in the open-source library \flups{}, are verified by comparison with independent quadratures, by a padding test sensitive to the boundary condition enforced, and by convergence at the order of each stencil on an axially modulated tube source, on domains up to $64$ times longer than wide and up to $2.7\times10^{11}$ unknowns.

papers.title: Aberration stabilized light bullets in normal dispersion injected Kerr resonators
papers.abstract: We investigate three-dimensional light bullets (LBs) in an optically injected, vertically emitting Kerr-Gires-Tournois interferometer operating in the normal dispersion regime. In the uniform field limit, the dynamics is governed by a generalized Lugiato-Lefever equation with third-order dispersion, paraxial diffraction, and fourth-order diffraction, stemming from lens and mirror aberrations close to the self-imaging condition. Using direct numerical simulations, we show that without aberration only transversely drifting, tilted multi-peak localized states (LSs) are stable in two dimensions, whereas no stable LBs exist in three dimensions. However, a small negative spherical aberration stabilizes a rich multistable family of two-dimensional LSs, including straight and tilted multi-peak LSs, oscillating states, and complex bound states, which persist even for negative paraxial diffraction. We identify an Andronov-Hopf bifurcation followed by a homoclinic transition toward tilted states, accompanied by hysteresis. Finally, we demonstrate that stable straight and tilted LBs exist in three dimensions in the presence of aberration, the latter forming a continuous family parametrized by the transverse tilt direction.

papers.title: Surface charges and quantum reflection of hydrogen-isotope beams at grazing incidence
papers.abstract: Experiments with cryogenic beams of hydrogen isotopes (hydrogen (H), deuterium (D), and tritium (T)) can be used to study quantum reflection from solid dielectric mirrors. Most dielectric surfaces carry trapped electric charges whose field polarizes the incident atom. We study theoretically how such charges, distributed randomly, in clusters, with compensation over a finite length, or in order, change specular reflection and diffuse scattering of H, D, and T at grazing incidence on typical dielectric mirrors (SiO$_2$/Si and MgF$_2$), for longitudinal velocities of 100--300~m/s and normal velocities of 3--100~cm/s which might become available soon in grazing incidence experiments. Starting from the exact coupled-channel equations, we show that the specular wave feels only the laterally averaged polarization potential, which is fixed by the structure factor of the charges and, for uncorrelated charges, is an inverse-square tail $-C_2/z^2$. The exact solution replaces the linear threshold law $1-\Rr\propto\vperp$ by the fractional power $\vperp^{2ν}$, $ν=(1/4-ζ)^{1/2}$, with the coupling $ζ\propto C_2$; for weak coupling, this appears as a logarithmic velocity dependence, and for $ζ>1/4$, the reflection coefficient oscillates log-periodically. At the surface charge density of $10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$, absorption increases by up to 26\% for SiO$_2$/Si and by a factor of two to three for MgF$_2$; the effect increases with atomic mass, saturates for compensated charges, and is accompanied by diffuse scattering below $10^{-3}$ of charge-induced loss. We also formulate the condition of complete absorption at the solid surface.

papers.title: Unrolled gradients in disguise: bridging interpolation-based and Jacobian regularization for stable neural dynamics
papers.abstract: Hybrid models and neural differential equations (NDEs) are becoming increasingly important for modelling physical systems; however, they often encounter stability and accuracy issues during long-term integration. Training on unrolled trajectories is known to limit these divergences but quickly becomes too computationally expensive due to the need to compute gradients over an iterative process, making this method impractical for large-scale physical systems (e.g. weather and climate forecasting). Two popular paradigms for improving the stability of learned dynamics are to train on interpolated or noisy samples or to regularize the Jacobian of the learned representation. In this work, we demonstrate that these paradigms can be understood under a common lens and that they both correspond to an approximation of the gradients obtained in an unrolled learning strategy. Building on this understanding, we derive a principled and complete approach to regularize training and demonstrate its impact on the stability of learned dynamical systems.

papers.title: Fast nonparametric estimation of sparse precision matrices with a priori sparsity structure
papers.abstract: This work describes a computational approach for rapidly estimating and characterizing the covariance structure of a Gaussian random field from a modest number of i.i.d. replicates by formulating the problem in terms of a sparse inverse Cholesky factor of the data's covariance matrix. Borrowing from the extensive literature of using directed acyclic graphs to impose sparsity on inverse Cholesky factors (for example, Vecchia's approximation or nearest-neighbor Gaussian process models), a probabilistically parsimonious a priori sparsity pattern is imposed, and with careful formulation the estimation problem is given as an extremely well-structured convex problem that can be solved for millions of unknowns in seconds on a single processor core. After describing the problem and specific formulation of the optimization, we demonstrate the estimator's speed and effectiveness at capturing a variety of nonstationary structures in spatial or spatio-temporal data, and in ensemble data assimilation.

papers.title: Symbol-based residual certification of reduced and neural surrogates for tempered-fractional CGMY pricing
papers.abstract: We certify reduced and neural approximations of European-put price trajectories under the Carr--Geman--Madan--Yor model by residual bounds for the spline Galerkin discretisation of the tempered-fractional pricing equation. The Galerkin matrices are Toeplitz sections of an explicit periodised Fourier symbol; summing the alias series to a stated tail makes the assembled system exact to $10^{-8}$. A Lévy--Khintchine argument gives the parameter-explicit bound $λ_{\min}(S_I)\ge r\,m_{\min}$ for the symmetric part, valid for $Y\in(0,2)\setminus\{1\}$, replacing numerical spectral estimates. A banded comparison norm built from the mass and stiffness symbols yields a rigorous certificate at $O(N)$ cost with explicit effectivity, and empirical interpolation of the symbol makes the operator affine in about 36 terms with a rigorous error transfer, so a reduced model is certified at a cost independent of $N$; a three-stage rule escalates to the full-order bounds only when needed. At the resolution that prices the whole parameter box to one cent ($N=1024$), the full-order certificate costs 6% of a direct solve, and the certified POD--Galerkin model of rank 80 costs 3% of it and settles 99.8% of $10^4$ queries without touching the full space. No false accept occurs on any query with a reference solution (150 inside the parameter box, 264 outside), and outside the box the certificate accepts 193 of the 210 queries on which the reduced model is still within one cent. The neural reduced models trained here miss the one-cent tolerance by a factor of at least 46; the certificate detects this at every query in a few milliseconds and explains it as a trade-off between temporal smoothness and coefficient accuracy. A residual certificate for the American put is proved as an outlook.

papers.title: Spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities
papers.abstract: We give a formula for the spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities. This is a revised version of a conjecture proposed by Steenbrink fifty years ago. Although this conjecture fails in the non-simplicial Newton polytope case, we can find the correction term using the intersection complexes and the primitive intersection cohomologies of toric varieties associated with non-simplicial compact faces. To verify the correctness of the formula, we provide a sample code for Singular which computes the spectral pairs and compares the output with that of sppairs in Singular for the three variable case.

papers.title: HIVE-Diff: High Frame Rate HDR Video Reconstruction from a Single LDR Frame and Events
papers.abstract: High frame rate HDR video is important in applications such as autonomous driving and scientific imaging, where rapid motion and extreme illumination often occur simultaneously. Conventional frame cameras face a trade-off between temporal resolution and dynamic range, while event cameras provide complementary high-speed brightness-change measurements over a wide illumination range. These properties have motivated event-based HDR reconstruction, with existing methods broadly following event-only and hybrid event-frame paradigms. Event-only HDR reconstruction, however, suffers from brightness and color drift due to the lack of absolute intensity references. Hybrid event-frame methods alleviate this ambiguity using low-dynamic-range (LDR) frames as anchors, but most perform one-to-one HDR reconstruction at available LDR timestamps. In this work, we investigate single-reference HDR temporal expansion, reconstructing N HDR frames from one LDR reference and events instead of N aligned LDR observations. We develop HIVE-Diff, an event-conditioned video diffusion framework that decomposes the task into event-guided temporal generation and HDR content completion. Because paired real HDR-event data are scarce, we train on synthetic data and adapt the model to real event domains using LDR-event sequences as proxy supervision with teacher-student distillation. Experiments on synthetic and multiple real-world datasets demonstrate strong reconstruction quality and robust real-data adaptation.

papers.title: A Bayesian Framework for Safe Optimal Control of Unknown Systems from Input-Output Data
papers.abstract: As control engineering is applied to increasingly complex systems, learning-based control, which uses empirical data to reduce the reliance on first-principles models, has emerged as a promising paradigm. However, such approaches must cope with nonlinear and stochastic dynamics, the absence of state measurements, and scarce data, while ensuring safe operation under constraints, which requires rigorous uncertainty quantification. Whereas existing methods treat these challenges in isolation, this article proposes a Bayesian framework that jointly addresses them. A prior in state-space form is updated from input-output data using particle Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, yielding a representation of joint uncertainty over dynamics and latent states. Building on this representation, a validation procedure is developed that provides probabilistic guarantees for constraint satisfaction under arbitrary causal control laws. For control synthesis, a formulation penalizing the conditional value-at-risk of the constraint function is proposed, together with an adaptive calibration mechanism that adjusts the performance-robustness trade-off to achieve a desired robustness level. The probability of successful certification is characterized theoretically. The framework is extended to a receding-horizon setting, where posterior updates from new measurements allow the controller to progressively reduce uncertainty and improve performance. The approach is demonstrated on the optimal control of a vertical farm.

papers.title: Fractional $θ$-dependence from the sum over all instanton sectors
papers.abstract: An instanton carries integer topological charge, seemingly at odds with the multibranched $θ$ dependence of the Yang-Mills vacuum. We show that summing over all instanton sectors resolves this mismatch in self-dual supersymmetric $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$ and $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Yang-Mills theories with a chiral mass, in two and four dimensions. The path integral reduces to a sum of instanton moduli-space volumes, yielding the multibranched vacuum structure. In four dimensions, this extends Nekrasov's instanton counting for Seiberg-Witten theory to a QCD-like theory without scalars.

papers.title: The Optimizer's Windfall: Bounding Hindsight Gain under Random Restrictions
papers.abstract: Suppose an optimization problem is randomly restricted, independently on each variable, and re-optimized after the restriction is revealed. For multilinear objectives, every fixed solution is unbiased after rescaling, but re-optimizing introduces an upward bias. We bound this excess, the hindsight gain, over products of arbitrary compact local domains in Euclidean unit balls. For interactions $A=(A_e)_e$ among $r$ distinct variables and independent random weights $ζ_i$, the gain is at most $O_r(\|A\|_F M^{(r-1)/2}σ_{\max})$, where $\|A\|_F^2$ is the sum of squared coefficients, $M=\sum_i\mathbb{E}ζ_i^2$, and $σ_{\max}^2=\max_i\mathrm{Var}(ζ_i)$; only second moments are needed. Under uniform retention with probability $p$, we sharpen this to $O_r(p^{r-1/2}\sqrt{1-p}\,n^{(r-1)/2}\|A\|_F)$, which is tight for every fixed $r$ and $p\in(0,1)$. Our proof combines a comparison principle along a single support direction with tensor projection, vector contraction, and repeated thinning. Applications: (i) For fixed arity and alphabet size, solving the subproblem induced by $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ sampled variables estimates a dense Max-$r$CSP optimum within $\pm\varepsilon n^r$, and this sample size is optimal. (ii) The same approach estimates MaxCut and the distance to bipartiteness within $\pm\varepsilon n^2$ using $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ nonadaptive queries and $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ examined vertices, both optimal. (iii) We answer a question of Yufei Zhao: vertex percolation at rate $p$ preserves the max-cut fraction whenever $p\,e(G)/v(G)\to\infty$, and this condition is sharp. (iv) For bounded $r$-local quantum Hamiltonians of fixed local dimension, $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ uniformly sampled particles suffice to estimate the ground-state energy within $\pm\varepsilon n^r$, improving the previous $O(\varepsilon^{-6}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bound.

papers.title: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: Continuous blind stabilizer measurements turn stabilizer codes into a Liouvillian spectral problem in which Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. We show that this competition generically enables Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is constrained by the code distance. Exceptional points are detrimental in this regime of error correction as they maximize the decay rate of encoded coherences. We then optimize the encoding of the logical qubit using the eigenmodes of the Lindblad operator. This phase-optimized encoding cancels the linear short-time decay of logical qubit coherences. We apply this encoding to the [[5,1,3]] code and demonstrate that it outperforms naive encoding methods near the exceptional point, improves the fidelity of a logical $π$ rotation and remains effective in the presence of additional weak error channels.

papers.title: Zeta functions of quasi-split reductive algebraic groups over local fields
papers.abstract: We calculate zeta functions of quasi-split reductive algebraic groups over local fields using the classification of Tits and prove a functional equation. We give explicit exam- ples of these zeta functions for non-split unitary and orthogonal groups.

papers.title: An Active Flux Method for Maxwell's equations
papers.abstract: We present a novel Active Flux method and a divergence-free method using exact evolution operators for solving Maxwell's equations in three space dimensions on Cartesian grids. The proposed methods are fully discrete, third-order accurate and rely on a truly multidimensional evolution operator based on Kirchhoff's formula for the electromagnetic wave equation. The first method is a classical Active Flux method with globally continuous reconstruction while the second method is an adaptation of the Active Flux method to a locally divergence-free reconstruction by Balsara. The applied reconstruction is built from facial degrees of freedom and is no longer globally continuous. The classical method keeps the divergence error bounded. The divergence-free method with face averages initialized by a potential keeps the constraints at round-off. We compare the accuracy of both methods for smooth and discontinuous test problems.

papers.title: Tilted Convexity and an Exact Offline-Online Separation
papers.abstract: Convexity has three equivalent descriptions: support by affine functions, monotonicity of the subdifferential, and increasing secant slopes. We weaken all three by one distortion with parameter $γ\in(0,1]$, which multiplies positive changes by $γ$ and divides negative ones by $γ$. The resulting classes are the convex functions at $γ=1$ and, for $γ<1$, are distinct and nested, with the parameter dropping by at most a square along the chain. For proper lower semicontinuous functions in these classes, the effective domain is convex, local minimizers are global, and the function is locally Lipschitz on the relative interior of its domain. The classes separate offline from online optimization over compact convex sets with efficient projection, with access to function values and bounded support vectors. A smooth member of any class can be minimized to additive accuracy $\varepsilon$ with $\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)$ first-order queries and projections. Online, with nonpositive losses and $α$-regret measured against $α$ times the best fixed point, a polynomial-time algorithm achieves $γ$-regret $O(\sqrt T)$ on the largest class. For every fixed, effectively specified $γ\in(0,1)$ and every $α\in(γ,1]$, no randomized polynomial-time algorithm has sublinear expected $α$-regret unless $\mathbf{NP}=\mathbf{RP}$, already for smooth concave polynomial losses in the smallest class, each minimized by one linear optimization. Thus, unless $\mathbf{NP}=\mathbf{RP}$, $γ$ is the exact online coefficient of each class, while the offline coefficient is one.

papers.title: Fracture-Bench: A Controlled Benchmark Suite for Machine Learning Surrogates in Phase-Field Fracture Mechanics
papers.abstract: Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly proposed to replace phase-field fracture simulations in many-query tasks such as uncertainty quantification, inverse analysis and design. Little controlled evidence shows which architectures are reliable, for which fracture problems and how far beyond their training data. We introduce Fracture-Bench, an open benchmark of two phase-field datasets with fixed splits, common test metrics and a description of each dataset's physical regime. Dataset~1 contains 1,000 AT2 simulations of multiple cracks growing from a notched hole in a hyperelastic plate under random non-uniform biaxial boundary displacements (44 load steps, $128\times128$ grid). Dataset~2 contains 4,000 PF-CZM simulations of a pre-cracked plate with two inclusions, each ten times stiffer or more compliant than the matrix ($128\times256$ grid). We train a Fourier neural operator (FNO), DeepONet, Latent DeepONet, a UNet and a conditional diffusion model on identical splits and compare one test metric per dataset, training time, inference time and model size. On Dataset~1, FNO and Latent DeepONet attain mean test errors of order $10^{-6}$, about ten times lower than UNet and DeepONet. On Dataset~2, the diffusion model is most accurate, with about one sixth of the UNet error, but requires \SI{706}{s} per prediction versus \SI{6}{ms} for UNet. For all architectures, most of the error occurs in the final load steps, after crack localization. Dataset~2 contains initial cracks less than one grid cell apart that produce qualitatively different paths. Architecture rankings therefore depend on the task, and errors averaged over densely sampled inputs reveal little about near-bifurcation cases. Data, codes, splits, regime descriptors and generalization splits are public, with a protocol for adding under-represented regimes such as mixed-mode, three-dimensional and experimentally paired fracture.

papers.title: Polarity-Programmed Topological Gating of Knotting in Spatially Patterned Active Polymers
papers.abstract: Spatially patterned tangential activity provides a route to program polymer topology through both geometry and propulsion direction. We use Langevin-dynamics simulations of a flexible, self-avoiding linear polymer to determine how active-domain placement and independently assigned propulsion polarities control nonequilibrium knotting. Reversing the polarities of two terminal active blocks switches the steady state from a nearly always-knotted regime to effective knot suppression, changing the knotting probability by more than three orders of magnitude despite identical active-block positions and activity magnitude. Across symmetric terminal two-block architectures, we further identify an approximate zero-one-two free-end-alignment rule: zero, one, and two free-end-aligned active blocks correspond, respectively, to suppressed, intermediate, and high-knotting states. A two-state kinetic decomposition shows that the conditional knot-formation rate changes only by about threefold under polarity reversal, whereas the mean knot lifetime changes by several orders of magnitude, demonstrating that knot survival and passive-region storage dominate the polarity-controlled switch. Block placement provides an additional geometrical gate: moving an active domain from the chain interior to a terminal region strongly enhances both knot formation and survival. Knot-center residence, knotted-arc distributions, and episode-resolved kymographs reveal formation near free-end-aligned active blocks, directed contour migration, tightening, and long-lived retention in passive regions. Together, these results support a source-conveyor-reservoir-sink mechanism in which signed polarity and spatial activity patterning control whether knots are generated, transported, stored, or rapidly lost, providing a route to programmable topological states in nonequilibrium active polymers.

papers.title: Structured Neural Network Models for Anisotropic Magnetic Constitutive Laws
papers.abstract: High-performance electrical steel used for iron cores of power transformers and generators exhibits complex material behavior. While modeling and simulation of isotropic nonlinear response is well understood, the incorporation of magnetic anisotropy remains challenging. This work proposes to utilize a structured neural network architecture to systematically describe the anisotropic nonlinear anhysteretic magnetic material response of electrical steel sheets. By constructing a convex and smooth co-energy density with dedicated behavior at infinity, we can ensure thermodynamic consistency and correct physical behavior and further guarantee basic mathematical properties which provide well-posedness of corresponding magnetic field problems and efficient numerical solvers. Numerical tests demonstrate the capability of the proposed method to describe strongly anisotropic behavior as well as its robust convergence in finite-element simulations.

papers.title: Higgs pair production and Higgs potential in arbitrary renormalisable extensions of the Higgs sector
papers.abstract: Higgs self-interactions are crucial for probing the up to now largely unknown form of the Higgs potential that is realised in nature. Higgs boson pair production at the (High-Luminosity) LHC is of prime importance in this context as it provides experimental access to the trilinear Higgs self-interaction that enters at leading order in this process. The predictions for the trilinear Higgs self-couplings and the shape of the Higgs potential can vastly differ from the predictions of the Standard Model (SM) as a consequence of physics beyond the SM (BSM). If additional particles are relatively light (but in agreement with all existing experimental and theoretical constraints), their effects may not necessarily be accurately described by established effective field theory methods. Because of the potentially large modifications compared to the SM predictions the di-Higgs process has a high sensitivity for probing BSM physics. In order to enable the comparison between experiment and theory for a wide range of BSM models, automatised predictions for double Higgs production are in order. In this contribution to the LHC Higgs Working Group Report 5 we present \texttt{anyHH}, a novel tool for calculating the Higgs boson pair production cross-section in gluon fusion, which is the dominant production process for two Higgs bosons at the (HL-)LHC, for arbitrary renormalisable extensions of the Higgs sector.

papers.title: A heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent test for process noise calibration of Kalman filters in multi-sensor orbit determination
papers.abstract: Process noise calibration is a central problem in sequential orbit determination. If the process noise covariance is too small the filter is overconfident, and if it is too large it is overconservative. In both cases the estimation error grows and the reported covariance stops describing it, which affects downstream products such as conjunction assessment or re-entry prediction. No widely adopted method diagnoses the calibration in multi-sensor settings, where measurements of different type and dimension must enter a single consistency metric. This work presents the Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Dimensionless Averaged Normalised Innovation Squared (HAC-DANIS) test, which evaluates process noise calibration from the innovation sequence of the filter, without ground truth. The normalised innovation squared (NIS) of each measurement is divided by its dimension, which puts sensors of any dimension on a common scale, and the standard error of the averaged sequence is obtained with the heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent (HAC) Newey--West estimator, which accounts for the sensor-dependent variance of the sequence and for the serial correlation left by a miscalibrated filter or an imperfect dynamical model. Under mixing and moment conditions the statistic is asymptotically standard normal for a calibrated filter, and for a miscalibrated one its sign indicates the direction of the miscalibration. The autocorrelation function of the normalised sequence complements the test with a characterisation of the mistuning regime. Applied to an unscented Kalman filter processing simulated laser, telescope and radar observations of four satellites in low Earth orbit, the test rejects the eight miscalibrated process noise configurations with the sign of their miscalibration and does not reject the four calibrated with it.

papers.title: Theory of the Ferroaxial Charge Density Wave in 1T-TiSe$_2$
papers.abstract: Recent experiments using strain to probe the charge-density wave (CDW) of 1T-TiSe$_2$ have uncovered additional transitions and broken symmetries inside the CDW state. The elastocaloric effect reveals a second transition below $T_\mathrm{CDW}$, which elastoresistivity shows to be associated with ferroaxial order, breaking all vertical mirror symmetries while preserving inversion. In addition, at even lower temperatures, a diverging nematic susceptibility has been reported through elastoresistivity. In this work, we argue that this rich phenomenology cannot be explained by the standard $L_1^-$ CDW order parameter, and instead requires the existence of a secondary CDW order parameter. Based on symmetry, microscopic, and diffraction considerations, we propose this subleading CDW to have $L_2^-$ symmetry. By analyzing the Landau theory of coupled $L_1^-$ and $L_2^-$ orders in the presence of strain, we reproduce the phase boundaries observed in the elastocaloric measurements and the emergence of ferroaxial order below the CDW transition. Moreover, the model supports a third threefold-rotational symmetry breaking transition at lower temperatures, consistent with the reported divergence of the nematic susceptibility.

papers.title: High-order in-cell discontinuous reconstruction path-conservative methods for conservative systems in primitive variables
papers.abstract: We present a path-conservative methodology for the numerical approximation of conservative systems formulated exclusively in primitive variables, the most physically relevant set of variables. The approach is designed to preserve the correct weak solution while avoiding the spurious oscillations near contact discontinuities that may arise in conservative formulations. Nonconservative products are treated through the selection of a suitable family of paths combined with an in-cell discontinuous reconstruction strategy, which is locally activated near shocks. To choose the path we introduce a compatibility condition between the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions of the non-conservative form, with the exact ones, assumed to be known. In smooth regions and across contact discontinuities, a standard path-conservative scheme is employed. The method is further extended to achieve high-order accuracy. Numerical results for the Euler multimaterial and shear interface model demonstrates correct shock-capturing property, suppression of spurious oscillations due to contact discontinuities, and convergence without using hybrid formulations.

papers.title: Study on the charmless decay modes of $Z_{cs}(3985)$
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the charmless decay modes of the hidden-charm tetraquark state with strangeness, $Z_{cs}(3985)$, assuming it to be an $S$-wave hadronic molecule of $D_{s}^{*-}D^{0}$ and $D_{s}^{-}D^{*0}$ with quantum numbers $I(J^{P}) = \frac{1}{2}(1^{+})$. Using an effective Lagrangian approach, we calculate the decay amplitudes for $Z_{cs} \to \mathcal{PV}$ (where $\mathcal P$ and $\mathcal V$ denote light pseudoscalar and vector mesons, respectively) via triangle loop diagrams. We use the experimental upper limit on $Z_c(3900)\to πω$ to constrain the cutoff parameter for both the dipole and tripole form factors. Numerical results from the dipole form factor show that the branching ratios for $Z_{cs} \to πK^*$ can reach up to the order of $10^{-2}$, which is of the same order of magnitude as the hidden charm decay modes and may be detected in future measurements. The branching ratios from tripole form factor are not consistent with those from the dipole form factor, indicating a certain degree of model dependence in the present work. The relative ratios of the branching ratios for different decay channels are found to be almost independent of the cutoff parameter. However, some ratios are highly dependent on the choice of the dipole or tripole form factor. The branching ratio of $Z_{cs} \to ηK^{*}$ is found to be highly sensitive to the $η$-$η^\prime$ mixing angle, while that for $Z_{cs} \to η^\prime K^{*}$ is almost independent of the mixing angle, making it a clean channel for future experimental measurements.

papers.title: Robustness against lying of the confidence interval for a fraction of population with a sensitive characteristic
papers.abstract: In the investigations devoted to sensitive questions the problem is with the truthfulness of survey participants. We offer a fresh perspective on respondent deception. We investigate the influence of lying on the properties of the confidence intervals for the fraction of the sensitive part of a population. It is shown that the coverage probability is robust against lying.

papers.title: GIST: Location-Dependent Uplink Path Structure Transfer for FDD Downlink Channel Estimation
papers.abstract: A key challenge of downlink (DL) channel estimation in frequency division duplex (FDD) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems is the pilot overhead, which grows with the numbers of antennas and subcarriers. However, a prior on path delays and directions shared by the uplink (UL) and DL channels can reduce this overhead. A model trained only on UL channels measured at a base station (BS) can predict the path structure (delays, directions and power gains) from the location of a user equipment (UE) and thereby assist DL channel estimation. In this paper, we propose Gaussian-Informed Structure Transfer (GIST), in which each Gaussian primitive models one propagation path, whose delay, directions and power gain are predicted from the UE location relative to the primitive center. The complex gains of the predicted paths are estimated from DL pilots by linear minimum mean square error estimation with this prior. Experiments on a ray-traced and a measured dataset show that GIST outperforms all baselines, reaching a lower DL estimation error with fewer pilot subcarriers. Further experiments demonstrate its robustness to UE location errors, its low storage and computational requirements.

papers.title: ISAC-Assisted Proactive Handover in mmWave Networks: Value of Foresight and Localization Requirements
papers.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) links can lose tens of decibels within milliseconds when a person or vehicle crosses the line of sight, and reactive handover recovers only after the outage has begun. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) promises to let the network see blockers coming and move users to another cell in advance. This paper asks how much such foresight is worth relative to the best reactive handover, and what sensing accuracy is needed to harvest it. We formulate cost-aware cell selection with knowledge of the future signal-to- noise ratio as a sequential decision problem, define the value of foresight through a policy-independent bound, and develop an ISAC-assisted handover framework in which a radio unit senses blockers with its own communication waveform and a simulated Open RAN xApp plans handovers. Ray-traced experiments in a 28 GHz street canyon, reported on held-out scenarios, show that, with a short look-ahead, perfect foresight closes most of the gap between service-aware (Layer-3) reactive handover and an instantaneous oracle. Harvesting this value, however, requires the user and nearby blockers to be localized to about a decimeter, well beyond what our radar tracker and meter- level user positioning provide; with realistic errors, even an uncertainty-aware planner largely defers to reactive handover.

papers.title: Sharp bounds and asymptotic profiles for Lane-Emden systems at the Serrin threshold
papers.abstract: We classify isolated singularities of $p$-Laplace and $k$-Hessian Lane--Emden systems on their Serrin critical curves without radial symmetry. Our approach reconstructs a radial profile from the source measures through a truncated Wolff potential, providing a nonlinear counterpart of spherical averaging. For upper inequalities at equal powers, we determine the sharp joint logarithmic lower bound on the zero-mass singular branch. A radial pair attains this bound while both normalized components oscillate between zero and infinity. For exact systems at equal powers, we obtain a common second-order profile with a shared phase and a sharp two-term logarithmic expansion of the component difference. At unequal powers, we establish power--logarithmic asymptotics with explicit leading constants. These asymptotics hold uniformly in direction.

papers.title: On the Failure Probability of Quantum Leftover Hashing with Bad Seeds
papers.abstract: We study hashing against quantum adversaries, as used in cryptographic applications, and provide bounds on the probability of failure in practical settings where seeds might be reused and might be non-ideal. Randomness extraction and privacy amplification are key components of quantum cryptographic protocols, such as quantum randomness generation or key distribution, that allow the compression of partially secure raw data into shorter output with high security. To ensure the security of any cryptographic construction that integrates them, it is desirable to establish composable security. This can be done by using methods based on universal hashing and leveraging the general leftover hash lemma, which allows extraction of near-uniform random numbers from an imperfect entropy source by sampling from an almost two-universal family of hash functions using a seed. This approach is taken in many practical implementations, commonly using Toeplitz hashing. The lemma provides an upper bound $\varepsilon$ on the distance of the output to uniform randomness, which holds on average over the choice of seeds. It makes no claim that any particular seed yields near-uniform random numbers. This poses a problem for practical applications where a seed is sampled once and reused for many rounds (blockwise hashing). Here, we study the subset of \textit{bad} seeds yielding far-from-uniform outputs. We show that randomness extraction against quantum side information is guaranteed to produce $δ$-close-to-uniform random numbers except with failure probability $\left(\frac{\varepsilon}δ\right)^2$. This result is generalised to blockwise hashing providing a guarantee of the security of $k$ rounds except with failure probability $\big(\frac{(2k-1)\varepsilon}δ\big)^2$. Moreover, we extend the general leftover hash lemma to blockwise hashing and relax the assumption of almost two-universality.

papers.title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
papers.abstract: The shear piezoelectric coefficient $e_{15}$ governs the shear-mode electromechanical coupling in piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, but measuring it typically requires destructive resonance testing on dedicated specimens. On simulated data, $e_{15}$ can instead be recovered non-destructively from sparse, noisy subsurface wavefield observations using a constrained physics-informed neural network (PINN). By building exact spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers directly into the network output, the clamped, grounded boundaries and resting initial state hold automatically, leaving the loss with only the interior equations of coupled electro-elastodynamics and the data misfit. Non-dimensional scaling brings all governing coefficients within one decade of O(1), and the setup removes the boundary and initial-condition penalty weights that soft-constraint methods must tune. In a six-way comparison (plane-strain PZT-5H, manufactured wavefield, 30 dB noise), a soft-penalty baseline with adaptive weights converges to an erroneous $e_{15}$ in four of the five runs (51.7% mean error), and fixed penalties reach an error of 0.85% only after a second-order optimization stage. The constrained formulations reach mean $e_{15}$ errors between 0.15% and 0.51% with held-out displacement errors below 1%. Within these variants, the spatial multiplier gives rapid first-order convergence, and the quadratic temporal multiplier lowers the early-time electrostatic residual by a factor of 6.8 versus a linear one. On finite-element data along one subsurface line, the full formulation recovers $e_{15}$ with 1.19% mean error at 30 dB and keeps it between 0.65% and 2.71% across a 40 to 0 dB noise sweep. Finally, training on displacements alone still recovers $e_{15}$ with mean errors of 0.45% on finite-element and 1.64% on manufactured data.

papers.title: A Hybrid Visitor Prediction Framework using Interpretable Temporal features, Integrating IQR and Anomaly Detection in Lakes in Nebraska
papers.abstract: For effective resource management, infrastructure planning, and sustainable tourism, it is really important to predict accurate visitors. This paper estimates the daily visitation of Nebraska lakes using spatial, basic temporal, and interpretable temporal features. Moreover, we evaluate the base models with multiple metrics. Using the best three models, our method will ensemble hybrid models and choose the best hybrid technique. Further, we investigate the impact of lag features and how the models work with different outlier detection techniques such as Interquartile Range (IQR) and anomaly detection. The models are evaluated using regression metrics (MAE, MSE, RMSE, MAPE, and R2). Experiment results show that, after removing anomalies, MAE, MSE, RMSE, and MAPE are reduced. Adding lag features also shows some positive effects on the results. Moreover, anomaly detection techniques perform better than IQR in improving performance while preserving data. The reported anomaly-based cross-validation results favored the voting ensemble over the compared base models on the evaluated metrics. In anomaly-based cross-validation, VOTE improved prediction errors compared with MLP (256,128,64); improvements varied in the single-split comparison. Specifically, the hybrid model reduced MAE by 9.82%, MSE by 3.12%, RMSE by 1.76%, and MAPE by 6.77%. In the reported cross-validation comparison, the best anomaly-based hybrid model had lower MAE, MSE, RMSE, and MAPE than the best IQR-based hybrid model by 9.81%, 34.30%, 18.99%, and 0.66%, respectively.

papers.title: Efficient congruencing in $\mathbb Z[t]$ modulo $t^2$
papers.abstract: We develop an analogue of nested efficient congruencing applicable in the ring $\mathbb Z[t]/t^2\mathbb Z[t]$ so as to estimate mean values related to that of Vinogradov. Let $k$ be a natural number, and suppose that $\varphi_j(u)\in \mathbb Z[t,u]$ $(1\le j\le k)$ is a system of polynomials having Wronskian $W(u;\boldsymbol \varphi)=\det ({\rm d}^i\varphi_j(u)/{\rm d}u^i)_{1\le i,j\le k}$ with respect to $u$. Consider the number $Υ_{s,k}(X;\boldsymbol \varphi)$ of integral solutions of the system of equations \[ \sum_{i=1}^s \bigl( \varphi_j(u_i+v_it)-\varphi_j(u_{s+i}+v_{s+i}t)\bigr) \equiv 0 \pmod{t^2}\quad (1\le j\le k), \] with $|u_i|\le X$ and $|v_i|\le X$ $(1\le i\le s)$. We show that when $W(u;\boldsymbol \varphi)\not\equiv 0\pmod{t}$ and $1\le s\le k(k+1)/2$, then $Υ_{s,k}(X;\boldsymbol \varphi)\ll X^{2s+\varepsilon}$. Our conclusions extend to number fields and function fields, as we outline. We describe several consequences of our results, including forthcoming work establishing the main conjecture for certain systems of equations not possessing translation-dilation invariant properties.

papers.title: Cherenkov radiation constraint on the photon mass from a two-form gauge potential
papers.abstract: We investigate how electromagnetic radiation in massive antisymmetric tensor theories can be used to constrain the photon mass. In this context, massive electrodynamics constitutes one realization of the $B \wedge F$ class of models in $(3+1)$ dimensions and is obtained by dualizing Stueckelberg-like massive gauge theories. Notably, this model is characterized by the mixing of a $U(1)$ gauge potential with an Abelian $3$-form field of the type found in the topological sector of QCD. We then examine how mass affects permittivity and susceptibility and, consequently, modifies the refractive index through the dispersion relation. We subsequently investigate the electromagnetic radiation emitted by a moving charged particle as it interacts with a medium within the framework of massive electrodynamics. Our findings indicate that the medium through which the particle travels drives the radiation, in a manner analogous to the Cherenkov effect. Applying our results to data on Cherenkov radiation produced at Super-Kamiokande, we derive a photon mass bound of 1 eV ($ 10^ {- 36} $ kg), which is consistent with known estimates based on superconductors.

papers.title: RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills
papers.abstract: Third-party Agent Skills extend what an autonomous agent can do, but a malicious Skill can hide data exposure or output manipulation inside a legitimate workflow. Neither reading a Skill's description nor granting it tool permissions tells whether its execution meets the user's security requirements. We introduce RuntimeTickets, a protocol that enforces and audits these requirements while a Skill runs. From released malicious-Skill datasets we derive a risk model and build adversarial-benign Skill pairs. From the task's delivery contract, a language model proposes security obligations for that task. Each obligation cites the Skill lines it answers, and the ticket tightens the host's approvals into fine-grained allowed actions but never loosens them. A runtime gate checks the recipient, object and amount of every outbound send before forwarding it, and trusted monitors record the effects within their observation scope. The ticket links these checks and observations to the approved obligations of each Skill run, and a deterministic decoder turns the ticket's status into governable data flows and verifies each obligation. Neither enforcement nor decoding involves a language model, so text injected by a Skill can change the proposal but never the rule that decides a send. We evaluate RuntimeTickets at the network egress boundary of three unmodified agent frameworks against production Skill scanners and runtime baselines, among them an AgentBound-derived allow-list and SkillGuard. RuntimeTickets eliminated both failure modes of current Skill defenses, overlook (malicious Skills let through) and overkill (benign Skills blocked): its overlook rate was 0.0% and its overkill rate 0.0%, while the scanners erred on both sides. RuntimeTickets ties approved requirements to verifiable execution evidence and offers a common foundation for the safe and auditable deployment of third-party Skills.

papers.title: Exploring Proximity and Tactile Sensing for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Pre-touch sensing, or sensing information about an object before contact, is an attractive modality for robot hands as it can allow a robot to anticipate and respond to a contact before it happens. In this work, we introduce ToFTouch, a multimodal tactile sensor combining three multizone (4$\times$4 resolution) time-of-flight sensors with an optics-based pressure sensing array. We mount this sensor on a parallel jaw gripper and demonstrate its utility on three distinct tasks: (i) pre-grasp adjustment, (ii) item extraction from clutter, and (iii) item insertion into tight spaces. For pre-grasp adjustment, ToF feedback reduced cycle time by 7.4$\%$ by enabling anticipatory gripper closure during approach. For extraction, ToF sensing enabled successful retrieval across all tested depth offsets ($\pm$2 cm) deviating from the nominal pick point, including conditions where baseline approaches failed, with standard deviations below 0.4 cm. For insertion into dense clutter, we explore the proximity and tactile information provided from ToFTouch during an insertion trajectory. The results demonstrate the utility of multizone ToF sensing in a manipulation environment.

papers.title: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
papers.abstract: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions.

papers.title: Gradient flow formulation and discrete approximation of reaction-cross-diffusion systems with size exclusion
papers.abstract: We characterize a class of possibly degenerate nonlinear reaction-cross-diffusion systems with size exclusion as (non-metric) gradient flows in continuity-equation format driven by entropy. We then establish a connection between these systems and discrete reaction networks by proving an EDP-type lower limit inequality for the associated gradient systems. In the non-degenerate case, we show a chain rule identity that allows us to identify minimizers of the corresponding energy-dissipation functional as weak solutions to the PDE system. In conjunction with the lower limit, this yields an alternative proof of existence of weak solutions and their approximability by solutions to the proposed discrete ODE systems. Finally, we generalize our results to models including drift terms by extending the established framework to tilted energy landscapes.

papers.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
papers.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. Thermodynamic stability at high pressure and dynamical stability at ambient pressure indicate that it can be made by the route established for this family.

papers.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Signing and Verification Performance of Verifiable Credential Formats: A Cross-Language Benchmark of SD-JWT VC, W3C VCDM, and mdoc
papers.abstract: We compare the signing and verification performance of three Verifiable Credential (VC) formats--SD-JWT VC; the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 with a Data Integrity cryptosuite (W3C VCDM); and mdoc (ISO/IEC 18013-5)--over one scope: issue, present with selective disclosure, verify. Node.js, Go and Python implementations ran in four environments, one a cloud VM (N=2,000 across five runs; medians of each statistic and the spread). For an end-to-end exchange disclosing 5 of 20 attributes, the total (issue, present, verify) on Node.js in the cloud VM is 0.265 ms for mdoc, 0.298 ms for SD-JWT VC and 0.534 ms for W3C VCDM. The four span a factor of five in speed; across them W3C VCDM takes 1.73--2.04x mdoc and 1.57--1.79x SD-JWT VC--at least five times our 10% band--and the ordering survives unifying the algorithm on Ed25519 and P-256. The mdoc--SD-JWT VC difference is not robust: the totals differ by 12%, 28%, 19% and 10% in the four environments, and at verification mdoc is the slower in one of them. RDFC-1.0 canonicalization produces the gap: the cryptosuite canonicalizes twice per operation, so one exchange canonicalizes six times. We attribute that cost to the specification rather than to a library mainly by replacing RDFC-1.0 with JCS, which brings W3C VCDM verification to within 5% of SD-JWT VC in three environments and within 12% in the fourth; three implementations in three languages agree, though they share a lineage. Because eddsa-rdfc-2022 has no derivation step, presenting a subset re-signs it; ecdsa-sd-2023, which preserves the issuer signature, costs 3.4 ms to issue and 1.5--2.4 ms to derive and verify there. With production education schemas, canonicalization costs 31--49x a simple credential across the four, and blank node labeling is not the driver. The measured path ends at the issuer signature check.

papers.title: Harder Than the Task: From Technical to Organizational Difficulty in AI Benchmarking
papers.abstract: AI benchmarks have made remarkable progress in measuring the ability of AI systems to perform increasingly demanding cognitive and technical tasks. Yet, many of these benchmarks treat technical tasks as the unit of analysis, while much economically valuable work takes place within organizations, where tasks are embedded in a system of relations. Within organizations, successful task performance depends not only on solving the technical demands of the task but also on navigating the interdependence of activities, distributed knowledge, differentiated authority, temporal constraints, conflicting interests, and changing environmental conditions while the task is underway. Accordingly, we argue that organizational task difficulty constitutes a distinct and insufficiently recognized dimension of AI capability, and that existing approaches to benchmarking provide an incomplete basis for assessing how effectively AI agents can perform real-world organizational work. By drawing on organization theory, we develop a taxonomy of the structure of work that characterizes the conditions that agents face in organizational work. Applying this taxonomy to analyze existing benchmarks, we find limited and uneven coverage of organizational dimensions, with fewer than one quarter of prominent benchmarks claiming any of them. We therefore argue that AI benchmarks should increasingly move beyond the evaluation of technically difficult tasks toward the systematic assessment of agents' ability to navigate the organizational conditions under which economically valuable work takes place.

papers.title: Gaussian Products: Deterministic Principal Ideals and Wick Order Recovery
papers.abstract: For fixed Hilbert--Schmidt operators $A,B$ and a standard Gaussian array $G$, the algebraic principal ideal generated by $AGB$ almost surely equals a deterministic ideal obtained by multiplying the square tails of $s(A)$ and $s(B)$. In fixed coordinates, the corresponding singular-value comparisons hold simultaneously for all nonincreasing square-summable diagonal weights. We characterize the numerical arrays with this uniform realization property on any two prescribed rank flags by rectangular operator-norm upper bounds and Hilbert--Schmidt lower bounds; the optimal universal upper dilation is two. A family of strictly positive factors reflects every inclusion of principal ideals if and only if its tail-rank profiles have no common eventual upper bound. Otherwise, every local flag region contains a common fibre whose input ideals form a copy of $\mathcal P(\mathbb N)/\mathrm{Fin}$ as a sublattice. For a specified family of operator-valued Gaussian chaoses, Wick composition with one fixed random operator yields principal ideals that recover these inclusion relations. The random ideal identities hold almost surely for each fixed parameter choice.

papers.title: Online Label-Free Gradient Matching for Continual Language Model Training
papers.abstract: Language models in customer-facing products must be continually updated, since the data they serve shifts over time. As retraining on the full accumulated data is impractical, each update should instead run on a small set of examples carrying the training signal of all data seen so far. The strongest current methods build this set by gradient matching, which synthesizes examples whose training gradients match those of the full data. However, they require ground-truth labels, run once on a fixed snapshot rather than on a growing stream, and are slow on large data. We introduce \textbf{OLGA}, which lifts these limitations. It distills unlabeled data by drawing the gradient matching targets from the model's own next-token predictions. Across five text classification benchmarks with phi-1.5, it improves accuracy by 10 percentage points over the strongest selection baseline using as few as five examples. OLGA also distills online data streams by keeping a running rehearsal memory of synthetic examples, which is re-distilled together with each new batch as it arrives. In the online setting, it outperforms the strongest selection-based continual baseline by 6.6 stream-AUC percentage points. Finally, our method scales to large data by pairing distillation with selection in a hybrid pipeline, letting selection handle the mild stage of compression and distillation the extreme one. It cuts runtime by 30\% versus distillation alone at similar accuracy, and beats the best selection-only pipeline by up to 12.6 percentage points.

papers.title: Multiprobe strategies for Kinematic Lensing with the Roman Space Telescope High Latitude Wide Area Survey
papers.abstract: In its latest design, the High Latitude Wide Area Survey (HLWAS) Medium Tier comprises overlapping photometric and spectroscopic data across 2,300 square degrees. This dataset enables Kinematic Lensing (KL), a Weak Lensing (WL) technique that exploits galaxy kinematics to control for shape noise, the dominant statistical limitation of traditional WL. We present several simulated analyses quantifying the expected cosmological science return of a Roman KL analysis with the latest design of the HLWAS: We explore KL prospects with early Roman data from the Deep Tier fields and from the early Medium Tier fields; we demonstrate the impact of different roll-angle choices on the KL performance; we benchmark KL against traditional WL; we introduce a KL-based multiprobe analysis that jointly models KL, galaxy clustering, and galaxy-galaxy lensing. In these analyses, we consider systematics, including photometric uncertainties, shear calibration bias, galaxy bias, and baryonic feedback. Our results show that KL alone achieves a dark energy figure of merit (FoM) of 22.54, which is more than a factor of two improvement over a corresponding WL analysis. The KL multiprobe approach improves the full-survey FoM to 34.58, even assuming conservative scale cuts in the clustering and galaxy-galaxy lensing. For the HLWAS roll-angle strategy, we find that the current plan of 4 passes with rotations of approximately 0, 10, 170, 180 degrees are near optimal for KL.

papers.title: SNAP: Semantic Navigation Among Pedestrians
papers.abstract: Navigating crowded urban environments requires robots to avoid pedestrians while adhering to social norms such as remaining on sidewalks. Existing approaches typically address either crowd avoidance or semantic path planning in isolation. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) navigation policy that jointly reasons about semantic terrain and dynamic obstacles from a single semantically annotated bird's-eye-view (BEV) map, without relying on explicit human-state estimation. Our policy outperforms established crowd-navigation and semantic-aware baselines and transfers zero-shot to a legged robot, demonstrating socially compliant navigation in highly dynamic real-world scenarios.

papers.title: Shadow Molecular Dynamics for General Nonlinear Flexible-Charge Models
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials have greatly expanded the reach of molecular dynamics simulations, but complex chemical environments often require explicit treatment of long-range electronic response, including charge transfer and polarization. Physics-based flexible-charge models capture these effects but require global nonlinear charge equilibration at every time step to obtain Born-Oppenheimer energies and forces. This process is computationally expensive and can lead to instabilities unless tightly converged. Here, we introduce a shadow molecular dynamics framework for flexible-charge models with arbitrary local nonlinearities and long-range multipolar electrostatics. We replace the exact Born-Oppenheimer potential with a nearby shadow potential obtained by exactly equilibrating a partially linearized electronic energy functional. This provides conservative forces and reduces the global nonlinear equilibration to a quasi-diagonal linear problem that can be solved directly at low cost. Auxiliary dynamical electronic degrees of freedom, propagated through an extended-Lagrangian dynamics, capture the long-range electronic response and define the reference state for the linearization of the energy functional. GPU-accelerated simulations with over 100,000 atoms demonstrate that the shadow potential closely follows the tightly converged Born-Oppenheimer surface, while maintaining long-term stability at a computational cost approaching that of a fixed-charge model. These advances establish an efficient and broadly applicable framework for machine-learned interatomic potentials that explicitly incorporate long-range electrostatic interactions and environment-dependent electronic response.

papers.title: Can AI Do Formal Demography? Why Vaccinating the Oldest Saves Both the Most Lives and the Most Years of Life
papers.abstract: Can AI contribute to formal demography? We report an experiment in which an AI model, Claude, was asked to explain and then simplify the proof of an earlier result: that vaccinating the oldest against COVID-19 saves both the most lives and the most years of life, because the years saved per person treated rise with age. The model proposed a new proof that is shorter, more intuitive, and somewhat more general than the original, built from a known life-table identity and the definition of convexity. It states the condition for the result as the convexity of the reciprocal of the hazard, which can be checked from the hazard alone and holds for most familiar parametric models, and it yields a lower bound on life expectancy whenever that condition is met. Prompted by a further question, the model also gave an exact form of the condition, showing how far convexity can be relaxed. The model traced these identities and related results in earlier literature. An edited record of the sessions is provided, and complete transcripts are available on request. The exercise suggests that AI can revisit established results, make them easier to understand, and prove valuable generalizations.

papers.title: When Robots Outweigh Objects: How Inertia Mismatch Shapes Robot Policy Learning
papers.abstract: Conventional robot arms can be extremely heavy compared with the everyday objects they manipulate, creating a significant inertia mismatch at contact. Even a small accidental bump from a heavy arm can knock a light object out of place. Modern learning methods have nevertheless demonstrated a wide range of successful manipulation behaviors on these platforms, suggesting that even extreme inertia mismatch can be overcome with sufficient data. However, it remains unclear whether high inertia imposes a hidden cost on learning, potentially worsening scaling with data or lowering the performance ceiling of modern robot learning methods. We investigate this question through controlled simulation experiments that vary robot and object masses. We find that reinforcement learning succeeds across a broad range of mass combinations, while behavior cloning learns more reliable policies when a lighter robot manipulates a heavier object. Heavier robots require more demonstrations to attain the same performance as lighter robots. Finally, because new hardware is rarely an option, we explore ways to lower an existing arm's inertia at contact with existing hardware, either by choosing a lower-inertia workspace before collecting data or by steering the demonstrator toward lower-inertia configurations during the task. In both cases, the lower-inertia demonstrations are imitated more reliably. Project website: https://younghyopark.me/inertia-mismatch/

papers.title: Toward Artifact-Free Dermoscopy: Characterization of ISIC 2019 Image Defects for Deep Learning Applications
papers.abstract: The International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) archive offers the largest publicly available collection of dermoscopic images for skin lesion analysis. However, the ISIC 2019 dataset suffers from several acquisition artifacts such as hair occlusions, vignetting, surgical ink markings, and ruler scales, all of which compromise its utility in deep learning workflows by introducing non-biological visual structures. To address these limitations, we present a rigorously annotated version of ISIC 2019 that includes binary masks for key artifact types. Ink marks and vignetting were annotated through systematic manual review and iterative refinement using professional image editing software. For hair and ruler artifacts, we implemented a semi-automatic pipeline based on our previously developed deep learning architecture, ChimeraNet. Automated predictions were then manually corrected as needed for precision. The resulting dataset supports both the development of our own melanoma detection model and broader community research requiring artifact-mitigated dermoscopic images.

papers.title: A Cross-Domain Matrix Engine for Signal Processing and Deep Neural Net Inference
papers.abstract: Matrix multiplication dominates both PHY signal processing and Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference, yet these domains place opposing demands on the matrix engine. Signal processing requires low-latency execution of relatively small matrix operations, whereas DNN inference, particularly at large batch sizes, prioritizes high throughput and energy efficiency for large matrix multiplications. While offering efficient memory access profile, a Systolic Array (SA) adds fill and drain delays per matrix. Those can be amortized for large matrices but not for small matrices. Conversely, a tensor unit completes the kernel in few cycles but would require repeated reads of same operand tiles over large matrices. This makes SA too slow for signal processing and tensor too inefficient for AI. We show that this need not be a choice between systolic and tensor structuring of Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) units. We propose a single engine that operates primarily as a SA and, through low-cost reconfiguration, transforms into a tensor-style engine on a per-operation basis. MUXes create both the spatial reduction adder tree and temporal reduction accumulators from the existing MACs and registers within the systolic array. The proposed reconfigurable SA simulated using modified SCALESim simulator, verified on an Zynq 702 FPGA and synthesized using ASAP 7nm FinFET library. SCALE-Sim simulations shows up to 7.5x lower latency for small complex value PHY kernels. Even on DNN workloads, it achieves up to 1.65x speedups over vanilla SA execution with trivial increase of memory accesses, retaining the systolic array's memory access advantage. Synthesis results estimate reconfigurable fabric costs only 8% power and 13.6% area overheads.

papers.title: Hyperplane Furstenberg Sets in Higher Dimensions
papers.abstract: The hyperplane Furstenberg problem asks how small the Hausdorff dimension of $E\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ can be when a $t$-dimensional family of affine $(n-1)$-dimensional hyperplanes meets $E$ in sets of dimension at least $s$. For $0<s\le n-1$ and $0<t\le n$, we prove the sharp bound in $\mathbb{R}^n$ $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}E\ge\mathbf{F}(s,t;n,n-1)$, where $\mathbf{F}$ is Gan's Furstenberg index proposed in prime fields. We also construct examples attaining this bound for all parameters. Our main reduction theorem, Theorem 3.1, states that for $n\ge3$, $0<s\le n-2$, and $1<t\le n$, every weighted $(s,t)$ configuration $(E,H)$ at scale $δ$ produces a dual weighted $(s,t-1)$ configuration $(P,\mathcal{T})$ inside a hyperplane $H_{y_0}\cong\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$. The reduction uses radial projection and energy estimates for Frostman measures. Iterating this reduction and applying the Csörnyei--Stull incidence theorem yields the bound.

papers.title: Hyperbolic periodic orbits and optimal $1/t$ convergence of the Lax--Oleinik semigroup
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed manifold and $H:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ a $C^k$ ($k\geq2$) Tonelli Hamiltonian whose Aubry set consists of finitely many hyperbolic orbits, each of which is either a periodic orbit or a fixed point. We construct a $C^k$ critical subsolution that is quadratically strict outside the projected Aubry set. We then use this subsolution to establish an $O(1/t)$ rate of convergence for the associated Lax--Oleinik semigroup and the minimal action functions. This rate is optimal whenever at least one of these hyperbolic orbits is periodic.

papers.title: Polariton tweezers
papers.abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. We show that introducing targeted frequency detunings between the continuous-wave pumps strictly breaks the spatiotemporal symmetry of the system, converting the stationary macroscopic interference pattern into a dynamically moving conveyor belt. By precisely customizing these frequency detunings, the entire lattice - along with the electrostatically trapped electrons - can be rigidly driven in any arbitrary in-plane direction. This precise phase-matching mechanism bypasses the need for a net kinetic momentum transfer, establishing a robust, optically controlled platform for the long-range routing of charged particles and topological defects in driven-dissipative quantum fluids.

papers.title: The effects of an alternating bias on a single orbital spin impurity
papers.abstract: Electron spin resonance with the scanning tunneling microscope (ESR-STM) enables coherent manipulation and detection of individual atomic spins with atomic-scale spatial resolution, yet the microscopic mechanism by which the radiofrequency (RF) bias drives the spin remains under debate. We study this problem using a Redfield quantum-master-equation framework in which the oscillating bias enters explicitly through the electronic reservoirs rather than through an effective time-dependent tunneling amplitude. In the semiclassical limit, the RF voltage periodically sweeps the system through its static transport landscape, so that the transport regime depends jointly on the DC bias and RF amplitude. When the RF trajectory approaches or crosses a charge transition, the damping-like torque (DLT) associated with spin-polarized charge transfer is strongly enhanced. By contrast, the field-like torque (FLT) induced by the exchange field remains finite deeper in the Coulomb-blockade (CB) regime because it originates from virtual charge fluctuations. The RF trajectory also averages strongly bias-dependent static quantities over a finite voltage range, smoothing features such as the Lamb shift near the charge thresholds. These results establish the RF amplitude as a control parameter not only for the strength of the ESR drive, but also for the transport regime and the ratio between FLT and DLT.

papers.title: LODox: A Web-Based Platform for Cultural Heritage Linked Data Discovery
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models have transformed how data can be linked, discovered, and enhanced. LODox, Linked Open Data at Oxford, is an evolving web-based platform that embraces this transformation for cultural heritage Linked Open Data. LODox features a novel interface with intuitive card-based data presentation and visualization in a semantic portal. It represents an evolving approach to explore heterogeneous cultural heritage data across multiple sources through a unified interface. In this paper, we will briefly describe the LODox architecture, its implementation, and future development plan, particularly its alignment and integration with Solid.

papers.title: Attacking P2P Networks: Liveness Attacks on the GossipSub and DOG Gossip Protocols
