We detect the stellar rotation period at 12.7~d in the photometry, implying a fairly young gyrochronal age of $1.20^{+0.16}_{-0.30}~$Gyr for the system. With a Transmission Spectroscopy Metric of $112\pm 30$, this adolescent Neptune is a good target for atmospheric observations with \textit{JWST} and \textit{Ariel}, and we also find that it is amenable to future constraints on the (three-dimensional) stellar obliquity. TOI-4129\,b will therefore be an important testing ground for the idea that planets in the Neptune ridge underwent HEM to arrive at their current locations.

papers.title: Long-range entangled criticality from coherent errors
papers.abstract: We find that coherent error can induce a phase transition from the clean surface code phase into an extended long-range entangled critical regime with diverging Markov length. To demonstrate this, we establish two general results of independent interest. The first relates topology and quantum information to mixed-state entanglement: we show that when a noise channel acting on a topological code preserves a higher-form symmetry and nonzero coherent information, the noisy state for generic logical input is long-range entangled. The second generalizes the local recovery construction based on finite Markov length to any locally parameterized family, thus encompassing local Lindbladian evolution, coherent errors followed by syndrome dephasing, and thermal states. We apply these results to the honeycomb surface code, in which we find an extended long-range entangled critical regime that is a quasi-long-ranged counterpart of 1-form strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. As a byproduct of these studies, we relate the conditional mutual information to conductance in a Majorana network model.

papers.title: The STARfall pathway: forging intermediate-mass black holes through stellar collisions in dense star clusters
papers.abstract: Intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs, $10^2 < m_{\rm BH}/\mathrm{M}_{\odot} < 10^5$) are elusive objects bridging the gap between stellar-mass and supermassive black holes, whose origin remains uncertain. They may form from the collapse of very massive stars (VMSs, $m_*\geq150\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) assembled through repeated stellar collisions in compact and fast evolving star clusters. We investigate the formation of VMSs and IMBH seeds via repeated mergers and collisions as a function of cluster initial conditions, assessing the implications for globular clusters and dense high-redshift system. We develop STARfall, a semi-analytic tool that follows the evolution of a massive stellar binary via binary-single interactions, mergers, collisions, and stellar evolution, while consistently accounting for the host cluster evolution. Our results show that clusters with central densities above $10^6\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc}^{-3}$ can undergo a catastrophic sequence of stellar collisions, or "starastrophe", within $3$ Myr. Through this process, VMSs rapidly grow in mass and collapse into IMBHs with masses of up to $10^3-10^4\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$, despite the effects of intense stellar winds. Applying our models to observed systems, we find that compact clusters in the Cosmic Gems Arc and Milky Way globular clusters could have hosted VMSs that collapsed into IMBHs in this mass range. Despite their longer core-collapse timescales, the inferred central densities of Little Red Dots may also support IMBH formation in the same mass interval. Our models show that VMS assembly requires two essential ingredients: short core-collapse times and large central densities. Compared to observed systems, our models suggest that clusters in the Cosmic Gems Arcs and several Galactic globular clusters could have nurtured VMSs that directly collapsed to IMBHs with masses $10^3-10^4\,\text{M}_{\odot}$.

papers.title: Presupernovae Strongly Constrain Electrophilic MeV Bosons
papers.abstract: The years preceding a supernova (SN) can constrain new electrophilic bosons with MeV masses more than the explosion itself. Although cooler than SNe, the massive progenitors maintain consistently high temperatures much longer, injecting more particles whose decays to positrons contribute to the diffuse Galactic 511-keV emission. For dark photons, the increase is exacerbated by the lower plasma frequency compared to SNe, where MeV excitations are screened. We find preSNe bounds on dark photon couplings up to two orders of magnitude stronger than SNe for masses between 1 and 3~MeV, with similar improvements for other electrophilic species such as axion-like particles.

papers.title: Revisiting the Missing Baryon Problem: Baryon Redistribution Across Halo Evolution
papers.abstract: The baryon fraction provides a fundamental diagnostic of baryonic matter distribution within dark matter halos and the baryon cycle. While its cosmic value is well constrained, the baryon content within halos on nearly all scales is significantly lower than the cosmic mean; this is called the ``missing baryon problem.'' Using the high spatial, mass, and temporal resolutions of the NewCluster simulation, we investigate the baryon fraction evolution by tracing halo assembly histories from merger trees and gas tracer particles. We identify three distinct evolutionary phases: an early growth phase driven by cold accretion in low-mass halos, a suppression phase likely dominated by supernova feedback, and a recovery phase in massive halos enabled by deeper potential wells and hot-mode accretion. We further find that the redshift dependence of baryon fraction, particularly in low-mass halos, is influenced by the thermal state of the intergalactic medium, with suppression emerging after the surrounding gas becomes persistently hotter than the halo virial temperature. In addition, the scatter in baryon fraction at fixed halo mass correlates with the large-scale environment, with baryon-rich halos preferentially residing closer to filamentary structures. Overall, our results highlight that baryon fraction evolution is governed by the interplay between feedback and environment, requiring a time-resolved perspective on the baryon cycle.

papers.title: AIRoA-0: Long-Horizon, Precise, Cross-Embodiment Manipulation from Handheld Data
papers.abstract: AIRoA-0 (A-0) is a bimanual manipulation system learned from 16,151 hours of handheld demonstrations, with no robot data collected at any stage. The demonstrations are recorded with YUBI, our open-source handheld gripper, which lets people record manipulation data anywhere with no robot present. From a single instruction, A-0 sorts more than a dozen small parts into their numbered cells and changes the mop pads and brush of a robot vacuum; among other tasks, it unzips a pencil case and folds a towel. It performs these tasks using only a camera on each wrist, with no head or scene camera, at a site where none of its training data was recorded. Across the ten tasks of our evaluation, it averages a success rate of 78%, against 27% for the strongest of four other vision-language-action models post-trained on the same task demonstrations. We collect no teleoperation data and use no reinforcement learning or on-robot corrections, and the robot appears only at test time. The system learns which regions of each wrist view matter for the task, predicts the stage the task has reached, and decodes actions as a continuous stream. A-0 is embodiment-agnostic: it runs on robots that mount the YUBI gripper, such as a bimanual Franka, TX-G2, OpenArm and UR. We are releasing the dataset, to our knowledge the largest open dataset of handheld-gripper demonstrations with task and subtask instructions, together with the pre-trained weights and the post-training recipe. Videos of A-0 on every task are on the project page, https://a-0.airoa.io. Anyone can build the gripper, record a task of their own and post-train the model on it in under four hours on a single node of eight H200 GPUs.

papers.title: Data-Driven Spectrum Access Technologies for 6G
papers.abstract: The surge in global mobile traffic, driven by 5G adoption and emerging applications, necessitates new spectrum allocations for 6G systems. With most major swaths of spectrum below 15 GHz already allocated to other services, co-existence between cellular and incumbent services such as satellite or radar systems is critical to make such spectrum accessible for 6G. At the same time, the advent of artificial intelligence offers a new opportunity for designing more efficient spectrum sharing techniques. This paper presents four novel data-driven spectrum access techniques to enable efficient use of spectrum for the 6G era: 1) co-existence technique for efficient protection of fixed incumbent receivers within an established protection area; 2) data-driven approach for protecting satellite receivers via control of radiated power above the horizon; 3) spectrum sensing-based fast-time-scale physical resource block blanking; and 4) base station-based spectrum occupancy detection to enable fast-time-scale spectrum sharing with satellite and non-terrestrial network incumbents. These techniques leverage artificial intelligence and extreme multiple-input multiple-output capabilities to enable efficient spectrum co-existence/sharing while maintaining cellular network performance.

papers.title: Reconstruction of the conformal algebra from a critical groundstate on the (fuzzy) sphere
papers.abstract: Recently, we found a method to reconstruct the dilatation operator (sphere Hamiltonian) from a regulated conformal field theory groundstate. In this paper, we explore methods to construct the whole global conformal algebra, and test our construction using fuzzy sphere regularization. Starting from a groundstate of the same Hamiltonian, these methods perform better than constructions of the conformal generators based on a Hamiltonian density, are model-independent, require no additional tuning, and improve with system size. One purpose of reconstructing the conformal algebra is to identify conformal primary states, which we do with some success. We also find further evidence supporting the model of the short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian proposed earlier and use it to make systematic improvements.

papers.title: H 0557$-$385: A Candidate Missing Link Between Radio-Quiet Seyferts and Young Radio Galaxies
papers.abstract: The Seyfert 1 galaxy H 0557$-$385 (z = 0.034) has long been classified as radio-quiet on the basis of its radio-to-optical flux ratio, yet its radio properties are physically inconsistent with this designation. We present a broadband ($0.076 - 258.8$ GHz) radio spectral analysis combining new Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) observations with archival Murchison Widefield Array (MWA), Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) and Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) data. The spectrum requires a two-component model: a compact, self-absorbed component with a stratified gigahertz-peaked (GPS)/high-frequency-peaked (HFP) spectral shape (turnover at $9.4^{+0.6}_{-0.5}$ GHz), superposed on an extended, optically thin power-law lobe ($α_{\rm pl} = -0.78$) that dominates below ~1.6 GHz. The derived parameters $-$ a source size of ~15 pc, an equipartition magnetic field of 2.8 mG, a synchrotron age of $\lesssim1.8\times10^{3}$ yr, and a time-averaged jet power of ${\sim}5\times10^{41}$ $-$ $5\times10^{44}$ erg s$^{-1}$ $-$ are characteristic of compact steep-spectrum and GPS young radio galaxies, not of canonical radio-quiet AGN. The two-component structure admits two interpretations that the present data cannot distinguish: the extended emission may be the growing lobe of a genuinely young, expanding radio galaxy, or relic plasma from an earlier episode of a transient or recurrent jet. Under either, H 0557$-$385 is better understood as an intermediate object: optically a Seyfert, but with the radio-physical properties of a newly ignited or recently re-triggered radio galaxy. It is therefore a candidate missing link between radio-quiet AGN and large-scale radio galaxies. Distinguishing these scenarios will require high-resolution imaging and multi-epoch monitoring

papers.title: Towards Self-consistent Modeling of Quasi-Stars and their NLTE Spectra: Implications for Little Red Dots
papers.abstract: Quasi-stars, massive envelopes surrounding rapidly accreting black hole (BH) seeds, are promising candidates for explaining the rapid formation of supermassive black holes in the early Universe and may account for some of the JWST-discovered Little Red Dots (LRDs). We present a self-consistent framework combining stellar evolution calculations with non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) spectral synthesis to test this connection. Our models drop the polytropic assumptions of previous work: the envelope is described entirely by mixing-length theory, with saturated convection and radiative energy setting the luminosity at an inner boundary a few hundred Schwarzschild radii from the BH. This removes the BH-mass limits of earlier models, and we follow the evolution up to BH-to-total mass ratios approaching unity. We then use TLUSTY to compute the first converged NLTE atmospheric models for the surface conditions and primordial hydrogen-helium composition expected in quasi-stars. Our models produce cool photospheres, prominent Balmer breaks, and Balmer and Paschen absorption features. NLTE effects substantially modify line strengths, increasing Balmer absorption depths by $\sim 35-55\%$ relative to LTE models, while having a minor effect on the continuum. Comparison with observed LRD spectral energy distributions shows broad agreement in continuum shape, although our models do not reproduce their commonly observed strong emission lines. Under the quasi-star interpretation, comparisons with individual LRDs suggest characteristic quasi-star masses of approximately $10^5-10^7 M_\odot$. These results establish a physically motivated connection between quasi-star evolution and observable spectra, providing a framework for testing quasi-stars as progenitors of LRDs while identifying limitations of current atmospheric models.

papers.title: X-rays from Low-mass Active Galaxies in the Galaxy And Mass Assembly (GAMA) Survey
papers.abstract: We present new Chandra observations of seven broad-line AGNs in low-mass galaxies ($M_\star < 5 \times 10^9\,M_\odot$) selected from the GAMA sample of Salehirad et al. (2022). X-ray emission is detected in six galaxies, with luminosities spanning $\log(L_{\rm 0.5-8\,keV}/{\rm erg\,s^{-1}})\approx40.5$--43.8. Their X-ray luminosities generally exceed predictions for X-ray binary populations, and their proximity to the optical galaxy nuclei favors accreting massive black holes as the dominant emission source. Spectral fits for four sources yield photon indices $Γ\approx1.7$--2.2, with little evidence for intrinsic absorption in most cases. Virial black hole masses and hard X-ray bolometric corrections imply nominal Eddington ratios $λ_{\rm Edd}\approx0.004$--1.1, although uncertainties are substantial. Optical tracers generally imply higher bolometric luminosities and Eddington ratios, particularly for the X-ray-undetected galaxy. The X-ray-bright sources are broadly consistent with optical AGN scaling relations involving H$α$ and [O III], whereas most lie below the established X-ray--mid-infrared relation, potentially reflecting host-galaxy contamination. Four sources are consistent with the expected UV-to-X-ray spectral slope relation, while three show evidence for relative X-ray weakness. These results reveal diverse X-ray properties among broad-line AGNs in low-mass galaxies and highlight the importance of multiwavelength diagnostics for understanding black hole accretion and interpreting broad-line AGN candidates at high redshift.

papers.title: He I $λ$10830 Resonant Scattering in M17: Toward a Diagnostic of Optical Depth and Gas Kinematics
papers.abstract: The lower level of the He I $λ$10830 transition is metastable and therefore well populated. In H II regions, the line can become optically thick, and its photons then undergo resonant scattering. Draine (2026) predicted that scattering splits the profile into several peaks. We present Magellan/WINERED spectra ($R \approx 70{,}000$) at six pointings along a line from the ionizing source CEN 1 across the southwestern bar of M17, with He I $λ$10830 and Pa$γ$ in the same exposures. Every He I $λ$10830 profile is multi-peaked, while the Pa$γ$ profiles are single-peaked. Because Pa$γ$ does not undergo resonant scattering, it traces gas kinematics; its single peak argues against a purely kinematic origin of the He I peaks, and the shared exposures exclude an instrumental origin. We therefore attribute the He I peaks to resonant scattering, as predicted. We compare the profiles quantitatively with the static, spherically symmetric models of Draine (2026), using width and asymmetry measures independent of the systemic velocity. At two pointings far from CEN 1, no static model of any optical depth reproduces width and asymmetry together: both profiles are more red-weighted than static models of comparable width. Such profiles cannot arise from uniform motion but are expected from scattering in expanding gas. We argue that the profile is shaped by both the kinematics and the optical depth of the He$^{+}$ zone, and resolved He I $λ$10830 profiles could therefore provide a new diagnostic of these properties in H II regions.

papers.title: Coexisting Kondo and Weyl-like transport in kagome heavy-fermion metal, Yb$_y$Co$_3$G$e_{3-x}$Sn$_x$
papers.abstract: Strong electron correlations and topology offer complementary routes to controlling electrical conduction, as correlations can make electrons heavy (e.g. Kondo lattices) whereas topology can make them behave as massless particles (e.g. Dirac or Weyl systems), and having both in one material is rare. In Kondo lattice systems, Kondo hybridization between localized 4$f$ and conduction electrons strongly enhances the quasiparticle mass, where in Weyl-Kondo systems these Kondo-renormalized bands form Weyl states, and simultaneous signs of both Kondo and Weyl states in one material have not been observed in transport. Here we report signs of both in the kagome metal \ce{Yb_yCo3Ge_{3-x}Sn_x} by combining magnetotransport, heat capacity, magnetization, angle-resolved and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy, and DFT+U calculations to reveal Yb-dependent Kondo scattering developing into lattice coherence, with extrapolated Sommerfeld coefficient of approximately 2 ~Jmol$_{\mathrm{Yb}}^{-1}$K$^{-2}$. Transverse magnetoresistance (MR) follows single-ion Kondo scaling, whereas longitudinal transport contains an additional negative response proportional to B$^2$ and remains unsaturated up to 32 T, consistent with a chiral anomaly. These findings support a picture of Kondo and Weyl-like conduction arising from distinct electronic states without external Fermi-level tuning, suggesting a possible route to combining correlated and topological functionality in a bulk material.

papers.title: Conjugate radius and parabolicity along the Ricci flow
papers.abstract: We study the behaviour of the conjugate radius under the Ricci flow on complete noncompact manifolds. We show that if $(M^n,g(t))_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a complete Ricci flow with nonnegative scalar curvature at $t=0$, the initial metric is parabolic and not Ricci-flat, and the Einstein tensor $\mathrm{Ric}-\tfrac12 Rg$ is bounded above, then parabolicity is preserved along the flow and the conjugate radius of $g(t)$ is finite for every $t\in(0,T]$. As an application, we prove that a complete noncompact gradient shrinking Ricci soliton whose volume growth is subquadratic, in the sense that $\liminf_{r\to\infty}\Vol(B(p,r))/r^2=0$, has finite conjugate radius.

papers.title: A lattice construction of the Kormos-Runkel-Watts defect flows in minimal models
papers.abstract: Kormos, Runkel, and Watts (KRW) showed that a topological defect of a diagonal minimal model $M(p,p+1)$, perturbed by a weakly relevant defect field, flows to a new conformal interface. We study the flow of the $(2,1)$ Verlinde defect $D_{(2,1)}$ driven by the spinful defect field $φ_{(1,3)}\otimes\barφ_{(3,3)}$ on the lattice. The flow preserves the $(r,1)$ Verlinde lines. This preserved symmetry makes a dilute RSOS realisation possible. We study this flow numerically using both exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG). At $p=4$, the flow ends on the invertible line $η=D_{(3,1)}$. At $p=5$ it ends on a non-trivial conformal interface $C_5$ with $g=1.503(2)$ and transmission coefficient $T=0.665(10)$. We report its spectrum, leading irrelevant dimension, and lattice $β$-function. Gauging $η$ maps $C_5$ to an interface of the three-state Potts model, which breaks $\mathbb{Z}_3$ but is a stable interface once the Fibonacci line $τ_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ and charge conjugation are imposed. A loop-model formulation allows us to follow the family $C_p$ at continuous $4\le p\le5$: it moves smoothly from $C_5$ to $η$ as we lower $p$.

papers.title: A Tutorial on Shape Servoing of Deformable Objects-Part II: Advanced Concepts
papers.abstract: In robotics, shape control, or shape servoing, refers to the automatic manipulation of a deformable object toward a desired shape. This article is the second of a two-part tutorial on data-driven, Jacobian-based shape control, in which the deformation Jacobian, a local model of how robot motion changes the measured shape, is estimated from measurements. Part I built the shape-servoing loop and derived a local stability condition. This paper starts by using the singular value decomposition of the deformation Jacobian to identify shape changes that can be produced by small robot motions, those that require large robot motions, and those that are locally unavailable. It then analyses how the choice of shape features determines how the controller regulates the object's shape and, therefore, how much the object deforms on its way to the target. It then describes three ways in which the shape control loop can fail: loss of controllability, loss of observability, and occurrence of mechanical instabilities. It closes with shape-control extensions to time-varying targets, secondary tasks, and three-dimensional objects.

papers.title: Rethinking Next-Visit Diagnosis Prediction Beyond Aggregate Metrics: Retrieval--Memory Multi-Agent Adjudication
papers.abstract: Next-visit diagnosis prediction forecasts the diagnoses documented at a patient's next encounter, turning retrospective electronic health records into prospective clinical prediction. However, conventional aggregate evaluation obscures its multifaceted nature: distributionally, models must handle variable-size diagnosis sets and long-tailed labels; temporally, they must distinguish persistent, newly recorded, and recurrent diagnoses; and both vary with observed history depth. We introduce an evaluation framework along these dimensions and apply it to rule-based heuristics, LLM-based prompting, retrieval, memory, and multi-agent approaches. This reveals that repeating the last visit outperforms most LLM-based approaches overall despite predicting no new or recurrent diagnoses, and that retrieval and memory exhibit distinct profiles whose relative strengths vary across temporal transitions and backbones. Motivated by this, we propose LONGINUS, a retrieval-memory multi-agent adjudication framework combining evidence retrieved from patient records with structured memory of the patient trajectory. Using cross-view agreement as a reliability heuristic, it preserves shared predictions and adjudicates disagreements without revealing their source. Across MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV with four LLM backbones, LONGINUS achieves the best transition-specific performance among LLM-based methods in nearly all settings while remaining competitive with them on aggregate metrics.

papers.title: From off-shell strings to entropy flows
papers.abstract: Bit threads express holographic entropy as the maximal flux of a divergenceless vector field subject to a local capacity bound, but do not identify a physical carrier of that flux. In our previous work, we identified the projected string charge density with a bit-thread flow, reproduced the entropies of BTZ and ten-dimensional three-charge black holes, and showed that the maximal entropy flux is preserved under S- and T-dualities. However, the norm bound was imported from the bit-thread prescription, while the string-current configurations were prescribed along known bit-thread lines. In this paper, we give a stringy foundation for the local capacity and construct dynamical probe-string representatives of maximal flow. At genus zero and two-derivative order, the conical variation of the target-space action derived from the off-shell sphere fixes the string-frame entropy density. The gravitational replica construction and weighted flow-cut duality then yield the string-frame norm bound. We next find regular stationary F1 solutions in an NS-NS supported BTZ black hole whose spatial parts are logarithmic spirals. A uniform ensemble produces a conserved, constant-norm projected string charge density and realizes a maximal flow whose flux equals the BTZ entropy. We finally extend the construction to BTZ backgrounds with mixed NS-NS and RR flux. Varying the flux fraction changes the stationary F1 configurations at fixed metric and dilaton, while the corresponding conserved flows reproduce the same leading BTZ entropy. Thus, both the norm bound and its physical maximal-flow representative arise from string theory, with stationary strings providing physical channels for the entropic flux represented geometrically by bit threads.

papers.title: Estimating LuSEE-Night's Sensitivity to Cα Radio Recombination Lines
papers.abstract: Carbon radio recombination lines (CRRLs) arising from the cold neutral medium (CNM) of the interstellar medium are potential foregrounds in the 1-50 MHz band that LuSEE-Night will observe from the lunar far side. CRRLs are sensitive probes of the temperature, density, and radiation field of the CNM, and LuSEE-Night will provide sky-averaged measurements in a poorly explored frequency range. We model CRRLs across this band, accounting for doppler, collisional, and radiation broadening, and we estimate line strengths using two independent methods - fixing either the peak or the frequency-integrated optical depth - applied both uniformly across the sky and with region-dependent values informed by prior low-frequency observations. We simulate LuSEE-Night's expected response to these CRRLs and further convolve the beam-diluted spectra with LuSEE-Night's polyphase-filter-bank spectrometer response, including its zoomed-mode frequency resolution of $\sim$390 Hz, to obtain the expected observed brightness temperature. Using these simulated spectra, we estimate the integration time required to detect individual CRRLs at SNR=5 across the six sky models considered. Required integration times range from as short as 30 hours (in the most optimistic model where the optical depth across the sky is $\sim$10$^{-3}$) to 27.6 years (in the most conservative models where the optical depth across the sky is $\sim$10$^{-4}$). Stacking the 361 simulated C$α$ lines between 10 and 50 MHz reduces the integration time needed for an SNR=5 detection to $\sim$11 minutes and $\sim$151 hours respectively, indicating that LuSEE-Night has realistic chances of making a stacked detection of C$α$ RRLs within a realistic mission lifetime, even under the most conservative optical-depth assumptions.

papers.title: XMM-Newton and NuSTAR quasi-simultaneous follow-up of the very high energy flare of PKS~1725+123 in August 2025
papers.abstract: We report the results of the spectral timing analysis of the quasi-simultaneous X-ray follow-up with XMM-Newton ($50\,\rm ks$) and NuSTAR ($180\,\rm ks$) of the very high energy flare of the blazar PKS 1725+123 ($z=0.586$) in August of 2025. The X-ray monitoring started $\sim3$ days after the announcement of the VHE flare by LST-1, MAGIC and H.E.S.S. and lasted for almost 5 days. The high sensitivity of XMM-Newton reveals two spectral components, a soft ($Γ_{\rm X}>2$) and a hard ($Γ_{\rm X}<2$) power law. While the soft component dominates at $E<2\,\rm keV$, the hard component dominates at $E>2\,\rm keV$, likely marking the transition between the synchrotron and the high-energy emission, the "valley" of this blazar's spectral energy distribution. Within the XMM-Newton pointing ($\sim14$ hours) we witness the shift of the synchrotron component out of the X-ray band. In the following $\sim 4$ days, NuSTAR further reveals the brightening by a factor of 1.5 of the hard component, following the shift of the high-energy part of the SED into the X-ray band. Overall, within a week (observed frame) of the VHE flare, PKS 1725+123 went from temporarily being an intermediate synchrotron peaked blazar to transitioning back to its `normal' state of a low synchrotron peaked one. This is the first time that the evolution of a VHE flare from a blazar jet has been followed continuously in X-rays over such an extended period and our results highlight the importance of long-term quasi-simultaneous X-ray follow-up of VHE blazar flares.

papers.title: Bayesian Filters via the Stochastic Category
papers.abstract: We extend the categorical treatment of Bayesian filters to models with feedback, whose transitions and observations may depend on the past observations. We work in the stochastic category, whose objects are measurable spaces and whose morphisms are Markov kernels, which we refer to as stochastic morphisms. We systematically parameterize stochastic morphisms by a measurable space, and develop the calculus of conditioning in a notation intuitively compatible with classical probability theory, requiring neither string diagrams nor densities. A stochastic morphism into a product space is regarded as a parameterized family of joint laws, and its conditional law is again a stochastic morphism, so that the rules of conditioning become equalities of stochastic morphisms. We define the Bayesian inverse with respect to a parameterized prior and prove Bayesian coherence. A model with feedback is then a model whose parameter space grows with the observations, and we derive the Bayesian filter, prediction and smoothing for such models, with standard Borel hidden states and countably generated observation spaces. The affine Gaussian stochastic morphisms parameterized by a measurable space form a family strictly larger than the Markov category $\mathbf{Gauss}$, closed under composition and Bayesian inversion, in which we obtain the Kalman filter and the Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother with feedback.

papers.title: The Inverse Mean First-Passage Time Problem
papers.abstract: We consider the mean first-passage time $τ(x)$ for an overdamped particle in a one-dimensional potential landscape, and address the problem inverse to the textbook one: Given $τ(x)$ as a function of starting distance, we look for a potential that realizes it. We derive the conditions on $τ(x)$ under which such a potential exists. We show that while the power-law dependences $τ(x)\sim x^α$ with $α\leq 2$ may be realized by monotonic potentials, any realizable $τ(x)$ with superquadratic growth requires potential wells arbitrarily far from the target; $α= 2$ separates sliding from trapping-dominated motion regimes.

papers.title: El Agente Fármaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Computational drug discovery offers a growing range of tools for proposing and evaluating molecules, but combining them and deciding what to do next still requires substantial expert effort. Here, we introduce El Agente Fármaco, an AI scientist that uses modern large language model (LLM) technology to turn discovery goals expressed in everyday language into complex, scalable computational screening workflows. The agentic harness selects scientific tools, reviews their results, and adjusts subsequent steps to the target and the user's objectives. Our approach centers on a shared scientific memory: Fármaco Atlas, which stores molecules, structures, and results together with their provenance -- a record of how they were obtained. The agent uses targeted database queries to retrieve the evidence needed for each decision. A single request can launch calculations for an entire collection of molecules, without requiring a separate LLM decision for every compound. This design limits the information the model must process as screening collections grow, while keeping the underlying results available for inspection and further analysis. The integrated tools support molecule generation, prediction of binding and molecular properties, and searches for compounds available for purchase. In a retrospective comparison with an expert-led campaign, the agent proposed chemically distinct candidates with competitive docking scores and higher calculated drug-likeness under explicitly imposed selection criteria. In a 22-task benchmark against plain tool calls and Codex, the agent achieved the highest observed mean model-judged score, with lower median cumulative token use and peak context. Fármaco provides a foundation for flexible, scalable drug discovery workflows that connect scientific reasoning with an enduring, traceable record of computational work.

papers.title: Repulsion-Driven Topological Superconductivity in Twisted MoTe$_2$
papers.abstract: We show that a microscopic model of twisted MoTe$_2$ with screened Coulomb interactions produces topological superconductivity. Using the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) on infinite cylinders, we find that the narrow Chern band of twisted MoTe$_2$ has Cooper pair correlations that strengthen with cylinder circumference, consistent with two dimensional superconductivity. The superconductor has chiral $f$-wave pairing around the valley center, and its topology produces chiral Majorana edge modes and non-Abelian vortex cores. At zero displacement field, the superconductor spans fillings $-0.78\lesssimν\lesssim-0.72$, close to the experimental range, and extends in a dome to finite displacement field. We then predict how its stiffness evolves with the filling and the tunable displacement field. The interplay with screening length is also examined. Nearby, we find a fractional Chern insulator, a topological charge density wave, a metal, and a charge-ordered state. The last is a candidate for the reentrant integer Hall regime in experiments. These results establish a route from repulsive interactions in microscopic models of moiré materials to chiral topological uperconductors with chiral Majorana edge modes.

papers.title: Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging for Efficient Long-to-Short Reasoning
papers.abstract: Long-to-Short (L2S) model merging seeks to combine the strong reasoning capability of long chain-of-thought models with the concise style of base models, but existing methods that rely on linear interpolation and first-order activation statistics fail to capture how the loss landscape responds to parameter displacement, leading to degraded accuracy on hard tasks. We propose Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging (LHM), a training-free framework that replaces heuristic statistics with lightweight second-order curvature information. LHM consists of three components: (1) a low-rank Hessian approximation that efficiently estimates per-layer Hessian traces via Hutchinson's estimator on random inputs, eliminating the need for task-specific data; (2) a Layer Second-Order Sensitivity (LSOS) index that combines Hessian trace with task-vector norm to quantify per-layer fusion difficulty; and (3) a Dual-Constraint Coefficient Mapping (DCCM) that converts LSOS scores into layer-adaptive merge coefficients while jointly satisfying a fusion-error bound and a global length-reduction target. Experiments across six mathematical benchmarks on 1.5B and 7B models show that LHM outperforms state-of-the-art methods such as ACM-TIES and ORCA, achieving over 4\% accuracy gain and up to 93.1\% reduction in output length relative to the long-CoT model.

papers.title: One-Sided Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operators on Variable Lebesgue Spaces Beyond Log-Hölder Continuity
papers.abstract: We study the boundedness of the right-sided Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on variable Lebesgue spaces over the real line. Motivated by the $K_0$ condition for the classical Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator, we introduce a directional condition $K_0^+$ adapted to the geometry of the one-sided maximal operator. We characterize $K_0^+$ in terms of the uniform boundedness of a family of one-sided averaging operators and prove that it is a necessary condition for the boundedness of $M^+$ on $L^{p(\cdot)}(\mathbb{R})$. We also establish one-sided analogues of the modular and reverse Hölder estimates associated with the classical $K_0$ condition. These estimates constitute the main local ingredients in the proof of boundedness of $M^+$ under the combined assumptions $K_0^+$ and $N_\infty$.

papers.title: A Conditional Mutual Information Analysis of Response Variety in Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models provide a variety of responses at inference (generation) that conventionally depend on a temperature parameter. Using a conditional mutual information approach, a quantitative, entropy based analysis of response variety is given. Three limiting behaviors are defined: arbiter, independent (conditionally) and neutral (deterministic) that span no to maximal mutual information. We give examples of each behavior and suggest their application to: temperature analysis, language analysis, prompt compression, and knowledge graphs.

papers.title: Lattice spin systems coupled to a compact U(1) gauge field with negative gauge coupling favoring frustration
papers.abstract: We investigate the phase diagram and nature of the phase transitions of three-dimensional compact lattice Abelian Higgs models with negative gauge coupling. These models describe multicomponent complex scalar fields coupled to a compact U(1) gauge field. Negative gauge coupling favors frustrated plaquette configurations, competing with the tendency of the matter ferromagnetic-like interaction to suppress frustration. Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analyses of models with one- and two-component scalar fields of unit charge reveal a substantially richer phase structure than at nonnegative gauge coupling. For two components, the O(3) transition line associated with gauge-invariant bilinear ordering extends into the negative-coupling region, and turns into a first-order transition line with decreasing $K$, toward the fully-frustrated $K\to -\infty$ limit. An analogous first-order transition line is also found for the one-component scalar matter with negative gauge coupling. Both one- and two-component models exhibit two additional continuous transition lines at sufficiently large matter coupling. Their energy-cumulant scaling is consistent with three-dimensional Ising and XY critical exponents, suggesting topological transitions in the $\mathbb Z_2$ and XY gauge universality classes, respectively. These results uncover additional phases generated by the competition between matter ordering and dynamical gauge frustration, whose physical characterization remains an open question.

papers.title: A King for Almost Everyone
papers.abstract: A tournament is an orientation of a complete graph. A vertex $v$ controls a vertex $u\neq v$ if there is a directed path of length at most two from $v$ to $u$, and a $δ$-king is one that controls at least $δ(n-1)$ vertices. In the query complexity model, each query reveals the orientation of an edge. Shen, Sheng and Wu [SICOMP'03] established an $Ω(n^{4/3})$ lower bound on the deterministic query complexity of finding a $1$-king, and a non-matching upper bound of $O(n^{3/2})$. Neither bound has been improved in over two decades, despite substantial progress on variants of the problem. For $δ$-kings with $δ< 1$, Biswas, Jayapaul, Raman and Satti [Discrete Applied Mathematics'22] showed that $O(n^{4/3})$ queries suffice to find a $\frac12$-king. Lachish, Reidl and Trehan [FSTTCS'22] improved this guarantee to $\frac12+\frac{2}{17}$ using $\widetilde{O}(n^{4/3})$ queries, and asked whether a larger fraction could be achieved within the same query bound. We answer this question affirmatively for every fixed fraction below one: for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, we give a deterministic algorithm that finds a $(1-\varepsilon)$-king using $O(n^{4/3})$ queries. The design of our algorithm is informed by a structural analysis combining a sparse regularity lemma due to Allen, Kohayakawa, Mota and Parente [Electronic Journal of Combinatorics'14] with a new sampling argument based on a reachability theorem of Afek, Gafni and Linial [arXiv'19].

papers.title: PianoBench: Evaluating Musical Perception and Reasoning in Language Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal language models continue to improve on broad music understanding benchmarks, but which musical features can they perceive and reason about? We investigate this question by introducing PianoBench, a benchmark that tasks language models with reasoning about musical performances across congruent acoustic and symbolic input representations. PianoBench is derived from our new multimodal, training-scale dataset comprising more than 20,000 hours of interleaved transcripts of music and spoken musical commentary from instructional piano videos. Open-weight audio-language models achieve at most 52.8% accuracy on PianoBench, and at best only modestly outperform their accuracy on a no-audio control. In contrast, frontier models using chain of thought achieve up to 93.2% accuracy when provided transcripts of music as text, exposing a gap between perceiving musical features from audio and reasoning about musical events when they are given explicitly. We then test whether mid-training on interleaved musical instruction can improve question answering without chain of thought, raising Qwen 3.5 9B Base's zero-shot accuracy on PianoBench with music transcripts from 42.8% to 56.0% after instruction tuning. These experiments suggest that instructional videos may represent an overlooked source of multimodal supervision for music. Available: https://gclef-cmu.org/pianobench.

papers.title: Solutions of the space-fractional heat equation with polynomial growth: Liouville theorems and Schauder estimates
papers.abstract: With the aim of extending to parabolic equations the framework developed by the first three authors in [Dipierro, Savin, and Valdinoci, Rev. Mat. Iberoam. (2019)], we introduce a notion of (viscosity) solutions for the space-fractional heat equation modulo $k$. In turn, we are able to define $s$-caloric functions with polynomial growth at infinity, showing also related Schauder estimates, a Liouville-type result, and a stability property with respect to the $L^\infty_{\rm{loc}}$-convergence.

papers.title: Evolved Spiking Neural Networks for EEG Seizure Detection: Calcium Dynamics and Delay Mechanics
papers.abstract: Neuroevolution can discover compact network designs that are hard to specify by hand. The EONS framework evolves the topology, weights, thresholds and delays of neuromorphic spiking networks without gradients. We tested whether giving integrate-and-fire (IF) neurons an activity-dependent calcium current (Ca-IF neurons) improves evolved networks for EEG seizure detection, with calcium parameters fixed, shared across a network, or evolved for each neuron. On 10 held-out CHB-MIT patients never seen in training, per-neuron calcium raised the record-level Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) from 0.592 to 0.726 over 20 independent runs (p = 0.008) and lowered the false-alarm rate from 0.17 to 0.10. Fixed or per-network calcium gave no significant benefit. IF networks with evolved synaptic delays of 1-3 ticks gave a similar gain (p = 0.005), whereas axonal delays did not. On Siena, with unchanged settings, per-neuron calcium gained +0.096 MCC over IF in one patient-disjoint split (p = 0.011) and +0.059 in the other (p = 0.052). These results suggest that calcium and delays may make the evolutionary search more effective, and motivate testing on more data and in neuromorphic hardware.

papers.title: Possibility of Potts Spin-Ice in Rare Earth Twisted-Kagome Layers: an Example of DyAgGe
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spin-ice compounds, predominantly based on the pyrochlore or spinel structure, have been attracting considerable interest in the last two decades. A two-dimensional (2D) analogue is the spin-ice consisting of kagome planes. So far, only Ising spin ice has been discovered in any material, and only one 2D material, the kagome compound HoAgGe, has been identified as a spin ice. In this Letter, we show that another rare-earth twisted Kagome magnetic compound, DyAgGe, is in fact a Potts spin ice (or color ice), where at each site not two but four spin directions are allowed. We argue that an 8-state spin ice may also exist in this class of systems. We present a first-principles calculation of magnetic interactions in DyAgGe, and confirm the 4-state Potts structure of this material by matching our model predictions with the available experimental data.

papers.title: The Iterated Local Transitivity Model for oriented graphs
papers.abstract: Transitivity in social and other complex networks describes the tendency for two nodes with a common neighbor to become adjacent. We propose a new model for complex networks based on transitivity, called the Iterated Local Transitivity Model for Oriented Graphs (ILTO). The model generalizes the Iterated Local Model for Tournaments (ILMT). As in ILMT, oriented graphs are generated iteratively by cloning nodes and their adjacencies, with arcs between clones oriented either as the corresponding arcs between their parents or in the reverse direction. This process produces dense oriented graphs and, under suitable conditions, graphs with high connectivity and small diameter. We analyze the universality properties of ILTO, showing that, for generating sequences with infinite support, the base oriented graph determines which oriented graphs appear as induced subgraphs, unlike in ILMT. We study motifs in ILTO and show that when the base graph is a tournament and the generating sequence has infinite support, the model generates quasirandom tournament sequences. Finally, we study domination numbers, the cop number, and the dichromatic number. We bound the cop number in terms of the independence number of the base graph and show that, for each fixed base graph, the dichromatic number is $Θ(2^t)$ after $2t$ consecutive 0-steps.

papers.title: Probabilistic Steering of Generative Priors for Lab-in-the-Loop Antibody Optimization
papers.abstract: Therapeutic antibody development is often framed as comprising two discrete stages: initial discovery of novel binders followed by iterative optimization to refine these hits into therapeutic-grade molecules. Models and methods often reflect these stages, with generative structure models applied to discovery and probabilistic black-box optimization methods applied to refinement. Here we propose to unify these stages by smoothly transitioning a generative discovery model into iterative optimization, allowing the handoff between the structure-based prior and supervision from wet lab data to be guided by the posterior uncertainty of a probabilistic surrogate. We show that this yields improvements in optimization efficiency in the low-N regime, as well as improved diversity amongst the optimized molecules.

papers.title: Entanglement-Aware Quantum Circuit Optimization through Globally Optimal Partitioning
papers.abstract: We introduce a scalable framework for globally optimal quantum-circuit partitioning and entanglement-aware block resynthesis. The partitioning problem is formulated as an integer linear program over qubit-feasible convex subcircuits, supporting objectives such as minimizing the number of partitions or a weighted execution cost. The resulting partition selection is exact over the enumerated feasible candidates and their computed costs when the ILP is solved to proven optimality. The selected partitions are resynthesized using an operator-Schmidt rank (OSR) based synthesis technique, which exploits their internal entanglement structure. We compare the end-to-end integer linear programming (ILP)--OSR workflow with BQSKit while identifying their different routing methods, and separately compare local OSR and BQSKit synthesis on matched three- and four-qubit unitaries. On the frozen sample of 772 local unitary targets, OSR produces 741 verified syntheses versus 617 for BQSKit, and matches or improves the CNOT count in all 617 jointly verified pairs. These results demonstrate that globally optimal partition selection combined with entanglement-aware resynthesis improves circuit quality and extends block-based optimization to problem sizes that are impractical for existing optimization workflows.

papers.title: SS 433 Eastern Jet Turbulence Revealed by Spatially-Resolved IXPE Data Analysis
papers.abstract: The extended X-ray jet (EXJ) of SS 433/W50 shows hard X-ray and very-high-energy gamma-ray emission, indicating strong particle acceleration, likely sensitive to the EXJ magnetic field structure and turbulence. To study this field, we re-analyze the 2023 Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) observation of the eastern EXJ using the publicly available polarization fitting package LeakageLib. Compared with standard PCUBE and spectropolarimetric analyses, this approach improves the polarization constraints and enables spatially resolved polarization measurements. Dividing the EXJ into head, spine, and sheath regions with independent polarization properties, we find significant (>3 sigma) improvement over a single-zone model. The sheath exhibits lower polarization than the head and spine, while the electric vector position angles are consistent across all regions, indicating magnetic fields aligned with the jet axis. The measurements imply enhanced magnetic turbulence at the jet boundary, potentially driven by Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities.

papers.title: Combination Theorems and the Farrell--Jones Conjecture for Graph Products of Pairs
papers.abstract: We study the Farrell--Jones conjecture for graph products of pairs and for fundamental groups of polyhedral products. We introduce a pair-deletion decomposition and a local notion of FJ-admissibility, and prove a vertexwise combination theorem for graph products of pairs. The criterion applies, in particular, to ordinary graph products, free-factor pairs, suitable normal pairs, and classes controlled by acylindrical Bass--Serre actions. For polyhedral products, we combine these results with their description by relative graph products and graph products of pairs. We also obtain bounds and exact computations for amenable category, together with applications to simplicial volume and Borel rigidity of closed aspherical polyhedral-product manifolds.

papers.title: Evidence for strong shocks in the ISM of small radio sources
papers.abstract: Radio jets deposit energy into the interstellar medium of their host galaxies, and while a jet is still confined within the host it is expected to drive shocks through the gas. Broad [OIII] 5007 profiles trace ionized gas that has been disturbed, the [OI]/H-alpha versus [OIII]/H-beta diagram helps distinguish gas photoionized by an AGN from gas excited by shocks, and the high ionization [NeV] 3426 line traces the hard UV continuum of the accretion disk, which shocks only reproduce at very high velocities. We have selected two samples of radio-loud AGN from a cross-match of the VLA Sky Survey with DESI Data Release 1, at 0.15 < z < 0.5 and with [OI] 6300 detected at > 5-sigma: one with projected radio sizes of 10-15 kpc, whose jets are still inside the host, and one with sizes greater than 25 kpc, whose jets have broken out. We fit the [OIII] and [OI] profiles, measure W80, and classify each source on the BPT diagram. The confined sources have broader [OIII] lines, sit systematically closer to the LINER region, and are detected less often in [NeV], and the [NeV] difference is not explained by redshift or dust. The broad components are not systematically blueshifted, so the confined sources are distinguished by line width rather than by outflow velocity. We then discuss how these results indicate that the jets of the confined sources are driving strong shocks through the interstellar medium of their hosts.

papers.title: LaplaceDiag: Fault Diagnosis through Changes in Learned Actuator Effects
papers.abstract: Identifying faulty components from sensor anomalies is difficult because fault effects can propagate through a plant and different faults can produce similar observations. Detailed component models and labeled fault examples may also be unavailable. We introduce LaplaceDiag, a data-driven method that uses changes in actuator effects to narrow the search for faulty equipment. Actuators act on specific devices and mechanisms, so their changed effects can provide clues to root causes. LaplaceDiag learns a healthy plant model with LaplaceNet, a neural network that operates in Laplace space. It separates nonlinear prediction based on measured history from an explicit matrix that describes how actuator values affect sensor values. Keeping the history predictor fixed allows current actuator effects to be estimated by linear regression without retraining the neural network. Comparison with a healthy reference accounts for estimation uncertainty and normal variation to detect changes and generate actuator-related diagnostic hypotheses. The method supports online and offline diagnosis, providing an intermediate step between anomaly detection and identifying faulty components. We successfully evaluate LaplaceDiag on two datasets.

papers.title: RoboScope Kit: Unified Interfaces for Fast and Scalable Embodied-AI Evaluation
papers.abstract: Simulation benchmarks are the standard way to compare robot policies, but each benchmark brings its own evaluator, observation layout, and action convention, and evaluation is slow: 500 RoboTwin Easy episodes with one simulator and one model on one GPU take 359.7 minutes. Profiling the official StarVLA evaluator shows that simulation occupies CPU cores while the GPU averages 14.3% utilization. RoboScope Kit wraps each model once in a Python class called a Policy, and each benchmark once in an adapter around the benchmark's own evaluator, so the benchmark's rules and scoring stay unchanged. Scheduling runs simulator workers and Policy replicas as separate pools, sizes both from measured probes, and shards work deterministically across GPU instances; runtime optimization renders only the observations an action-chunk Policy reads. Adapters cover six benchmark families. On LIBERO-Long with a StarVLA checkpoint on one 48 GiB RTX 4090, the concurrency search selects twelve simulator workers sharing three Policy replicas, which evaluate 500 episodes 4.45$\times$ faster than the official StarVLA evaluation with equivalent success rates, 2.78$\times$ faster than RLinf, and 1.52$\times$ faster than vla-eval at its tuned configuration. With CUDA MPS, which lets the replicas run their kernels concurrently, the search selects sixteen workers sharing four replicas, 6.16$\times$ faster than StarVLA, 3.85$\times$ faster than RLinf, and 2.10$\times$ faster than vla-eval. On RoboTwin Easy, four GPUs with chunk-boundary observation complete the 500 episodes in 14.4 minutes, 25.04$\times$ faster than the single-GPU baseline, with identical success outcomes and terminal steps.

papers.title: High-fidelity quantum gate learning via physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: We propose a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach for high-fidelity quantum gate learning in both one- and two-qubit systems. We train a PINN using the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, where smooth control fields with fixed boundary conditions are obtained by minimizing a loss function that considers model dynamics, gate error, physical constraints, regularization terms, and multiple initial conditions. Training considers pairs of mutually unbiased bases, while independent validation combines Haar-random input states with the average gate fidelity. Unitary simulations yield an average gate infidelity of $8.49\times10^{-8}$ for Hadamard and values between $3.39\times10^{-7}$ and $4.96\times10^{-6}$ for controlled-NOT under $XX$, $YY$, and $ZZ$ interactions. We examine how the learned control fields depend on the coupling, training configuration, and available local fields, including five exchange-type dipolar scenarios. We test the learned control fields under the Lindblad master equation with dephasing and amplitude damping, theoretically reproducing the expected first-order fidelity loss in the weak-dissipation regime. Finally, boundary-adapted Chebyshev expansions represent 139 learned controls with a minimum common count of $K_\ast=24$ coefficients per control for all eleven family-averaged mean squared errors to fall below $10^{-6}$. Separately, square-pulse and Strang propagation at $K=30$ preserve all 31 continuous polynomial references within infidelity $10^{-5}$ at $N=128$ and all larger tested resolutions, under both sampling rules. These results connect multi-state gate synthesis, control-resource characterization, and compact square-pulse playback.

papers.title: Why Pay for Long Reasoning When Rewrite Do Trick? Causal Effects of Reasoning History Compaction on Future Generation and Agent Cost
papers.abstract: Reasoning substantially improves language models' ability to solve difficult problems, but long reasoning traces make these gains expensive. Efficient reasoning should express useful analysis in fewer tokens by reducing repetition and text that adds little value to solving the problem. Progress in proprietary models motivates this goal, yet their hidden scratchpads limit direct study of how it is achieved. We investigate whether open-weight models can generate less verbose reasoning by changing the form of their own earlier thoughts, without retraining. Our intervention rewrites prior reasoning into compact state records before pending tool results are revealed, then compares continuations from original and compact histories. Across the tested models, accepted compact histories usually shorten future reasoning; a coding case study also shows less repeated verification after a shared candidate solution. In software-agent deployments, compaction can reduce total spending, although task quality and rewrite-inclusive time depend on the target and compressor. These findings identify reasoning history as one way to reduce future reasoning-token use and motivate model-specific compaction policies evaluated for both efficiency and retained capability.

papers.title: Performance, Scalability and Maintenance: An Experimental Study of RPA vs. Autonomous Agents in the Healthcare Domain
papers.abstract: Healthcare information systems are fragmented, and retrieving data from legacy web portals is a recurrent need. Robotic Process Automation (RPA) is deterministic but sensitive to interface changes, whereas autonomous agents based on large language models (Agent Process Automation, APA) promise adaptability at a higher computational cost. Following Design Science Research, we developed and compared an RPA solution (Playwright) and an APA solution (browser-use, LangGraph and Gemini 2.5 Flash-lite) to retrieve mammography and breast ultrasound reports from a laboratory portal, treating reports solely as informational artifacts. Across two rounds (T and T+7), RPA reached 98.90% accuracy and 98.27% F1-score versus 96.49% and 94.48% for APA, was about 13 times faster (16.07 s vs. 207.21 s per patient) and cost about six times less per report (USD 0.030 vs. 0.187). Both reached 100% step success rates; APA varied more over time. For a stable interface, RPA was superior.
authors: Ana Paula Wernz da Cunha Müller

papers.title: Towards Effective Fuzzing of EDK2 Components
papers.abstract: Securing bootloaders is critical to establishing the trusted computing base of modern systems. TianoCore's edk2, the de facto UEFI-based bootloader, is widely deployed but has recently been shown to contain numerous high-severity vulnerabilities. Existing approaches either focus on post-boot interfaces or rely on heavyweight simulation, limiting their scalability, throughput, and coverage of boot-time components. We present Metis, an automated technique for fuzzing edk2 protocols (i.e., boot-time interfaces) by rehosting them as user-space applications. Our key insight is that effective fuzzing must exercise not only protocol interfaces but also their dependency interactions, which serve as additional input channels. Metis employs a Direct-dependency Component Rehosting (DCR)-based strategy to construct semantically meaningful mocks for dependencies, enabling controlled input injection across all channels. It further leverages a hybrid approach combining static analysis and Large Language Model (LLM)-guided synthesis to generate and refine fuzzing harnesses. We implement Metis on the Host Based Firmware Analyzer (HBFA) framework and evaluate it on 60 drivers covering 162 protocols. Metis achieves 73.1% coverage, approximately 1.7 times higher than FuzzUEr, the state-of-the-art edk2 fuzzing technique, and discovers 137 previously unknown bugs. We have already reported 26 of them, including 12 that are remotely triggerable, and all reported vulnerabilities have been acknowledged by the vendors.

papers.title: A surface-group action on real-hyperbolic space with no Cannon--Thurston map
papers.abstract: We present discrete, faithful and purely loxodromic representations of a closed surface group of genus 431, and of a free group, into the group of isometries of a finite-dimensional real-hyperbolic space for which no Cannon--Thurston map exists. The construction combines three ingredients: the small-cancellation strategy employed by Baker--Riley to construct a subgroup of an ambient hyperbolic group with no Cannon--Thurston map, the realization of these groups by octagon complexes, and a theorem of Desgroseilliers--Haglund that supplies a convex cocompact faithful representation of the ambient hyperbolic group on a real-hyperbolic space. These examples admit ray Cannon--Thurston maps, as defined by Halder, Mahan Mj and Sardar.

papers.title: A Unified Perspective on Poincaré and Galilei Relativity: II. General Relativity: A. Kinematics
papers.abstract: Building on the first paper in this series (Paper~I), a unified perspective on Poincaré and Galilei physics in a 5-dimensional spacetime setting is further pursued by consideration of the kinematics of general relativity, with the gravitational dynamics to be addressed separately. The metric of the 5-dimensional affine spacetimes governed by the Bargmann groups considered in Paper~I (central extensions of the Poincaré and Galilei groups) is generalized to curved spacetime by extending the usual 1+3 (traditionally `3+1') formalism of general relativity on 4-dimensional spacetime to a 1+3+1 formalism, whose spacetime kinematics is shown to be consistent with that of the usual 1+3 formalism. Spacetime tensor laws governing the motion of an elementary classical material particle and the dynamics of a simple fluid are presented, along with their 1+3+1 decompositions; these reference the foliation of spacetime in a manner that partially reverts the Einstein perspective (accelerated fiducial observers, and geodesic material particles and fluid elements) to a Newton-like perspective (geodesic fiducial observers, and accelerated material particles and fluid elements subject to a gravitational force). These spacetime laws of motion for particles and fluids also suggest that a strong-field Galilei general relativity would involve a limit in which not only $c \rightarrow \infty$, but also $G \rightarrow \infty$, such that $G / c^2$ remains constant.

papers.title: On uniqueness of probability solutions to one-dimensional Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equations
papers.abstract: We give new sufficient conditions for uniqueness of probability solutions to one-dimensional Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equations in the case where the drift coefficient depends on time.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform
papers.abstract: The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.

papers.title: A Family of Well-Behaved Multiflow Instances
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of cut-sufficient instances for undirected multiflow that generalizes single-source planar and fully-planar instances. We also show the family has an additive $6 d_{\max}$ error for converting a fractional flow into an unsplittable one.

papers.title: Factorized approximate inverse preconditioners in the tensor train format
papers.abstract: We present a preconditioning pipeline that accelerates Tensor Train (TT) linear solvers for symmetric positive-definite problems. Extending the Factorized Sparse Approximate Inverse framework to tensor networks, we construct a preconditioner as the product of a TT operator and its transpose. This formulation is positive semidefinite for any bond dimension and truncation, and definite whenever the factor is non-singular, satisfying the mathematical requirements of the Conjugate Gradient method. We detail the construction of this preconditioner and its integration into Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG)-like linear solvers. Performance evaluations show consistent iteration reductions for anisotropic diffusion and Poisson problems across various configurations, leading to net speedups of up to 25% in ill-conditioned settings of time stepping schemes that can reuse the approximate inverses. These benchmarks were performed with the open-source Julia library DifferenTT.jl, which we also introduce in this work to provide out-of-the-box access to these preconditioned pipelines.

papers.title: Sharp Weighted Hardy-Trace Inequalities for Homogeneous Magnetic Potentials
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp magnetic improvement of the family of weighted inequalities on the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}^{N+1}_+$ that interpolate between the Hardy inequality and the trace Hardy inequality. The magnetic potentials are of Aharonov-Bohm type, $\mathbf{A}(x)=|x|^{-1}\boldsymbol{a}(x/|x|)$, where the tangential field $\boldsymbol{a}$ may be singular on a closed subset of the sphere. We compute the sharp constant explicitly: it is given by the constant of the corresponding nonmagnetic inequality, evaluated in a virtual dimension that depends on the first eigenvalue of the magnetic Laplacian on the sphere. In particular, the magnetic trace Hardy constant strictly exceeds its Euclidean value whenever this eigenvalue is positive. The proof rests on a ground state representation of the deficit, which also shows that the sharp constant is not attained in the energy space. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp Hardy inequality for the fractional powers $(-Δ_{\mathbf{A}})^σ$, $0<σ<1$, of the magnetic Laplacian: the constant is the same on smooth functions supported away from the singular set and on the form domain of $(-Δ_{\mathbf{A}})^σ$, and it is not attained. Examples include the planar Aharonov-Bohm potential with nonintegral flux and, in dimension three, the Aharonov-Bohm potential and the Dirac monopole.

papers.title: Predictive gains, causal losses: why interventional competence cannot be learned from data alone
papers.abstract: Retaining predictive gains can require persistent errors in a model's response to interventions. For deterministic predictors with finite second moments under squared-error loss, any observational advantage over the best predictor using only an outcome's direct causes requires dependence on other inputs, regardless of the learning rule. When admissible interventions vary inputs while preserving the worldly outcome, this dependence yields a positive lower bound on root-mean-square intervention-response error. We identify conditions under which population gradient updates introduce this dependence from a parent-only baseline or damage a previously correct mechanism through shared parameters while improving other predictions. These dependencies can also make model behavior vary with how the same intervention is realized. We characterize interventional alignment through a common output mapping across internal states and physical processes realizing the same intervention target and relevant context. Correction is limited by the causal hypotheses currently admitted within inquiry. The relevant hypothesis class comprises these causal alternatives, rather than the function class the computational system could in principle represent. For predictions restricted to these alternatives, interventional mean error cannot fall below the best approximation they permit, whether evidence is observational or interventional. Reducing error below a positive limit requires admitting better hypotheses, which may entail revising the causal variables, mechanism structure, or intervention interpretation. Interventional criticism constrains replacements without determining them. We conjecture that reliably acquiring and maintaining interventional competence when causal commitments fail requires autonomous participation in proposing alternatives, testing their consequences, and revising them in response to error.

papers.title: Dr. No: Feature Steering for Abstention in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Large foundation models often answer even when the available visual or textual evidence is insufficient to support a reliable conclusion. This failure to abstain makes them hard to trust in high-stakes or information-seeking settings, where a confident but unsupported answer can be worse than no answer at all. It also raises a natural question: can the internal mechanisms behind this behaviour be identified and controlled at inference time? We present Dr. No, a feature-steering approach that mines sparse autoencoder (SAE) features associated with abstention and commitment, then modulates a small set of them during the prefill pass, without retraining the base model. Dr. No is evaluated on LLaVA-1.6 Mistral 7B across multimodal abstention benchmarks, including UNK-VQA and MM-UPD, and additionally benchmarked on language reasoning tasks using Qwen3.5-2B on AbstentionBench subsets. Against multiple uncertainty-based abstention baselines, feature steering achieves a more favourable balance between correct answering and appropriate abstention than post-hoc rejection methods. The gains are strongest on UNK-VQA and on MM-UPD cases involving image--question or question--answer incompatibility, and transfer most clearly to mathematical reasoning subsets of AbstentionBench. However, performance is more limited on absent-answer detection and retrieval-heavy multi-hop QA, such as MuSiQue. These results suggest that sparse internal features provide lightweight control handles for shaping uncertainty-aware behaviour in foundation models, while also showing that abstention control is source-dependent rather than governed by a single universal signal.

papers.title: Statistical Stability and Linear Response for Suspension Measures under Base and Roof Perturbations
papers.abstract: We study the dependence of canonical invariant probability measures of suspension semiflows on simultaneous perturbations of the invariant base density and the roof function. We compare two natural representations of the suspension measure: physical-height coordinates, in which the support depends on the roof function, and normalised-height coordinates, in which all measures are defined on a fixed cylinder. In physical-height coordinates, we obtain an exact fibrewise formula for the $L^1$ discrepancy between suspension densities and derive quantitative total-variation estimates. In normalised-height coordinates, we establish corresponding stability estimates through the product of the base density and the roof function. These results transfer quantitative statistical-stability estimates for the base densities to the associated suspension measures. For one-parameter families whose base densities are differentiable in $L^1$ and whose roof functions are differentiable in $L^\infty$, we derive an $L^1$ linear-response formula on the fixed cylinder and a bounded-Lipschitz first-variation formula in physical height. The latter contains a signed measure supported on the graph of the unperturbed roof. We further compute the exact first-order total-variation speed and prove that total-variation differentiability holds if and only if the first-order roof velocity vanishes almost everywhere with respect to the unperturbed fibre density. The results are measure-theoretic and do not require spectral or mixing assumptions on the suspension semiflow.

papers.title: Interstellar and intergalactic medium in the ultraviolet band
papers.abstract: This article presents an overview of key scientific challenges in the astrophysics and astrochemistry of the interstellar and intergalactic media. Addressing many of these challenges will become possible with the Russian space observatory Spektr-UF, which is currently being prepared for launch. The ultraviolet (UV) spectral range is critically important for studying the evolution of the Universe, as it contains fundamental absorption and emission lines of most chemical elements and the most important molecules. These lines make it possible to reliably determine the physical conditions and chemical composition of various astrophysical objects, as well as the characteristics of the processes occurring within them. The article examines the prospects for UV observations across a broad range of scientific problems, from investigating the epoch of helium reionization and the thermal history of the Universe to mapping ongoing star formation in galaxies. Dedicated sections address the study of the chemical evolution of galaxies at intermediate redshifts, the distribution of "hidden" baryons and metals, the small-scale structure of interstellar clouds, the physics of photodissociation regions and protoplanetary disks, and the modeling of UV emission from nebulae surrounding fast-moving pulsars. The high sensitivity and spectral resolution of the Spektr-UF instruments are expected to provide fundamentally new data across all these research areas, filling existing gaps in our understanding of the interstellar and intergalactic media.

papers.title: Stationary distribution of active Brownian particles in a bounded domain
papers.abstract: Self-propelled particles such as swimming micro-organisms often accumulate at boundaries. Active Brownian particles (ABPs), that is, particles moving at constant speed with an orientation undergoing rotational diffusion, provide a simple model. ABPs have a finite probability to be on the boundary. Their probability density therefore includes both regular bulk and singular boundary components. Exchanges between these represent capture at the boundary and re-entry into the bulk. We examine the distribution of ABPs in the stationary regime. We first obtain a similarity solution that describes the probability density near the turning points, where orientation is tangential to the boundary and particles re-enter the bulk. This shows that the bulk density is singular and the boundary density is non-differentiable. We then add spatial diffusion to the ABP model and investigate the limit $\eps \to 0$ of small spatial diffusivity. We use matched asymptotics to describe the regularising effect of a finite $\eps$, focusing on the vicinity of the turning points. We assess our predictions against numerical simulations using both lattice Markov chain and finite-element discretisations.

papers.title: Curve-Supported Concentrations of Vortices and Screw Dislocations Subject to Confinement
papers.abstract: We study the concentration of logarithmically interacting defects, such as Ginzburg--Landau vortices and screw dislocations, on closed curves in two dimensions, subject to a confining field. We prove that a measure supported on a smooth closed curve solves the mean-field transport equation exactly when, in Lagrangian labels, the curve moves with the negative induced velocity and each label keeps its mass. This contour law is a gradient flow of the mean-field energy. We prove that the gradient of the energy on a curve has a leading term proportional to the operator $|D|$ with Fourier symbol $|k|$, which prevents every smooth equilibrium curve from being a local minimizer, in a gradient-flow analogue of the Kelvin--Helmholtz instability of vortex sheets. In a radially symmetric case with quadratic confinement, we find an explicit circular equilibrium whose linearization is diagonal in Fourier modes, and we show that, as $N\rightarrow \infty $, the linear spectrum of the regular $N$-gon converges, mode by mode, to that of the circle. Finally, we compute a critical point on two concentric circles with lower energy than the single circle, indicating a rich family of multi-circle equilibria.

papers.title: ExaTune: Exhaustive Hyperparameter Landscape Exploration at Scale
papers.abstract: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) returns a single optimal configuration, systematically discarding the explored performance landscape that encodes how results depend on configuration choices. Fitness landscape analysis comprises a robust collection of methods from evolutionary computation offering ruggedness indices, autocorrelation functions, and fitness-distance correlation that have never been applied to machine learning hyperparameter spaces at scale, given that fine-grained ground-truth enumeration data has not existed. We present ExaTune, an open-source HPC system to produce a new artifact class: the hyperparameter landscape map. ExaTune exhaustively evaluates every point on a discretized hyperparameter grid via $K$-fold cross-validation, aggregates results into reproducible parquet benchmarks, and applies a suite of five formalized landscape metrics: spatial autocorrelation (Moran's $I$), ruggedness, local optima density, fitness-distance correlation (FDC), and variance-based parameter importance.
